Abelisauridae.description: Abelisauridae is a family of ceratosaurian theropod dinosaurs that were dominant predators in Gondwanan landmasses during the Cretaceous period. Abelisaurids are characterized by short, deep skulls, heavily ornamented cranial bones, and dramatically reduced forelimbs that are even more vestigial than those of tyrannosaurids. Notable members include Carnotaurus, Majungasaurus, and Abelisaurus. The family was most diverse in South America, Madagascar, and India.
diagnostic_features: Short, deep skull with rugose ornamentation on frontal and nasal bones
Extremely reduced forelimbs with vestigial digits
Thickened skull roof bones
Robust and short cervical vertebrae
Well-developed femoral musculature attachment sites indicating powerful hindlimbs

references.title: Abelisaurus comahuensis, n.g., n.sp., Carnosauria del Cretacico Tardio de Patagonia

Allosauridae.description: Allosauridae is a family of large carnosaur theropod dinosaurs best known from the Late Jurassic of North America and Europe. The family is typified by Allosaurus, one of the most abundant and well-studied large predatory dinosaurs. Allosaurids were apex predators characterized by large skulls with prominent lacrimal horns, powerful forelimbs with three clawed digits, and laterally compressed serrated teeth.
diagnostic_features: Prominent lacrimal horns or hornlets above the eyes
Large skull with paired nasal crests
Laterally compressed, recurved, serrated teeth
Three-fingered manus with large manual unguals
Robust cervical vertebrae with well-developed epipophyses

references.title: Notice of new dinosaurian reptiles

Ankylopollexia.description: Ankylopollexia, meaning "fused thumb," is a clade of ornithopod dinosaurs characterized by a robust, conical thumb spike formed by a modified and enlarged pollex (first manual digit). This distinctive feature likely served as a defensive weapon or for intraspecific combat. Ankylopollexians range from medium-sized bipedal forms such as Camptosaurus to the large iguanodonts and hadrosaurs. The clade represents one of the most diverse and successful ornithischian radiations.
diagnostic_features: Conical, spike-like thumb (pollex) formed by a fused and enlarged first manual ungual
Robust metacarpal I fused to or tightly articulating with the carpus
Progressive reduction of manual digit V
Elongate and robust prepubic process
Trend toward increasingly complex dental batteries in derived members

references.title: Phylogeny of the bird-hipped dinosaurs (Order Ornithischia)

Ankylosauria.description: Ankylosauria is a clade of heavily armored thyreophoran ornithischian dinosaurs known from the Middle Jurassic to the end of the Cretaceous. Ankylosaurs were low-slung, quadrupedal herbivores encased in extensive dermal armor consisting of osteoderms arranged in transverse rows across the body, often supplemented by lateral spines. Some ankylosaurs, particularly ankylosaurids, possessed a massive bony tail club used for defense. The clade includes Ankylosauridae and Nodosauridae.
diagnostic_features: Extensive dermal armor covering the dorsal surface and flanks
Low, wide body plan with short, robust limbs
Fused osteoderms on the skull forming a solid cranial shield
Tail club present in Ankylosauridae (modified distal caudal vertebrae and osteoderms)
Laterally projecting cervical or shoulder spines in many taxa
Secondary palate present

references.title: Two Lower Cretaceous dinosaurs of Mongolia

Ankylosauridae.description: Ankylosauridae is a family of armored dinosaurs within Ankylosauria, and is the sister group to Nodosauridae. The oldest known ankylosaurids date to around 122 million years ago, and the clade went extinct 66 million years ago during the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event. These animals were mainly herbivorous and were obligate quadrupeds, with leaf-shaped teeth and robust, scute-covered bodies. Ankylosaurids possess a distinctly domed and short snout, wedge-shaped osteoderms on their skull, scutes along their torso, and a tail club.

references.title: The ankylosauridea, a new family of armored dinosaurs from the upper cretaceous
references.journal: Zeitschrift für Induktive Abstammungs- und Vererbungslehre
references.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

Ankylosaurinae.description: Ankylosaurinae is a subfamily of ankylosaurid dinosaurs, existing from the Early Cretaceous about 105 million years ago until the end of the Late Cretaceous, about 66 mya. Many genera are included in the clade, such as Ankylosaurus, Pinacosaurus, Euoplocephalus, and Saichania.

references.authors: Leahey, L.G.; Molnar, R.E.; Carpenter, K.; Witmer, L.M.; Salisbury, S.W.
references.title: Cranial osteology of the ankylosaurian dinosaur formerly known asMinmisp. (Ornithischia: Thyreophora) from the Lower Cretaceous Allaru Mudstone of Richmond, Queensland, Australia

references.authors: Thompson, R.S.; Parish, J.C.; Maidment, S.C.R.; Barrett, P.M.
references.title: Phylogeny of the ankylosaurian dinosaurs (Ornithischia: Thyreophora)
Systematics, phylogeny and palaeobiogeography of the ankylosaurid dinosaurs

Ankylosaurini.description: Ankylosaurinae is a subfamily of ankylosaurid dinosaurs, existing from the Early Cretaceous about 105 million years ago until the end of the Late Cretaceous, about 66 mya.

references.authors: Arbour, Victoria M.; Currie, Philip J.
references.title: Systematics, phylogeny and palaeobiogeography of the ankylosaurid dinosaurs

Aphanosauria.description: Aphanosauria is a clade of early avemetatarsalian archosaurs from the Middle to Late Triassic, known from South America, Europe, and possibly Africa. Members of Aphanosauria were quadrupedal or semi-quadrupedal and possessed a long neck and tail. They are among the earliest-diverging members of the bird-line (Avemetatarsalia) and are important for understanding the early evolution of archosaurs prior to the origin of pterosaurs and dinosaurs.

Archosauromorpha.description: Archosauromorpha is a major clade of diapsid reptiles that includes archosaurs (birds, crocodilians, and their extinct relatives) and several related groups such as tanystropheids and rhynchosaurs. The clade originated in the Permian and diversified extensively during the Triassic, with members surviving to the present day as birds and crocodilians.

Avetheropoda.description: Avetheropoda is a clade of advanced theropod dinosaurs that unites Carnosauria and Coelurosauria. Avetheropods represent the more derived tetanurans, distinguished from megalosauroids by features of the skull, vertebral column, and limbs. The clade encompasses the majority of Late Jurassic and Cretaceous theropod diversity, including all living birds.
diagnostic_features: Maxillary fenestra present and well-developed
Reduced or absent prefrontal bone
Enlarged orbit relative to skull length
Fused interdental plates
Opisthopubic or mesopubic pelvis in derived members

references.title: Predatory Dinosaurs of the World

Brachiosauridae.description: Brachiosauridae is a family of macronarian sauropod dinosaurs known from the Late Jurassic to Early Cretaceous of North America, Africa, Europe, and possibly South America. Brachiosaurids are distinguished by their unusual body proportions, with forelimbs longer than or subequal to hindlimbs, giving them a distinctive giraffe-like elevated posture. This configuration allowed them to browse at greater heights than most other sauropods. Notable members include Brachiosaurus and Giraffatitan.
diagnostic_features: Forelimbs longer than or subequal in length to hindlimbs
Elevated, giraffe-like body posture with the shoulders higher than the hips
Elongated humerus exceeding femoral length
Highly elevated narial region on the skull
Spatulate teeth arranged along the full extent of the jaw margins
Relatively short tail compared to other sauropods

references.title: Brachiosaurus altithorax, the largest known dinosaur

Carcharodontosauridae.description: Carcharodontosauridae, meaning "shark-toothed lizard family," is a family of giant carnosaur theropod dinosaurs known from the Cretaceous of Africa, South America, Europe, Asia, and North America. The family includes some of the largest terrestrial predators ever to have lived, such as Carcharodontosaurus, Giganotosaurus, and Mapusaurus. They are named for their distinctive large, laterally compressed teeth with prominent serrations resembling those of Carcharodon (great white shark).
diagnostic_features: Large, laterally compressed teeth with pronounced, shark-like serrations
Very large body size, often exceeding 10 meters in length
Prominent ornamentation on lacrimal and postorbital bones
Pneumatized cranial bones with extensive sinus systems
Elongate and narrow maxilla

references.title: Wirbeltier-Reste der Baharije-Stufe (unterstes Cenoman). 10. Ein Skelett-Rest von Carcharodontosaurus nov. gen.
references.journal: Abhandlungen der Bayerischen Akademie der Wissenschaften, Mathematisch-naturwissenschaftliche Abteilung

Carnosauria.description: Carnosauria is a clade of large-bodied predatory theropod dinosaurs within Avetheropoda. In modern phylogenetic usage, Carnosauria is largely synonymous with Allosauroidea and includes the allosaurids, carcharodontosaurids, and their relatives. Carnosaurs were apex predators during the Jurassic and Early to mid-Cretaceous periods, with some reaching body sizes comparable to or exceeding Tyrannosaurus.
diagnostic_features: Large body size with proportionally large skull
Lacrimal bone with pneumatic recesses and ornamentation
Pronounced cnemial crest on the tibia
Large, laterally compressed, serrated teeth
Robust and well-developed forelimbs with three-fingered hands

references.title: Bemerkungen zur Systematik und Stammesgeschichte einiger Reptilien
references.journal: Zeitschrift fur Induktive Abstammungs- und Vererbungslehre

Cerapoda.description: Cerapoda is a clade of ornithischian dinosaurs that unites Ornithopoda and Marginocephalia. Cerapodans are characterized by specialized jaw mechanics adapted for efficient oral processing of plant material, including a well- developed coronoid process on the dentary, asymmetrical enamel on the teeth enabling precise occlusion, and the loss of premaxillary teeth. The clade encompasses a wide range of herbivorous dinosaurs from small bipeds to giant quadrupedal forms.
diagnostic_features: Well-developed coronoid process on the dentary
Asymmetrical enamel distribution on teeth facilitating shearing occlusion
Reduction or loss of premaxillary teeth
Diastema between premaxillary and maxillary tooth rows
Specialized jaw mechanics for efficient oral processing of vegetation

references.title: Phylogeny of the bird-hipped dinosaurs (Order Ornithischia)

Ceratopsia.description: Ceratopsia, meaning "horned faces," is a clade of marginocephalian ornithischian dinosaurs characterized by a unique rostral bone at the tip of the upper jaw and a parietosquamosal frill extending from the back of the skull. The clade includes small, bipedal basal forms such as Psittacosaurus and large, quadrupedal ceratopsids like Triceratops and Styracosaurus. Ceratopsians were exclusively herbivorous and were most diverse in the Late Cretaceous of North America and Asia. Horns above the eyes and nose evolved in more derived members.
diagnostic_features: Rostral bone forming a sharp, beak-like tip of the upper jaw
Parietosquamosal frill extending posterodorsally from the skull
Jugal flanges (flared cheek horns) on the skull
Shearing dentition with double-rooted cheek teeth
Nasal and supraorbital horns in derived ceratopsids
Predentary bone with a sharp cutting edge

references.title: Additional characters of the Ceratopsidae, with notice of new Cretaceous dinosaurs

Ceratopsidae.description: Ceratopsidae is a family of large-bodied ceratopsian ornithischian dinosaurs known from the Late Cretaceous of western North America (and possibly Asia). Ceratopsids are among the most recognizable dinosaurs, characterized by elaborate cranial ornamentation including large nasal and supraorbital horns, expansive parietosquamosal frills often decorated with epiossifications (epoccipitals and epiparietals), and a robust, barrel-shaped body. The family is divided into Chasmosaurinae (long-frilled forms like Triceratops) and Centrosaurinae (short-frilled forms like Centrosaurus).
diagnostic_features: Large parietosquamosal frill with marginal epiossifications (epoccipitals)
Prominent nasal horn and/or paired supraorbital horns
Very large skull, often exceeding 1.5 meters in length
Double-rooted, shearing cheek teeth arranged in dental batteries
Obligate quadrupedal stance with robust, graviportal limbs
Syncervical (fused anterior cervical vertebrae) supporting the massive skull

references.title: Additional characters of the Ceratopsidae, with notice of new Cretaceous dinosaurs

Ceratosauria.description: Ceratosauria is a clade of early-diverging theropod dinosaurs that radiated primarily during the Jurassic and Cretaceous periods. Many ceratosaurs possessed prominent cranial ornamentation, including horns and crests. The group was particularly diverse in Gondwanan landmasses and includes the abelisaurids, noasaurids, and the Jurassic ceratosaurids. Ceratosaurs generally retained four digits on the hand, unlike the three-fingered condition of more derived theropods.
diagnostic_features: Cranial ornamentation including horns, bosses, or rugose crests in many taxa
Fused pelvic elements (ilium, ischium, pubis) in mature individuals
Four functional digits on the manus in basal members
Specialized sacral vertebral articulations
Distinctive cervical vertebral morphology with low neural spines

references.title: Principal characters of American Jurassic dinosaurs, Part VIII

Coelurosauria.description: Coelurosauria is a large and diverse clade of theropod dinosaurs that includes tyrannosaurs, ornithomimosaurs, maniraptorans, and all living birds. Coelurosaurs are the most speciose theropod clade and exhibit an extraordinary range of body sizes, diets, and ecologies. Many coelurosaurs possessed filamentous integumentary structures or true feathers. The clade originated in the Middle Jurassic and includes the only dinosaur lineage to survive the end-Cretaceous extinction.
diagnostic_features: Elongate distal caudal vertebrae with reduced or absent transverse processes
Filamentous integument or feathers present in many lineages
Reduced or absent prefrontal bone
Semilunate carpal bone in wrist of many derived taxa
Tibiotarsus longer than femur
Enlarged cerebrum relative to body size

references.title: Das naturliche System der Saurischia
references.journal: Centralblatt fur Mineralogie, Geologie und Palaontologie B

Dinocephalia.description: Dinocephalia is an extinct group of large therapsids from the Middle Permian. They were among the first large terrestrial vertebrates, with some members exceeding 3 meters in length. Dinocephalians included both herbivorous and carnivorous forms and are characterized by thickened skull bones, often interpreted as adaptations for head-butting behavior. The group went extinct at the end of the Capitanian stage.

Dinosauria.description: Dinosauria is a clade of archosaurian reptiles that first appeared during the Triassic period, approximately 233 million years ago. Dinosaurs are united by a suite of anatomical features including a fully upright (parasagittal) stance, a fully open (perforated) acetabulum in the pelvis, and three or more sacral vertebrae. The clade encompasses two major lineages, Saurischia and Ornithischia, and includes all descendants of their most recent common ancestor, extending to modern birds (Aves).
diagnostic_features: Fully erect, parasagittal hindlimb posture
Perforated (fully open) acetabulum
Three or more sacral vertebrae
Elongate deltopectoral crest on the humerus
Asymmetrical fourth trochanter on the femur
Open hip socket allowing pillar-erect stance

references.title: Report on British fossil reptiles, Part II
references.journal: Report of the British Association for the Advancement of Science

Diplodocidae.description: Diplodocidae is a family of diplodocoid sauropod dinosaurs known primarily from the Late Jurassic of North America, with additional occurrences in Africa and Europe. Diplodocids are characterized by their extremely elongated bodies with long, whip-like tails, elongate and shallow skulls with anteriorly restricted pencil-shaped teeth, and bifurcated (forked) neural spines on cervical and dorsal vertebrae. Notable members include Diplodocus, Apatosaurus, and Brontosaurus.
diagnostic_features: Extremely elongated tail with whip-like distal section
Pencil-shaped (cylindrical) teeth restricted to the front of the jaws
Bifurcated (forked) neural spines on cervical and anterior dorsal vertebrae
Anteroposteriorly elongated skull with squared-off snout
Elongated cervical vertebrae with low neural arches
Tail chevrons with anterior and posterior projections (double-beamed)

references.title: Principal characters of American Jurassic dinosaurs, Part VIII

Dromaeosauridae.description: Dromaeosauridae is a family of small to medium-sized maniraptoran theropod dinosaurs commonly known as "raptors." Dromaeosaurids were agile, feathered predators characterized by their signature enlarged, sickle-shaped retractable claw on the second toe (pedal digit II), stiffened tails used for balance during rapid pursuit, and well-developed pennaceous feathers. The family includes well-known genera such as Velociraptor, Deinonychus, and Microraptor. Dromaeosaurids are among the closest non-avian relatives of birds.
diagnostic_features: Enlarged, hyperextensible, sickle-shaped ungual on pedal digit II
Stiffened tail with elongated prezygapophyses and chevrons
Pennaceous feathers on forelimbs and hindlimbs
Semilunate carpal bone enabling wing-folding motion of manus
Laterally compressed, recurved, serrated teeth
Reduced and stiffened distal tail functioning as a dynamic stabilizer

references.title: The family Deinodontidae, with notice of a new genus from the Cretaceous of Alberta
references.journal: Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History

Eutyrannosauria.description: Eutyrannosauria is a clade of derived tyrannosauroid theropod dinosaurs comprising Tyrannosauridae and its closest non- tyrannosaurid relatives, the North American taxa Appalachiosaurus and Dryptosaurus. Members of the clade are characterized by large body size, rugose nasal ornamentation, and a suite of cranial pneumaticity features. Voris et al. (2025) recover Khankhuuluu mongoliensis as the immediate sister taxon of Eutyrannosauria.
diagnostic_features: Rugose nasals with cornual ornamentation.
Lacrimal with an inflated cornual process that expands dorsally during ontogeny.
Anteroposteriorly expanded dorsal process of the quadratojugal.
Pneumatic recess on the anterior surface of the quadrate condyles.
Medial margins of the distal condyle and diaphysis of metatarsal III aligned (not offset).

references.authors: Voris, J. T.; Zelenitsky, D. K.; Kobayashi, Y.; Modesto, S. P.; Therrien, F.; Tsutsumi, H.; Chinzorig, T.; Tsogtbaatar, K.
references.title: A new Mongolian tyrannosauroid and the evolution of Eutyrannosauria
references.notes: Uses Eutyrannosauria (Delcourt and Grillo, 2018) as an established clade and recovers Khankhuuluu mongoliensis as its immediate sister taxon.

Hadrosauridae.description: Hadrosauridae is a family of large ornithopod dinosaurs commonly known as duck-billed dinosaurs. Hadrosaurs were the most diverse and abundant large herbivorous dinosaurs of the Late Cretaceous, with a global distribution. They are characterized by highly specialized dental batteries consisting of hundreds of closely packed teeth forming a continuous grinding surface, broad and flat edentulous premaxillary bills, and in the subfamily Lambeosaurinae, elaborate hollow cranial crests likely used for vocalization and display. Hadrosaurs include the two major subgroups Hadrosaurinae (flat-headed forms) and Lambeosaurinae (crested forms).
diagnostic_features: Highly specialized dental batteries with hundreds of interlocking teeth
Broad, spatulate, edentulous premaxillary bill
Hollow cranial crests in Lambeosaurinae (extensions of nasal passages)
Complete loss of the thumb spike
Extensive ossified tendons forming a lattice along the vertebral column
Hoof-like unguals on weight-bearing digits

references.title: Synopsis of the extinct Batrachia, Reptilia, and Aves of North America
references.journal: Transactions of the American Philosophical Society

Hadrosauriformes.description: Hadrosauriformes is a clade of styracosternan ornithopod dinosaurs that includes the hadrosaurs (duck-billed dinosaurs) and their immediate relatives such as Iguanodon. Hadrosauriforms are characterized by well- developed dental batteries consisting of multiple stacked replacement teeth, broad and flattened snouts (often described as duck-billed), and large body size. The clade was globally distributed during the Cretaceous period and represents one of the most successful ornithischian radiations.
diagnostic_features: Well-developed dental battery with multiple replacement teeth in each tooth position
Broad, flattened premaxilla forming a duck-like bill
Reduced or absent thumb spike compared to basal styracosternans
Elongate and dorsoventrally flattened rostrum
Three or more replacement teeth per tooth family

references.title: The origin and evolution of dinosaurs
references.journal: Annual Review of Earth and Planetary Sciences

Macronaria.description: Macronaria, meaning "large nostrils," is a clade of neosauropod dinosaurs characterized by large nasal openings (external nares) that are typically larger than the orbits. The clade includes brachiosaurids, titanosaurs, and their relatives, and was particularly diverse and dominant during the Cretaceous period. Macronarians tended to have more robust, box-like skulls with spatulate teeth, in contrast to the elongate skulls and peg-like teeth of diplodocoids.
diagnostic_features: Enlarged external nares larger than the orbit
Spatulate (spoon-shaped) teeth
Box-like, dorsoventrally deep skull
Opisthocoelous anterior caudal vertebrae
Metacarpals arranged in a tubular, U-shaped colonnade

references.title: Early evolution and higher-level phylogeny of sauropod dinosaurs

Maniraptora.description: Maniraptora, meaning "hand snatchers," is a clade of coelurosaurian theropod dinosaurs that includes dromaeosaurids, troodontids, oviraptorosaurs, therizinosaurs, and birds (Aves). Maniraptorans are characterized by elongated arms relative to body size, a semilunate carpal bone enabling a folding mechanism in the wrist, and the widespread presence of pennaceous feathers. The clade represents the closest relatives of and includes modern birds, making it one of the most significant groups in understanding avian origins.
diagnostic_features: Elongated forelimbs relative to body size
Semilunate (half-moon shaped) carpal bone allowing wrist folding
Pennaceous feathers present in many lineages
Elongate and mobile manus
Opisthopubic pelvis (posteriorly directed pubis) in many taxa
Reduced or absent postorbital bar

references.title: Saurischian monophyly and the origin of birds
references.journal: Memoirs of the California Academy of Sciences

Marginocephalia.description: Marginocephalia, meaning "fringed heads," is a clade of cerapodan ornithischian dinosaurs united by the presence of a distinctive bony shelf or frill projecting from the posterior margin of the skull. The clade includes Pachycephalosauria (dome-headed dinosaurs) and Ceratopsia (horned dinosaurs). Marginocephalians were exclusively herbivorous and ranged from small bipedal forms to massive quadrupedal ceratopsids. The group was most diverse in the Late Cretaceous of North America and Asia.
diagnostic_features: Parietosquamosal shelf or frill projecting from the posterior margin of the skull
Rostral bone at the tip of the upper jaw (in ceratopsians) or thickened skull roof (in pachycephalosaurs)
Short postorbital region of the skull
Reduction of the supratemporal fenestra
Herbivorous dentition with leaf-shaped or shearing teeth

references.title: Phylogeny of the bird-hipped dinosaurs (Order Ornithischia)

Megalosauridae.description: Megalosauridae is a family of large basal tetanuran theropod dinosaurs known primarily from the Middle to Late Jurassic of Europe, Africa, and South America. The family includes Megalosaurus bucklandii, the first dinosaur to be scientifically described and named (1824). Megalosaurids were robust, large- bodied predators with powerful forelimbs and laterally compressed, serrated teeth.
diagnostic_features: Large body size with robust skeletal construction
Laterally compressed, serrated teeth
Well-developed and powerful forelimbs with large manual claws
Tall neural spines on dorsal vertebrae
Distinctive premaxillary-maxillary contact morphology

references.title: On the upper jaw of Megalosaurus
references.journal: Quarterly Journal of the Geological Society of London

Megalosauroidea.description: Megalosauroidea is a superfamily of large-bodied basal tetanuran theropods that includes Megalosauridae and Spinosauridae. These predators were prominent during the Middle Jurassic through Late Cretaceous. Megalosauroids were among the first dinosaurs to be scientifically described and include some of the most specialized predatory forms, such as the semi-aquatic spinosaurids.
diagnostic_features: Large body size in most members
Elongate premaxilla-maxilla contact
Robust skull construction with well-developed antorbital fenestra
Elongate and robust manual unguals
Basal tetanuran grade of skeletal organization

references.authors: Holtz, T.R., Molnar, R.E. & Currie, P.J.
references.title: Basal Tetanurae

Nanotyrannidae.description: Nanotyrannidae is a family of eutyrannosaurian theropod dinosaurs erected by Zanno and Napoli (2025) for Nanotyrannus and any taxa more closely related to it than to Tyrannosaurus or Albertosaurus. The family is presently known from the Maastrichtian Hell Creek Formation of western North America; Bayesian biogeographic analysis also recovers Appalachiosaurus and Dryptosaurus within the clade, but the authors caution that this placement requires additional data.
diagnostic_features: Absence of a clearly defined embayment for the subnarial foramen at the premaxillary/maxillary suture.
Unserrated premaxillary tooth crowns that are straight and chisel-shaped.
Pneumatic foramen in the quadratojugal.
Extension of the glenoid fossa onto the lateral surface of the scapula.
Apomorphically elongate lower hindlimbs (tibia plus metatarsus) relative to femur length.

references.authors: Zanno, L. E.; Napoli, J. G.
references.title: Nanotyrannus and Tyrannosaurus coexisted at the close of the Cretaceous
references.notes: Erects Nanotyrannidae for Nanotyrannus on a branch-based phylogenetic definition; diagnostic characters are drawn from the genus-level Nanotyrannus diagnosis in the same paper.

Noasauridae.description: Noasauridae is a family of small to medium-sized ceratosaurian theropod dinosaurs known primarily from Gondwanan continents during the Cretaceous period. Noasaurids were lightly built, gracile predators or omnivores, and represent the smaller-bodied counterpart to their sister group Abelisauridae within Abelisauria. Notable members include Noasaurus, Masiakasaurus, and Elaphrosaurus.
diagnostic_features: Small to medium body size with gracile build
Lightly constructed skull
Elongate cervical vertebrae relative to abelisaurids
Procumbent (forward-projecting) teeth in some taxa
Relatively long and slender hindlimbs

references.title: A continental assemblage of tetrapods from the Upper Cretaceous beds of El Brete, northwestern Argentina (Sauropoda-Coelurosauria-Carnosauria-Aves)
references.journal: Memoires de la Societe Geologique de France

Ornithischia.description: Ornithischia, meaning "bird-hipped," is one of the two traditionally recognized major clades of dinosaurs. Ornithischians are united by a distinctive pelvic anatomy in which the pubis is rotated posteriorly to lie parallel with the ischium, convergently resembling the pelvic arrangement of birds (though birds are actually saurischians). The clade includes the armored thyreophorans (stegosaurs and ankylosaurs), the horned ceratopsians, the dome-headed pachycephalosaurs, and the duck-billed ornithopods. All ornithischians were herbivorous.
diagnostic_features: Opisthopubic pelvis with posteriorly directed pubis parallel to ischium
Predentary bone at the tip of the lower jaw
Ossified tendons along the vertebral column in many taxa
Leaf-shaped cheek teeth with denticulate margins
Palpebral bone in the orbit
Herbivorous diet across all members

references.title: On the classification of the fossil animals commonly named Dinosauria
references.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London

Ornithomimosauria.description: Ornithomimosauria, meaning "bird-mimic lizards," is a clade of coelurosaurian theropod dinosaurs known from the Cretaceous of North America, Asia, Europe, and Africa. Often called "ostrich dinosaurs," ornithomimosaurs were characterized by long legs adapted for swift running, elongate necks, small skulls with toothless beaks (in derived forms), and large eyes. They were likely omnivorous or herbivorous, representing a significant ecological departure from the ancestral carnivorous theropod condition.
diagnostic_features: Toothless, keratinous beak in derived members
Elongate cervical vertebrae forming a long, S-curved neck
Large orbits with well-developed sclerotic rings
Long, gracile hindlimbs adapted for cursorial locomotion
Arctometatarsalian foot in derived forms
Elongate manus with subequal metacarpals

references.title: Ostrich dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous of western Canada

Ornithopoda.description: Ornithopoda, meaning "bird feet," is a clade of cerapodan ornithischian dinosaurs that includes the iguanodonts and hadrosaurs along with numerous smaller, basal members. Ornithopods were among the most successful and widespread herbivorous dinosaurs, ranging from small bipedal forms in the Jurassic to large quadrupedal hadrosaurs in the Late Cretaceous. They are characterized by their efficient jaw mechanism that allowed transverse (pleurokinetic) chewing of plant material, a feature rare among reptiles.
diagnostic_features: Pleurokinetic skull allowing lateral movement of the maxillae during chewing
Tridactyl (three-toed) pes with hoof-like unguals
Absence of premaxillary teeth (keratinous beak present)
Well-developed dental battery in advanced forms
Tendency toward facultative or obligate quadrupedality in larger taxa
Elongate prepubic process of the pubis

references.title: Principal characters of American Jurassic dinosaurs, Part IV

Pachycephalosauria.description: Pachycephalosauria, meaning "thick-headed lizards," is a clade of marginocephalian ornithischian dinosaurs characterized by a dramatically thickened skull roof (frontoparietal dome). These bipedal herbivores or omnivores were most diverse during the Late Cretaceous of North America and Asia. The thickened dome has been hypothesized to have served in intraspecific head-butting or flank-butting contests, though this remains debated. Notable genera include Pachycephalosaurus, Stegoceras, and Dracorex.
diagnostic_features: Dramatically thickened frontoparietal dome on the skull roof
Peripheral ornamentation of nodes and horns around the dome margin
Wide, shelf-like squamosal
Relatively large orbits
Bipedal stance with stiffened tail
Broad body with flared iliac blades

Saurischia.description: Saurischia, meaning "lizard-hipped," is one of the two major clades of dinosaurs. Saurischians retain an ancestral pelvic configuration in which the pubis points forward and downward, in contrast to the retroverted pubis of ornithischians. The clade includes the bipedal, mostly carnivorous theropods and the long-necked, herbivorous sauropodomorphs. Saurischia is defined as all dinosaurs more closely related to birds than to Triceratops.
diagnostic_features: Forward-pointing (anteroventrally directed) pubis in basal members
Elongate, mobile neck with cervical vertebrae bearing well-developed pleurocoels
Asymmetrical hand with digit II longest
Subnarial foramen present between premaxilla and maxilla

references.title: On the classification of the fossil animals commonly named Dinosauria

Sauropoda.description: Sauropoda is a clade of large to gigantic sauropodomorph dinosaurs that includes the largest terrestrial animals in Earth's history. Sauropods were obligate quadrupeds with columnar limbs, extremely elongated necks containing 12 or more cervical vertebrae, long tails, and relatively small skulls. Extensive skeletal pneumaticity (air-filled bones) reduced body mass and may have aided respiration. Sauropods were globally distributed throughout the Jurassic and Cretaceous periods and occupied large-bodied herbivore niches on every continent.
diagnostic_features: Gigantic body size with columnar, graviportal limbs
Extremely elongated neck with 12 or more opisthocoelous cervical vertebrae
Extensive postcranial skeletal pneumaticity
Spatulate or peg-like teeth
Obligate quadrupedal posture
Reduced or absent manual phalanges on lateral digits

references.title: Principal characters of American Jurassic dinosaurs, Part I

Sauropodomorpha.description: Sauropodomorpha is a major clade of saurischian dinosaurs comprising the long-necked herbivorous dinosaurs and their ancestors. The clade ranges from small, facultatively bipedal early forms of the Late Triassic to the giant quadrupedal sauropods that dominated terrestrial herbivore niches throughout the Jurassic and Cretaceous. Sauropodomorphs include the largest land animals ever to have lived and are characterized by their elongated necks, small heads relative to body size, and herbivorous or omnivorous diets.
diagnostic_features: Elongated neck with ten or more cervical vertebrae
Small skull relative to body size
Leaf-shaped or spatulate teeth adapted for herbivory
Enlarged nares
Large pollex (thumb) claw on manus digit I
Trend toward increasing body size through evolutionary history

Spinosauridae.description: Spinosauridae is a family of large megalosauroid theropod dinosaurs characterized by elongated, crocodile-like snouts and conical, unserrated teeth adapted for piscivory (fish-eating). Many spinosaurids possessed enlarged dorsal neural spines forming a sail or ridge along the back. The family includes Spinosaurus, one of the largest known theropods, which shows evidence of semi-aquatic habits. Spinosaurids are known from the Cretaceous of Africa, Europe, and South America.
diagnostic_features: Elongated, narrow snout with a terminal rosette of premaxillary teeth
Conical, unserrated teeth adapted for grasping fish
Enlarged, elongate neural spines on dorsal and sacral vertebrae
Secondary palate partially developed
Enlarged manual ungual on digit I
Retracted external nares

Stegosauria.description: Stegosauria is a clade of thyreophoran ornithischian dinosaurs best known for their distinctive rows of dorsal plates and spines. Stegosaurs appeared in the Middle Jurassic and were most diverse during the Late Jurassic, with the group declining through the Cretaceous. They were medium to large quadrupedal herbivores with small heads, short necks, and hindlimbs significantly longer than forelimbs, giving the body a distinctive arched profile. The tail typically bore two pairs of elongate spines (the "thagomizer").
diagnostic_features: Parasagittal rows of alternating or paired dorsal plates and/or spines
Tail spines (thagomizer) used for defense
Hindlimbs substantially longer than forelimbs
Small skull with simple, leaf-shaped teeth and weak jaw musculature
Low, arched body profile
Relatively small brain (low encephalization quotient)

Styracosterna.description: Styracosterna, meaning "spiked stern," is a clade of ankylopollexian ornithopod dinosaurs characterized by a spike-like first manual ungual (thumb spike) that is more developed and conical than in basal ankylopollexians. The clade includes Iguanodon and more derived ornithopods leading to Hadrosauriformes. Styracosternans became the dominant large-bodied herbivores in many Early to Late Cretaceous ecosystems worldwide.
diagnostic_features: Well-developed, spike-like conical pollex ungual
Loss of manual digit V phalanges in many members
Elongate snout with expanded and edentulous premaxilla
Hoof-like unguals on pedal digits
Maxillary tooth rows set medially with a fleshy cheek inferred

references.title: Phylogeny of the bird-hipped dinosaurs (Order Ornithischia)

Tanystropheidae.description: Tanystropheidae is a family of non-archosauriform archosauromorphs from the Triassic period, characterized by an extremely elongated neck composed of elongate cervical vertebrae with extensive cervical ribs. Members ranged from small insectivores to large piscivores. The family was widespread during the Triassic, with fossils found in Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and North America.

Tapinocephalidae.description: Tapinocephalidae is a family of large herbivorous dinocephalians from the Middle Permian Karoo Basin of South Africa. Members are characterized by massive, heavily built bodies and distinctively thickened cranial roofs. Tapinocephalids were among the largest land animals of their time and are divided into the subfamilies Tapinocephalinae and Struthiocephalinae.

Tapinocephalinae.description: Tapinocephalinae is a subfamily of tapinocephalid dinocephalians, large herbivorous therapsids from the Middle Permian of South Africa. Members are characterized by a low, depressed skull with a thickened cranial roof, interpreted as an adaptation for intraspecific combat. Tapinocephalinae includes some of the largest terrestrial animals of the Permian.

Tetanurae.description: Tetanurae, meaning "stiff tails," is a large clade of theropod dinosaurs characterized by stiffened tails with interlocking zygapophyses in the distal caudal vertebrae, and the reduction of the hand to three functional digits. Tetanurans include the megalosauroids, allosaurs, and coelurosaurs (including birds). The clade represents the majority of theropod diversity from the Middle Jurassic onward.
diagnostic_features: Stiffened distal tail with interlocking zygapophyses
Reduction of the hand to three functional digits (loss of digit IV)
Maxillary tooth row restricted to anterior portion of skull, not extending posterior to antorbital fenestra
Large, well-developed maxillary fenestra
Tibia longer than or equal to femur

references.journal: Memoirs of the California Academy of Sciences

Therapsida.description: Therapsida is a major clade of synapsids that includes mammals and their extinct close relatives. Therapsids were the dominant large terrestrial vertebrates during the Permian period and diversified extensively before and after the end-Permian mass extinction. The clade encompasses a wide range of body plans, from large herbivorous dinocephalians to the small cynodonts that gave rise to mammals.

Therizinosauridae.description: Therizinosauridae is a family of bizarre, large-bodied maniraptoran theropod dinosaurs known from the Cretaceous of Asia and North America. Despite their theropod ancestry, therizinosaurs were herbivorous, possessing a suite of unusual adaptations including enormously elongated manual claws (up to 1 meter in Therizinosaurus), a wide, barrel-shaped torso for housing an enlarged herbivorous gut, a small head with a keratinous beak and leaf-shaped teeth, and a broad, four-toed foot.
diagnostic_features: Enormously elongated manual unguals (claws), especially on digit I
Wide, barrel-shaped torso accommodating an enlarged gut
Small skull with edentulous premaxilla and leaf-shaped cheek teeth
Opisthopubic (posteriorly directed) pelvis
Broad, functionally tetradactyl (four-toed) pes
Dense, filamentous integumentary covering

Theropoda.description: Theropoda, meaning "beast feet," is a clade of predominantly bipedal saurischian dinosaurs. Most theropods were carnivorous, though several lineages independently evolved herbivory or omnivory. Theropods are characterized by hollow (pneumatic) bones, three-toed weight-bearing hindlimbs, and a furcula (wishbone). The clade includes all living birds (Aves), making Theropoda one of the most successful vertebrate lineages in Earth's history.
diagnostic_features: Hollow (pneumatized) long bones
Obligate bipedal stance
Three weight-bearing digits on the pes (functionally tridactyl foot)
Furcula (fused clavicles) present
Intramandibular joint in the lower jaw
Carnivorous dentition with serrated, laterally compressed teeth in basal members

references.title: Principal characters of American Jurassic dinosaurs, Part V

Thyreophora.description: Thyreophora, meaning "shield bearers," is a clade of armored ornithischian dinosaurs that includes Stegosauria and Ankylosauria. Thyreophorans are characterized by the presence of dermal armor in the form of osteoderms (bony scutes, plates, or spines) embedded in the skin along the body. The clade appeared in the Early Jurassic and persisted until the end of the Cretaceous, with a global distribution. Thyreophorans were obligate quadrupeds and herbivores.
diagnostic_features: Parasagittal rows of osteoderms (dermal armor) along the dorsal surface
Keeled scutes or plates on the body
Quadrupedal stance in all but the most basal forms
Robust, low-slung body plan
Small head relative to body size with simple, leaf-shaped teeth

Titanosauria.description: Titanosauria is a diverse and species-rich clade of macronarian sauropod dinosaurs that dominated herbivore niches across Gondwana and Laurasia during the Cretaceous period. Titanosaurs include both the largest known dinosaurs (Argentinosaurus, Patagotitan) and some of the smallest sauropods (Magyarosaurus). Many titanosaurs possessed osteoderms (bony armor plates) embedded in the skin, a feature unique among sauropods. The clade was the last major sauropod radiation before the end-Cretaceous extinction.
diagnostic_features: Procoelous caudal vertebrae (concave anteriorly, convex posteriorly)
Osteoderms (bony dermal armor) present in many taxa
Wide-gauge (laterally splayed) limb posture
Loss of manual phalanges in derived forms
Strongly opisthocoelous dorsal and caudal vertebrae
Expanded iliac blade with a preacetabular process directed laterally

Troodontidae.description: Troodontidae is a family of small, bird-like maniraptoran theropod dinosaurs known from the Cretaceous of North America, Asia, and Europe. Troodontids are notable for possessing the largest brain-to-body-size ratio among non-avian dinosaurs, suggesting relatively high intelligence. They had large, forward- facing eyes indicating good binocular vision, long and slender legs adapted for speed, and a retractable sickle claw on the second toe (smaller than in dromaeosaurids). Troodontids are among the closest known relatives of Aves.
diagnostic_features: Large brain relative to body size (high encephalization quotient)
Large, forward-facing orbits with well-developed binocular vision
Closely packed, numerous small teeth with large denticles
Retractable sickle claw on pedal digit II (smaller than dromaeosaurid condition)
Slender and elongate metatarsus adapted for cursorial locomotion
Asymmetric trochlea of metatarsal IV

Tyrannosauridae.description: Tyrannosauridae is a family of large coelurosaurian theropod dinosaurs that were apex predators during the Late Cretaceous of North America and Asia. The family includes Tyrannosaurus rex, one of the largest and most powerful terrestrial predators known. Tyrannosaurids are characterized by their proportionally enormous skulls, massive bite force, robust heterodont dentition, extremely reduced two-fingered forelimbs, and powerful hindlimbs adapted for cursorial locomotion.
diagnostic_features: Proportionally enormous skull with robust, deeply rooted teeth

Massive adductor musculature indicating powerful bite force
Arctometatarsalian foot with pinched third metatarsal
Fused nasals along the midline

A. celestae was named after Celeste Yates, who prepared much of the first known fossil material of the species. It has arm features that are intermediate between basal sauropodomorphs and more derived sauropods.

Abdarainurus.description: Abdarainurus is a genus of titanosaur dinosaur from the Alagteeg Formation in Mongolia. The type and only species is A. barsboldi. Currently seen as an indeterminate titanosaur, it may represent a previously unknown lineage of Asian macronarians. Abdarainurus is not known from many remains; it is only known from eight front tail vertebrae and a middle tail vertebra and several chevrons.

Abditosaurus.etymology: From Latin 'abditus' meaning 'forgotten' or 'hidden' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'forgotten lizard'
Abditosaurus.description: Abditosaurus is an extinct genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) Conques Formation (Tremp Group) of Catalonia, Spain. The genus contains a single species, Abditosaurus kuehnei, known from a partial specimen representing the most complete titanosaur skeleton found in Europe. Phylogenetic analyses recover it within a clade of South American and African saltasaurines, distinct from other insular dwarf sauropods from the European archipelago. Abditosaurus inhabited the Ibero-Armorican Island, a prehistoric island made up of what is now Spain, Portugal, and southern France, and would have been the largest titanosaur species in its environment.
diagnostic_features: Anterior dorsal vertebrae with anterior centrodiapophyseal lamina not reaching centrum but intersecting centroprezygapophyseal lamina; diapophyses ventral to postzygapophyses; absence of centroprezygapophyseal lamina.

Middle dorsal vertebrae with oblique posterodorsally oriented accessory lamina dividing parapophyseal centrodiapophyseal fossa and secondary prezygodiapophyseal lamina dividing prezygapophyseal paradiapophyseal fossa.
Abundant pneumatic foramina in spinopostzygapophyseal, centropostzygapophyseal, and postzygapophyseal centrodiapophyseal fossae of dorsal vertebrae.
Anterior dorsal ribs lacking pneumatic foramina on anterolateral and posteromedial surfaces; second dorsal ribs with anteroposterior thickening or bulge on posterior margin of distal end.

Scapula with co-occurrence of posteroventral process on medial margin of acromial plate, subtle anteroventral process, prominent dorsomedial blade bulge, and two oval lateral fossae on posterior blade end.
Coracoid foramen elliptical and twisting its orientation from lateral through to medial surface; fibula distal end bevelled posteriorly 20° relative to long axis of shaft.

It was a bipedal herbivore or omnivore and was one of the most basal heterodontosaurids. It was approximately 1.2 meters (3.9 ft) long and weighed less than 45 kilograms (99 lb).

Abrosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'abros' meaning 'delicate' or 'dainty' and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', referring to the delicate skull structure.
Abrosaurus.description: Abrosaurus is a genus of macronarian sauropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Period of what is now Asia. It is one of many dinosaurs found at the Dashanpu Quarry in the Sichuan Province of China. Like most sauropods, Abrosaurus was a quadrupedal herbivore. It was rather small for a sauropod, measuring no more than 9.1 meters (30 ft) long. Its head was boxy and topped with a tall, bony arch containing the nostrils. The generic name refers to the nature of the skull, with large openings separated by thin, bony struts. The only named species is A. dongpoi, named after eleventh-century Chinese poet Su Shi, also known as Su Dongpo, who was born in Sichuan.

Acantholipan.description: Acantholipan is a genus of herbivorous nodosaurid dinosaur from Mexico from the early Santonian age of the Late Cretaceous. It includes one species, Acantholipan gonzalezi.
diagnostic_features: Ulna with anterolateral process prominent, tapering, and truncated proximally (triangular in lateral view), equal in length to the olecranon process (1:1 ratio).
Conical and slightly caudally curved lateral thoracic osteoderm with a longitudinal oval cross section (length/width ratio 1:3).
Vascular grooves on the lateral face of the osteodermal spine only.

Acanthopholis.etymology: From Greek 'akantha' meaning 'spine' or 'thorn' and 'pholis' meaning 'scale'; meaning 'spiny scales'
Acanthopholis.description: Acanthopholis is a genus of ankylosaurian dinosaur in the family Nodosauridae that lived during the Late Cretaceous Period of England. A single species, A. horrida, exists.
diagnostic_features: Dermal scutes highly variable in form, ranging from slightly raised oval disks to large asymmetrical spines approaching nine inches in length, with outer surfaces irregularly pitted and spine-like forms bearing branching vascular grooves.

Spine-like dermal plates wholly asymmetrical, with convex anterior edge, concave posterior edge, and a deep notch interrupting the posterior ridge near the base that likely received the anterior edge of the adjacent spine.
Teeth lance-head shaped with acute point, sharp serrated edges bearing eight serrations on each side of the apex, and a crown that expands suddenly and asymmetrically into a swollen base.
Crown surface ornamented with vertical dark chocolate-colored bands alternating with pale brown bands running from the serrated edges to the swollen base, a feature not reported in allied genera.

Occipital condyle more elongated transversely and more excavated above than in Crocodile, with exoccipitals entering more largely into its composition; Eustachian tubes not in Crocodilian disposition; carotids running up the side of the basisphenoid in Lacertilian fashion.

Achelousaurus.etymology: Named after Achelous, the Greek deity of rivers, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Achelous lizard'
Achelousaurus.description: Achelousaurus is a genus of centrosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous Period of what is now North America, about 77 to 74.8 million years ago. The first fossils of Achelousaurus were collected in Montana in 1987, by a team led by Jack Horner, with more finds made in 1989. In 1994, Achelousaurus horneri was described and named by Scott D. Sampson; the generic name means "Achelous lizard", in reference to the Greek deity Achelous, and the specific name refers to Horner. The genus is known from a few specimens consisting mainly of skull material from individuals, ranging from juveniles to adults.
diagnostic_features: Relatively small, thin, heavily-pitted nasal boss in adults restricted to the nasal region.
Relatively large, high-ridged supraorbital bosses in adults rather than true horns.
Sub-adults possessing true supraorbital horncores with concave surfaces medially.
Parietal with single pair of curved spikes projecting posterolaterally from the rear margin.

Acheroraptor.etymology: From Greek 'Acheron' (the underworld river) and Latin 'raptor' meaning 'thief' or 'plunderer'; meaning 'underworld thief'
Acheroraptor.description: Acheroraptor is an extinct genus of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in present-day Montana in the United States during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous period. It was described by Canadian paleontologists David Evans, Derek Larson, and Philip J. Currie in 2013. The genus contains a single species, A. temertyorum, named on an isolated maxilla with teeth. An incomplete dentary found nearby was also assigned to the species. These fossils were initially discovered by fossil poachers, though they were later sold to the Royal Ontario Museum, in layers belonging to the Hell Creek Formation. This indicates that these fossils date to the upper Maastrichtian stage, 67.2-66 million years ago.

Maxillary dentition with prominent apicobasal ridges on both labial and lingual surfaces, consistently close to the anterior margins of each side

Achillesaurus.etymology: Named for Achilles' heel from Greek mythology, referencing diagnostic features found in the heel anatomy; combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'. The species name honors Professor Rafael Manazzone.
Achillesaurus.description: Achillesaurus is a genus of alvarezsaurid theropod dinosaur from the Santonian-aged (Late Cretaceous) Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Rio Negro, Argentina. It contains one species, Achillesaurus manazzonei.

Achillobator.etymology: Named after Achilles, the Greek hero, combined with Mongolian 'bator' meaning 'hero'; meaning 'Achilles hero'
Achillobator.description: Achillobator is a genus of large dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period about 96 million to 89 million years ago in what is now the Bayan Shireh Formation of Mongolia. The genus is currently monotypic, only including the type species A. giganticus. The first remains were found in 1989 during a Mongolian-Russian field expedition and later described in 1999. Remains at the type locality of Achillobator may represent additional specimens. It represents the first and largest dromaeosaurid known from the Bayan Shireh Formation.

Acristavus.etymology: From Latin 'a-' meaning 'without', 'crista' meaning 'crest', and 'avus' meaning 'grandfather' or 'ancestor'; meaning 'non-crested grandfather'
Acristavus.description: Acristavus is a genus of saurolophine dinosaur. Fossils have been found from the Campanian Two Medicine Formation in Montana and Wahweap Formation in Utah, United States. The type species A. gagslarsoni was named in 2011. Unlike nearly all hadrosaurids except Edmontosaurus, Acristavus lacked ornamentation on its skull. The discovery of Acristavus is paleontologically significant because it supports the position that the ancestor of all hadrosaurids did not possess cranial ornamentation, and that ornamentation was an adaptation that later arose interdependently in the subfamilies Saurolophinae and Lambeosaurinae. It is closely related to Brachylophosaurus and Maiasaura, and was assigned to a new clade called Brachylophosaurini.
diagnostic_features: Enlarged posterodorsal brow of postorbital and basioccipital extending posteriorly well beyond the dorsal border of the foramen magnum to a greater extent than in other hadrosaurine species.
Deep laterally squared frontonasal suture, with posterolateral corners at nearly 90-degree angles, not seen in other hadrosaurids.
Swelling of the interdigitate suture between the prefrontal and frontal, not seen in other hadrosaurids.
Deep depression on the lateral surface of the postorbital jugal process, absent in all other known hadrosaurids.
Dentary with nearly flat (straight) ventral margin, differing from the downturned anterior dentary of all other hadrosaurids.

Acrocanthosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'akros' meaning 'high', 'akantha' meaning 'spine', and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', referring to its high-spined vertebrae.
Acrocanthosaurus.description: Acrocanthosaurus is a genus of carcharodontosaurid dinosaurs that existed in what is now North America during the Barremian and early Cenomanian stages of the Early Cretaceous and Late Cretaceous, from 125 to 99.6 million years ago. Like most dinosaur genera, Acrocanthosaurus contains only a single species, A. atokensis. It had a continent-wide range, with fossil remains known from the U.S. states of Oklahoma, Texas, and Wyoming in the west and Maryland in the east. However, most of these remains are assigned to the species based on the assumption that Acrocanthosaurus is the only large carcharodontosaurid from North America during this time, and the possibility exists that some referred specimens could represent distinct taxa.

Metatarsal III somewhat constricted proximally by lateral elements (metatarsals II and IV)

Acrotholus.etymology: From Greek 'akros' meaning 'highest' and 'tholos' meaning 'dome', referring to its prominent domed skull.
Acrotholus.description: Acrotholus is an extinct genus of pachycephalosaurian dinosaur that lived during the Santonian of the late Cretaceous, in the Milk River Formation of Canada. The type species, A. audeti, was named after Roy Audet allowing access to his ranch leading to the discovery of the species. The discovery of this specimen lead to several new revelations in the fossil records questioning the preservation of small-bodied organisms along with the evolution of early pachycephalosaurs. The iconic cranial dome found on Acrotholus makes it one of the earliest indisputable known members of the pachycephalosaur family. Like others of its clade, Acrotholus was a bipedal herbivore characterized by a dome-shaped head. The dome had often been associated with intra-species combat, although the exact methods of contact have been debated.

Adelolophus.etymology: From Greek 'adelos' meaning 'unknown' or 'obscure' and 'lophos' meaning 'crest'; meaning 'unknown crest'
Adelolophus.description: Adelolophus is a genus of lambeosaurine dinosaur (a crested "duck-bill") from Upper Cretaceous rocks in the U.S. state of Utah. The type and only known species is A. hutchisoni; the type specimen consists only of a broken maxilla. It constitutes the oldest known lambeosaur remains from North America, as well as the only known lambeosaur species from the Wahweap Formation, of which it pertains to the Upper Member. Among its relatives, it seems to be particularly similar to Parasaurolophus, rather than animals like Lambeosaurus; phylogenetic analysis confirms this, finding it in Parasaurolophini (tube-headed lambeosaurs). It would have lived in a wet environment, bordering on the sea but with a more arid season during some times of the year. This environment would have been shared with a diverse variety of fish and turtles, as well as other dinosaurs like ceratopsids and tyrannosaurids.

Adynomosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'adynamos' meaning 'weak' or 'powerless' and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', referring to its underdeveloped shoulder musculature.
Adynomosaurus.description: Adynomosaurus is a genus of lambeosaurine dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of what is now Catalonia, Spain. First discovered in 2012, it was named in 2019 with the type and only species being Adynomosaurus arcanus. It is only known from scant material, but is distinguished from other hadrosaurs by its weakly developed shoulder blade which would have had underdeveloped musculature, which lends it its scientific name, partially from the Greek word for "weak". Its exact relationships with other hadrosaurs remain unresolved, with it not consistently being recovered as a relative of any other specific genera, though some studies have allied it with Tsintaosaurini or even found it outside of Hadrosauridae. It would have lived as part of a diverse coastal estuary ecosystem, made up of meandering rivers and mud flats. The discovery of Adynomosaurus adds to the very incomplete fossil record of hadrosaurid dinosaurs in the Late Cretaceous of Europe, and it fits into a picture of major ecological turnover that was occurring during the Maastrichtian stage in the region.
diagnostic_features: Scapula with shallow blade: maximum depth of distal scapular blade is less than 75% of the depth of the proximal end (measured from dorsal margin of acromion process to ventral apex of glenoid).

Aegyptosaurus.description: Aegyptosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur discovered in Egypt, that lived in what is now Africa, around 95 million years ago, during the Late Cretaceous Period (Cenomanian faunal stage).
diagnostic_features: Middle caudal vertebral body short and higher than broad, procoelic, with neural arch and thick rudimentary transverse process restricted to anterior half, and concave surface above neural canal anterior to neural arch
Humerus relatively slender, with slight medial expansion of upper end and deltoid crest terminating anteriorly against the shaft midline rather than along the outer margin
Ulna relatively slender, upper end not strongly thickened or broadened, not concave medially above, lower outline oval with medial angle
Femur with weakly developed trochanter IV positioned in upper third of length, and broad surface facing posteriorly beside the lateral condyle below
Scapula lacking ridges, with obtuse angle between straight shaft anterior edge and convex anterior edge of expansion, and moderately acute angle between shaft axis and width axis
Tibia relatively slender, proximal end only moderately broadened with approximately semicircular outline, crista cnemialis apparently not prominent

Aeolosaurus.etymology: Named after Aeolus, the Greek god of winds, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Aeolus' lizard'
Aeolosaurus.description: Aeolosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period of what is now South America. Like most sauropods, it would have been a quadrupedal herbivore with a long neck and tail. Aeolosaurus is well known for a titanosaur, as it is represented by the remains of several individuals belonging to at least two species. However, like most titanosaurs, no remains of the skull are known.

Aepisaurus.etymology: From Greek 'aipeinos' meaning 'lofty' or 'high' and 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'lofty lizard'.
Aepisaurus.description: Aepisaurus was a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Albian-age Lower Cretaceous Grès vert of Département du Vaucluse, France, around 100.5 million years ago. It is an obscure genus from an unknown family, represented by a single humerus, now partly lost. Despite its lack of popularity, or perhaps because of it, it has been misspelled several ways in the scientific literature, with multiple dates given to the year of description as well.
diagnostic_features: Humerus approaching the size of an elephant humerus in a reptile, with total length 0.090 m, width at tuberosities 0.33 m, width at middle 0.15 m, width at condyles 0.25 m.
Humerus form and structure indicating a gigantic reptile with analogy to Monitors and Iguanas, but distinct from Wealden saurians described by Mantell.
Humerus shape closer to Iguanas and Monitors than to any other known group, but with some differences from both.

species.name: Aepisaurus elephantinus
species.etymology: From Latin 'elephantinus' meaning 'elephant-like', likely referring to the large size of the humerus on which the genus is based.

holotype.material: Humerus from green sandstones of Mont Ventoux, Vaucluse, collected near the village of Bedouin.

Aepyornithomimus.etymology: Named after Aepyornis (the extinct elephant bird) combined with Greek 'mimos' meaning 'mimic'; meaning 'Aepyornis mimic'
Aepyornithomimus.description: Aepyornithomimus is a genus of ornithomimid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Djadochta Formation of Mongolia. It lived in the Campanian, around 75 million years ago, when the area is thought to have been a desert. The type and only species is A. tugrikinensis.

Robust distal articular caput of second metatarsal in dorsal view, nearly as wide as distal articulation of Mt III

Medial condyle of phalanx IV-1 inclined laterally at ~35°, greater than in any other known ornithomimosaur
Proximoventral ridge of phalanx II-1 forming a rounded curvature (rectilinear in other ornithomimosaurs)

Aerosteon.etymology: From Greek 'aer' meaning 'air' and 'osteon' meaning 'bone', referring to its air-filled bones.
Aerosteon.description: Aerosteon is a genus of megaraptoran dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period of Argentina. Its remains were discovered in 1996 in the Anacleto Formation, which is from the late Campanian. The type and only known species is A. riocoloradensis. Its generic name can be translated as "air bone" and derives from Greek ἀήρ (aer, "air") and ὀστέον (osteon, "bone"), whereas its specific name indicates that its remains were found 1 km (0.6 miles) north of the Río Colorado, in Mendoza Province, Argentina. The genus shows evidence of a bird-like respiratory system.
diagnostic_features: Prefrontal with a very short ventral process along the orbital margin.
Enlarged quadrate foramen located entirely within the quadrate shaft, not shared with the quadratojugal.
Large tympanic diverticulum (pneumatocoel) extending deep into the quadrate shaft above the articular condyle.
Furcula with a median pneumatocoel opening as a slit-shaped pneumatopore on the posterior surface.
Medial gastral elements coossified with anterior and posterior flanges in the midline.
Posteriormost dorsal vertebra with a pneumatic canal running within the transverse process and an anterodorsally inclined neural spine.

species.name: Aerosteon riocoloradensis
species.etymology: Indicates that the remains were found approximately 1 km north of the Río Colorado in Mendoza Province, Argentina.

Afromimus.etymology: From 'Africa' combined with Greek 'mimos' meaning 'mimic'; meaning 'Africa mimic'
Afromimus.description: Afromimus is a genus of ceratosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Elrhaz Formation of Niger. It contains a single species, A. tenerensis, named in 2017 by Paul Sereno from parts of the right leg, vertebrae, and ribs found in the Ténéré Desert. It was originally described as a genus of ornithomimosaurian, but subsequent arguments have placed it as a taxon within or close to the superfamily Abelisauroidea.
diagnostic_features: Large elliptical attachment scar on the posterolateral aspect of the proximal tibial shaft distal to the lateral condyle
Rugose attachment surface on the fibula posterior to the tibial crest
Trough on the anteromedial aspect of the fibular shaft ventral to the anterior trochanter
Rugose texture on non-articular surfaces of pre- and postzygapophyses of mid caudal vertebrae, with elevated zygapophyseal facets
Fused pedicels on anterior chevrons that are less than one half as long anteroposteriorly as broad transversely

species.etymology: Combines the name of the Ténéré Desert of Niger, where the holotype was recovered.

Afrovenator.etymology: From Latin 'Afro' referring to Africa and 'venator' meaning 'hunter', meaning 'African hunter'.
Afrovenator.description: Afrovenator is an extinct genus of megalosaurid theropod dinosaur from the Middle or Late Jurassic Tiourarén Formation and maybe the Irhazer II Formation of the Sahara region of Niger in western Africa. Afrovenator represents the only named definitive Gondwanan megalosaur, with proposed material of the group present in the Tacuarembó Formation of Uruguay and the Tendaguru Formation of Tanzania, both dated to the Late Jurassic.
diagnostic_features: Maxilla with lobe-shaped anterior margin of antorbital fossa
Third cervical vertebra with a low, rectangular neural spine
Very flat semilunate carpal
Metacarpal I with a broad flange for articulation against metacarpal II

Agathaumas.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'αγαν' (agan, 'much') and 'θαυμα' (thauma, 'wonder'); meaning 'much wonder', given by Cope in reference to the large size of the type material.
Agathaumas.description: Agathaumas is a dubious genus of a large ceratopsid dinosaur that lived in Wyoming during the Late Cretaceous (late Maastrichtian stage, 66 million years ago). It was seen as the largest land animal known at the time of its discovery.
diagnostic_features: Dorsal centra vertically oval with small neural canal and greatly elevated neural spine, arch short antero-posteriorly
Sacrum of five vertebrae with huge diapophyses united by suture, each pair supporting a longitudinal convex articular face for the ilium
Ilium extended antero-posteriorly with large protuberance above acetabular sinus; one end dilated into a flat thin plate, total length approximately four feet

Agilisaurus.etymology: From Latin 'agilis' meaning 'agile' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'agile lizard'.
Agilisaurus.description: Agilisaurus is a genus of ornithischian dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Period of what is now eastern Asia. The only named species is A. louderbacki, recovered from the Lower Shaximiao Formation of Sichuan, China. It was about 1.2-1.7 m (3.9-5.6 ft) in length, 60 cm (2.0 ft) in hip height, and 40 kg (88 lb) in weight. It has leaf-shaped teeth that were well-adapted to its abrasive, plant-based diet. Most surprisingly, the wavy enamel of the teeth of this genus (and all other ornithopods), presumed to make them more resistant to wear, was previously thought to be exclusive to hadrosaurs. This is also the case for Changchunsaurus from the Cretaceous Period.

Nasal long with longitudinal depression at central suture
Posterior process of premaxilla does not contact the lacrimal
Palpebral bone well-developed, posterior end abutting lateral surface of postorbital, dividing orbit into upper and lower openings

Agrosaurus.etymology: From Greek agros ('field') and sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'field lizard'
Agrosaurus.description: Agrosaurus is a potentially dubious genus of thecodontosaurid sauropodomorph probably originating from the Magnesian Conglomerate of England that was originally believed to be a Triassic prosauropod from Australia. Agrosaurus would thus be the oldest dinosaur from that country. However, this appears to have been an error, and the material actually appears to come from Thecodontosaurus or a Thecodontosaurus-like animal from Bristol, England (Avon Fissure Fill). The type species is Agrosaurus macgillivrayi.

Proximal end of tibia enlarged and curves backward relative to slender shaft
Pre-cnemial crest only slightly developed
Distal end of tibia increases uniformly in size with no sharp definition from shaft
Distal tibial articulation moderately excavated on the inner side, with a deep anterior notch dividing the quadrate articular surface

Agujaceratops.description: Agujaceratops is a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) of western Texas. Two species are known: A. mariscalensis and A. mavericus, both recovered from the Aguja Formation.

Agustinia.etymology: Named for Agustin Martinelli, a student who discovered the skeleton and participated in the excavation team of the Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales.
Agustinia.description: Agustinia is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of South America. The genus contains a single species, A. ligabuei, known from a single specimen that was recovered from the Lohan Cura Formation of Neuquén Province in Argentina. It lived about 116-108 million years ago, in the Aptian-Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous Period.

Ahshislepelta.etymology: Named after Ah-shi-sle-pah Wash, the locality where the fossil was found, combined with Greek 'pelta' meaning 'shield'; meaning 'Ah-shi-sle-pah Wash shield'
Ahshislepelta.description: Ahshislepelta is a monospecific genus of ankylosaur dinosaur from New Mexico that lived during the Late Cretaceous (late Campanian stage, 74.5 Ma) in what is now the Hunter Wash Member of the Kirtland Formation. The type and only species, Ahshislepelta minor, is known only from an incomplete postcranial skeleton of a small subadult or adult individual. It was named in 2011 by Michael Burns and Robert M. Sullivan. Based on the size of the humerus, Ahshislepelta is larger than Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus but smaller than Talarurus and Pinacosaurus grangeri.

Sparse reticular pattern of neurovascular grooves on osteoderm surface.

Ahshislesaurus.etymology: Named for the Ah-shi-sle-pah Wilderness in New Mexico, a phonetic transliteration of the Navajo áshįįh łibá meaning 'salt, it is gray', combined with Ancient Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'. The species name honors Swedish paleontologist Carl Wiman.
Ahshislesaurus.description: Ahshislesaurus is an extinct genus of saurolophine hadrosaurid dinosaurs known from the Late Cretaceous of what is now New Mexico, United States. It is known from a partial skull and three neck vertebrae discovered in 1916 and first described in 1935. Prior to its scientific naming, researchers debated whether the specimen belonged to Kritosaurus navajovius, a related species from the same layers of rocks, or a distinct animal. The genus contains a single species, Ahshislesaurus wimani, named in 2025. A partial skeleton and isolated limb and girdle bones found in the same rock layers may also belong to Ahshislesaurus.

Ahvaytum.description: Ahvaytum is an extinct genus of probable basal sauropodomorph saurischian dinosaurs from the Late Triassic Popo Agie Formation of Wyoming, United States. The genus contains a single species, A. bahndooiveche, known from fragmentary hindlimb bones. Ahvaytum represents the oldest known named dinosaur of the ancient Laurasian landmass.

Ajkaceratops.etymology: Named for Ajka, the town in Hungary near where it was discovered, combined with Greek 'keratops' meaning 'horned face'.
Ajkaceratops.description: Ajkaceratops is a genus of ceratopsian dinosaur described in 2010. It lived during the Late Cretaceous in the western Tethyan archipelago, in what is now Europe. The type species, A. kozmai, was originally described as a ceratopsian most closely related to forms in east Asia, from where its ancestors may have migrated by island-hopping. Later research, however, questioned this assignment and treated Ajkaceratops as an ornithischian of unresolved affinity. In 2026, more complete cranial remains referable to the species were described, supporting its placement as a ceratopsian.

Ajnabia.etymology: From Arabic 'ajnabia' meaning 'stranger' or 'foreigner', reflecting the unexpected presence of hadrosaurs in Africa
Ajnabia.description: Ajnabia is a genus of lambeosaurine hadrosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) of Morocco. It is the first definitive hadrosaur from Africa and is thought to be related to European hadrosaurs like Adynomosaurus and Pararhabdodon. The discovery of Ajnabia came as a surprise to the paleontologists who found it because Africa was isolated by water from the rest of the world during the Cretaceous, such that hadrosaurs were assumed to have been unable to reach the continent.
diagnostic_features: Maxillary neurovascular foramina with a hypertrophied foramen below the jugal articulation and a smaller accessory foramen below that
Ectopterygoid ridge ventrally positioned on maxilla, weakly inclined relative to the dentigerous process, developed as a massive, dorsoventrally thick, rounded, lip-like structure
Ectopterygoid ridge reduced anteriorly, failing to contact the jugal articulation
Maxillary tooth crowns with tips curled medially, median ridge offset posteriorly, accessory ridges absent, denticles highly reduced
Strong downturn of the premaxillary process of the maxilla

species.name: Ajnabia odysseus
species.etymology: Named for the Greek hero and legendary sea voyager Odysseus, in reference to the oceanic dispersal believed to have brought this hadrosaur's ancestors to Africa.

holotype.material: Partial left maxilla with teeth, fragments of right maxilla, partial left dentary

Akainacephalus.etymology: From Greek 'akaina' meaning 'thorn' or 'spike' and 'kephale' meaning 'head'; meaning 'thorn head'
Akainacephalus.description: Akainacephalus is a monospecific genus of ankylosaurid dinosaur from southern Utah that lived during the Late Cretaceous (late Campanian, 76.26 Ma) in what is now the Horse Mountain Gryposaur Quarry of the Kaiparowits Formation. The type and only species, Akainacephalus johnsoni, is known from the most complete ankylosaur specimen ever discovered from southern Laramidia, including a complete skull, tail club, a number of osteoderms, limb elements and part of its pelvis, among other remains. It was described in 2018 by Jelle P. Wiersma and Randall B. Irmis. It is closely related and shares similar cranial anatomy to Nodocephalosaurus.
diagnostic_features: Massive supraorbital bosses forming a tall backswept flange extending laterally over the orbits and enveloping the anterodorsal and posterior margins of the orbit
Nearly vertical projecting triangular quadratojugal horns
Frontal bears a large, flat, centrally positioned hexagonal-shaped caputegulum
Tightly spaced, symmetrically positioned pyramidal and conical-shaped caputegulae across the frontonasal region
Distinct midline row of conical-shaped caputegulae across the nasal region, symmetrically separating dorsolateral caputegulae
Basioccipital foramen positioned anterior and dorsal to the occipital condyle

species.name: Akainacephalus johnsoni
species.etymology: Named for Randy Johnson, the volunteer preparator at the Natural History Museum of Utah who prepared the skull and lower jaws of the holotype.

Alamosaurus.etymology: Named after the Ojo Alamo rock formation combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Ojo Alamo lizard'
Alamosaurus.description: Alamosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaurs containing a single known species, Alamosaurus sanjuanensis, from the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period in what is now southwestern North America. It is one of the few known titanosaurs to have inhabited North America after the nearly 30-million-year absence of sauropods from the North American fossil record ("sauropod hiatus") and probably represents an immigrant from South America.
diagnostic_features: Scapula blade gradually widens from below upward to superior end with no expansion of anterior border and no rapid superior expansion of both borders as in other sauropods
Scapular spine runs at approximately 90 degrees to the longitudinal axis of the bone, not at an acute angle as in Diplodocus and Amphicoelias
No superior fossa on upper side of scapular ridge, unlike many sauropod scapulae
Ischium extremely short, lacking the long slender posterior extension characteristic of all other known sauropod ischia
Ischium with unusually great dorsoventral diameter at proximal end and pubic articular surface extending distalward more than half the total bone length

Alaskacephale.etymology: Named for Alaska, where it was discovered, combined with Greek 'kephale' meaning 'head', referring to its pachycephalosaurid dome-headed nature.
Alaskacephale.description: Alaskacephale is an extinct genus of pachycephalosaurid, a group of dome-headed, herbivorous ornithischian dinosaurs, that lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous period in what is now northern Alaska. The genus is one of the few known Arctic dinosaurs and was found in the Prince Creek Formation, which preserves a menagerie of fossils. The only known specimen, a squamosal bone, was found in 1999 and later described in 2005. However, Alaskacephale was not formally named until the next year.
