Baalsaurus.etymology: Named after the Baal fossil site in Argentina (itself named after the ancient Phoenician god Baal) combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'Baal lizard'.
Baalsaurus.description: Baalsaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Neuquén Province, Patagonia, Argentina. The type and only known species is B. mansillai, with the specific name honoring the discoverer Juan Eduardo Mansilla, a museum technician at the Geology and Paleontology Museum of the National University of Comahue.
diagnostic_features: Dentary alveoli with 10 alveoli on the anterior ramus (unique among known titanosaur dentaries).
Dentary symphysis inclined ventrally and anteriorly (anteroventrally), unlike other titanosaurs where it is perpendicular or inclined posteroventrally.
Wide ventral Meckelian groove surrounded by a thin lamina forming a keel on the ventral border of the dentary.

species.name: Baalsaurus mansillai
species.etymology: Named for Juan Eduardo Mansilla, a museum technician at the Geology and Paleontology Museum of the National University of Comahue who discovered the holotype.

holotype.material: Almost complete right dentary with 13 alveoli.

Bactrosaurus.etymology: From Greek baktron (βάκτρον) meaning 'club' or 'walking stick' + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'club lizard'.
Bactrosaurus.description: Bactrosaurus is a genus of herbivorous hadrosauroid dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous, from about 96 to 85 million years ago. The position Bactrosaurus occupies in the Cretaceous makes it one of the earliest known hadrosauroids, and although it is not known from a full skeleton, Bactrosaurus is one of the best known of these early hadrosauroids, making its discovery a significant finding.
diagnostic_features: Posterior dorsal vertebrae with tall club-shaped spines, transverse diameter increasing from base to top, nearly as wide fore-and-aft as centrum length.
Sacrum composed of seven coossified vertebrae.
Ilium strongly arched upward at center with strongly decurved, blade-like preacetabular process.
Pubis with very short neck and greatly expanded prepubic blade, far shorter and more expanded than in any other known hadrosaurian.
Dentition reduced: 20-23 vertical tooth rows in dentary, 28 in maxillary (fewest in any known hadrosaurian at adult size).
Pes unguals with squarely truncated, rugosely roughened anterior margins in adults.

Never formally published; reported by Olshevsky (1991).

Bagaceratops.etymology: From Mongolian baga meaning 'small' + Greek keras (κέρας) meaning 'horn' + ops (ὤψ) meaning 'face'; overall meaning 'small-horned face'.
Bagaceratops.description: Bagaceratops is a genus of small protoceratopsid dinosaurs that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous, around 72 to 71 million years ago. Bagaceratops remains have been reported from the Barun Goyot Formation and Bayan Mandahu Formation. One specimen may argue the possible presence of Bagaceratops in the Djadochta Formation.

Nasals bearing a prominent unpaired horn core
Additional antorbital fenestra present, located at the premaxilla-maxilla suture
Premaxillary dentition absent; anterior edentulous portion of upper jaw very long
Mandible shallow with straight ventral margin
Ten maxillary teeth in largest known specimen

Bagaraatan.etymology: From Mongolian 'baga' (small) and 'araatan' (carnivorous animal, beast of prey); meaning 'small predator'.
Bagaraatan.description: Bagaraatan is a genus of theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period of what is now the Nemegt Formation of Mongolia. It may have been a small predatory dinosaur measuring around 3 to 4 meters (9.8 to 13.1 ft) in length.
diagnostic_features: Mandible with two surangular foramina separated by a flat, ventrally descending process
Caudal vertebrae with hollow, very thin-walled centra filled with crystallized matrix
Hyposphene-hypantrum articulation stout and present in at least sixteen proximal caudals
Prezygapophyses in proximal caudals with ridges on lateral surfaces, subvertically oriented
Ilium with two deep depressions on lateral surface of postacetabular process separated by a crestlike projection
Femur with anterior crest below lesser trochanter (absent in all other known archosaurs)
Tibia and fibula fused distally with each other and with coalesced astragalocalcaneum
Double surangular foramina (anterior and posterior)
Horizontal ridge on lateral surface of postacetabular process of ilium

Bagualia.etymology: From Spanish baguala meaning 'wild horse', referencing Bagual Canyon in Chubut, Argentina, where the fossils were discovered.
Bagualia.description: Bagualia is an extinct genus of eusauropod dinosaur from the Early Jurassic (middle Toarcian) Cañadón Asfalto Formation in what is now the Chubut Province of Argentina. The type species, B. alba, was formally described in 2020. Bagualia represents the oldest known definitive eusauropod, and due to the completeness of its material, it represents one of the most important taxa for understanding the early evolution of the group.
diagnostic_features: Pointed process on the anteroventral end of the premaxilla and anterodorsal end of the dentary (autapomorphy).
Anterior margin of the premaxilla without a marked step (autapomorphy).
Orbital margin of the frontal with a close V-shape pointed medially, resulting in a short contribution to the orbit (autapomorphy).
Supratemporal fenestra about as anteroposteriorly long as lateromedially wide (autapomorphy).
Concave ventral margin of the distal portion of the cultriform process (autapomorphy).
Accessory lamina below the PCDL in middle cervical vertebrae (autapomorphy).

species.name: Bagualia alba
species.etymology: From Spanish 'alba' meaning 'dawn', highlighting the dinosaur's early position in the sauropod lineage.

holotype.material: Posterior half of skull articulated with seven cervical vertebrae.

Bagualosaurus.etymology: From 'bagual', a term in the dialect of Rio Grande do Sul (Brazil) meaning 'strongly built fellow', referring to the strong hindlimbs of the animal, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'. The species name refers to the provenance from the town of Agudo.
Bagualosaurus.description: Bagualosaurus is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Candelária Sequence (Uppermost Santa Maria Formation) of Brazil, dating to around 230 million years ago, in the Carnian of the Late Triassic. It includes one species, Bagualosaurus agudoensis.
diagnostic_features: Dorsal surface of iliac acetabulum straight, with supracetabular crest not overhanging the acetabulum ventrally (autapomorphy)
Pubic tubercle with a distinct longitudinal sulcus (autapomorphy)
Lateromedially widened pubic peduncle with no dorsal crest
Distal tibia with a conspicuous caudomedial notch
First premaxillary tooth at least as high as the highest tooth in the maxillary row
Premaxillary and dentary teeth retreated from the rostral margin of the snout

Bahariasaurus.etymology: From Bahariya (the Bahariya Oasis and Formation in Egypt, where the fossils were found) + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'Bahariya lizard'.
Bahariasaurus.description: Bahariasaurus is an enigmatic genus of large theropod dinosaur. The genus contains a single species, Bahariasaurus ingens, which was found in North African rock layers dating to the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous. The only fossils confidently assigned to Bahariasaurus were found in the Bahariya Formation of the Bahariya Oasis in Egypt by Ernst Stromer. This material was destroyed during a World War II bombing raid, with the same raid also destroying the holotypes of Spinosaurus, Aegyptosaurus, and other animals found in the Bahariya Formation.
diagnostic_features: Posterior dorsal vertebrae platycoelous, strongly elongate (nearly twice as long as high anteriorly), diaphysis constricted with lateral oval foramen indicating internal hollowness, diapophysis broad supported only by posterior strut, no parapophysis
Sacrum of 3 vertebrae with platycoelous elongate bodies, each with a lateral foramen and a broad longitudinal ventral groove
Pubic foot extremely small and almost lacking an anterior part, shaft forms U-shape with contralateral bone, very long symphysis with thin connecting lamella ending above the foot
Ilium with remarkably straight upper margin, postacetabular part tapering to an acute posterior angle, ischial process very short

Femur shaft slender and convexly curved forward; trochanter IV only a strong longitudinal ridge positioned above mid-shaft; medial condyle below flatter and less deeply projecting than the strongly arched outer condyle

Scapula shaft of approximately constant width to the very top (not expanded distally), contrasting with all known theropods; coracoid triangular without posterior median corner, with foramen near the joint

species.etymology: From Latin 'ingens' meaning 'huge', referring to the enormous size of the animal.

holotype.material: Group of gypsum-preserved bones: sacrum of 3 fused vertebral bodies, posterior dorsal and cervical vertebrae, ossa pubis, ischium, and rib fragments.

Bainoceratops.etymology: From the Bain-Dzak locality (Mongolian for "rich-in-saxaul", the Mongolian name for the Flaming Cliffs of the Gobi Desert) and Greek keratops (horned face); meaning "Bain-Dzak horned face".
Bainoceratops.description: Bainoceratops is a genus of ceratopsian dinosaur from the late Campanian in the Late Cretaceous. The type species is B. efremovi. Its fossils were found in southern Mongolia in the Djadochta Formation.
diagnostic_features: Presacral vertebral centra with concave cranial surfaces and flat caudal surfaces.
Diapophyses of the ninth dorsal vertebra circular in cross section; interprezygapophyseal spaces of dorsals 9 and 10 narrow.
Synapophyseal facets of the posteriormost dorsal vertebra sculptured with a median crest.

species.name: Bainoceratops efremovi
species.etymology: Named after Ivan Antonovich Efremov (1908-1972), the Soviet paleontologist and writer who led the early Soviet expeditions to the Gobi Desert.

holotype.institution: Paleontological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences
holotype.material: Postcranial vertebral series including cervicals 6, 7, 9; thoracics ?1, ?5-7, 9-13; sacral 8; and caudals 1-3, ?10-11, ?18-19. No cranial material.

Baiyinosaurus.etymology: From Baiyin (the city of Baiyin in Gansu Province, China, near where the fossils were found) + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'Baiyin reptile'.
Baiyinosaurus.description: Baiyinosaurus is an extinct genus of stegosaurian dinosaurs from the Middle Jurassic Wangjiashan Formation of China. The genus contains a single species, B. baojiensis, known from a partial skeleton including cranial bones. The skeletal anatomy of Baiyinosaurus demonstrates transitional features between basal thyreophorans and stegosaurs. While many stegosaurs are known from China, Baiyinosaurus is the only one currently named from Gansu Province.
diagnostic_features: Frontal wider than long and contributes to both the medial and anterior margins of the supratemporal fenestra (unique among Stegosauria).
Neural arches not greatly elongated dorsally: ratio of neural arch height to neural canal height is 1.59.
Parapophyses well developed and project somewhat laterally on stalks in anterior view.
Neural spines anteroposteriorly broad and axially expanded in lateral view: ratio of neural spine length to centrum length is 0.75.

species.name: Baiyinosaurus baojiensis
species.etymology: References the type locality in the Baojishan Basin in the Qilian Mountains, Gansu Province, China.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology, Gansu Agricultural University
holotype.material: Partial skeleton comprising a partial cranium, one cervical vertebra, seven dorsal vertebrae and one caudal vertebra.

Bajadasaurus.etymology: Named after La Bajada, the locality in Patagonia, Argentina where it was found, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'Bajada lizard'.
Bajadasaurus.description: Bajadasaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous epoch (late Berriasian to Valanginian stages, between 145 and 132.9 million years ago) of northern Patagonia, Argentina. It was first described in 2019 based on a single specimen found in 2010 that includes a largely complete skull and parts of the neck. The only species is Bajadasaurus pronuspinax. The genus is classified as a member of the Dicraeosauridae, a group of relatively small and short-necked sauropods.

Basipterygoid processes extremely slender and long, more than six times longer than lateromedially wide (autapomorphy)
Elongate angular, longer than the anteroposterior surangular length
Neural spine of the axis oriented vertically (autapomorphy)
Paired, anteriorly curved, and extremely elongate bifid neural spines of anterior-mid cervical vertebrae (autapomorphy)

Balaur.etymology: From Romanian balaur ('dragon' of Romanian folklore)
Balaur.description: Balaur is a genus of paravian theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) of what is now Romania. It contains a single species, Balaur bondoc, known from two partial skeletons. Its short, stocky build and double sickle claws on each foot are interpreted as an example of island syndrome on the Late Cretaceous Hațeg Island archipelago.
diagnostic_features: Fused carpometacarpus with reduced splint-like metacarpal III only 30% the mediolateral width of metacarpal II, digit III nonfunctional
Extremely retroverted pubes and ischia with long axes nearly horizontal, associated with enlarged cuppedicus fossa on laterally everted pubic peduncle
Fused metatarsus (metatarsals II-V fused across much of their lengths), tarsometatarsus substantially wider than distal tibiotarsus
Enlarged functional first pedal digit with hyperextensive ungual (second largest in foot), giving the animal a double set of raptorial claws
Hypertrophied coracoid tubercle projecting anteriorly and laterally as a conical projection that obscures the coracoid foramen in lateral view
Sinuous ridge on lateral surface of distal humerus extending for one-third the length of the bone, unique among all theropods

Bambiraptor.etymology: Named after the Disney movie character Bambi (itself from Italian bambino meaning 'child') combined with Latin raptor meaning 'thief'. Full meaning: 'Bambi thief', referring to its small size.
Bambiraptor.description: Bambiraptor is a genus of bird-like dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous (about 72 million years ago) of Montana. It was described by scientists at the University of Kansas, Yale University, and the University of New Orleans. The holotype fossil is less than 1 m (3.3 ft) long, although this specimen appears to be a juvenile, and it is possible that Bambiraptor is a juvenile Saurornitholestes. It is even suspected that the type specimen is a chimera, based on the fact that "there are elements of three different similarly sized lower legs included in the holotype." Because of its small size, it was named Bambiraptor feinbergi, after the popular Disney movie character (the name literally translates to "Bambi thief") and the surname of the wealthy family who bought and lent the specimen to the new Graves Museum of Natural History in Florida.

Scapula with large, medially directed acromion and distinct, short scapulocoracoid suture
Coracoid with neck or peduncle forming part of glenoid; coracoid foramen absent
13 Dentary teeth and 9 maxillary teeth
Ratio of humerus plus ulna to femur notably large (H+U/F = 1.68)
Femur strongly recurved both laterally and posteriorly; lacks fourth trochanter

Banji.description: Banji is an extinct genus of oviraptorid dinosaur that lived approximately 66 million years ago during the later part of the Cretaceous Period in what is now China. It was a small, lightly built, ground-dwelling, bipedal carnivore, that was an estimated 65 cm (2.1 ft) long, as a juvenile.

Bannykus.description: Bannykus is an extinct genus of alvarezsauroid from the Early Cretaceous Bayin-Gobi Formation of Inner Mongolia, China. It includes one species, Bannykus wulatensis.

Baotianmansaurus.etymology: Named for the Baotianman National Nature Reserve in Henan Province, China, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Baotianmansaurus.description: Baotianmansaurus is an extinct genus of somphospondylian sauropod. Its fossils were discovered in the Late Cretaceous Gaogou Formation of Henan Province, China. The type and only species is B. henanensis - named after the province in which it was found.
diagnostic_features: Transverse process of dorsal vertebra supported by four laminae (ppdl, pcdl, aspdl, pspdl), differing from all other sauropods whose transverse processes are supported by three laminae.
Dorsal portion of the anterior centroparapophyseal lamina is bifurcated, with a small branch extending to the ventral surface of the prezygapophysis.
Posterior centrodiapophyseal lamina is thin, nearly vertical, and plate-like, not forked at its ventral end.
Postzygodiapophyseal lamina undeveloped, not reaching the top of the diapophysis.
Anterior dorsal ribs apneumatic with a large concavity on the posterior surface of the proximal end, lacking a pneumatic foramen near the proximal end.
Anterior caudal vertebra much shorter than wide, amphicoelous, with suboval articular ends.

species.etymology: Named for Henan Province in China, where the fossil remains were discovered.

holotype.material: Incomplete anterior dorsal vertebra (3rd), nearly complete mid-posterior dorsal vertebra (5th), five dorsal ribs, one and a half sacral vertebrae, one incomplete anterior caudal vertebra, portion of distal scapula, unidentified bone fragments.

Barapasaurus.etymology: From 'bara' meaning 'big' and 'pa' meaning 'leg' in several Indian languages including Bengali, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'big-legged lizard', referring to a femur measuring over 1.7 m. The species name honors Bengali poet Rabindranath Tagore.
Barapasaurus.description: Barapasaurus is a genus of basal sauropod dinosaur from Jurassic rocks of India. The only species is B. tagorei. Barapasaurus comes from the lower part of the Kota Formation, which is of Early to Middle Jurassic in age. It is therefore one of the earliest known sauropods. Barapasaurus is known from approximately 300 bones from at least six individuals, so that the skeleton is almost completely known except for the anterior cervical vertebrae and the skull. This makes Barapasaurus one of the most completely known sauropods from the Early Jurassic.
diagnostic_features: Teeth spoon-shaped with anterior and posterior keels bearing coarse denticles
Centra not cavernous but with oval or ovoidal depressions in the lateral or laterodorsal surface
Sacricostal yokes of sacrum set close together and do not contribute to the medial wall of the acetabulum
Ilium with rather deep medial wall of the acetabulum; ischiadic peduncle short, pubic peduncle long and directed ventrally and slightly anteriorly
Femora retaining a central cavity; lesser trochanter absent, fourth trochanter well-developed ridge-like with possible acute declined tip
Scapula with tall narrow blade, anterior border passing by relatively shallow gradual curve into moderately broad proximal expansion

Barilium.etymology: From Greek barys meaning 'heavy' combined with Latin ilium (the hip bone). Full meaning: 'heavy ilium', referring to the robust hip bone.
Barilium.description: Barilium is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur which was first described as a species of Iguanodon (I. dawsoni) by Richard Lydekker in 1888, the specific epithet honoring the discoverer Charles Dawson, who collected the holotype during the 1880s.
diagnostic_features: Rim of the sacrodorsal rib facet visible in lateral view in the upper part of the recess between the preacetabular process and the pubic peduncle (autapomorphy).
Lateral surface of the preacetabular process twists axially to face dorsally toward its anterior end (autapomorphy).
Dorsal edge of the acetabular blade is flattened and transversely thick (autapomorphy).
Very restricted brevis shelf (fossa) not bounded by a prominent lateral ridge (autapomorphy).
Posterior dorsal vertebrae have spool-shaped cylindrical centra with thin everted articular margins and transversely rounded haemal surfaces (autapomorphy).
Proximal caudal vertebrae have broad, dorsoventrally compressed centra (subrectangular in anterior view) (autapomorphy).

holotype.material: Partial skeleton.

synonyms.reason: Iguanodon dawsoni was first reassigned to Barilium dawsoni and then independently re-erected as Torilion dawsoni; Torilion is now treated as a junior synonym of Barilium.

Barosaurus.etymology: From Greek barys (βαρυς) meaning 'heavy' and Greek sauros (σαυρος) meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'heavy lizard'.
Barosaurus.description: Barosaurus is an extinct genus of giant, long-tailed, long-necked, plant-eating sauropod dinosaur closely related to the more familiar Diplodocus. Definitive remains have been found in the Morrison Formation from the Upper Jurassic Period of South Dakota, Utah and Montana, with other possible remains also found in Colorado, eastern Wyoming and Oklahoma. The generic name, Barosaurus, comes from the Greek words barys (βαρυς) meaning "heavy" and sauros (σαυρος) meaning "lizard", and thus meaning "heavy lizard".
diagnostic_features: Anterior caudal centra deeply excavated on both sides, excavation extending nearly or quite through the centrum with only a thin septum remaining
Median caudal centra with a deep lateral cavity on each side
Caudal vertebrae proportionally shorter than in Diplodocus
Caudal chevrons lacking the anterior projection present in Diplodocus
Distal caudal centra with lateral cavities nearly or quite absent

Barrosasaurus.etymology: Named for the Sierra Barrosa in Neuquén Province, Argentina, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'. The species name honors Argentine paleontologist Rodolfo Casamiquela.
Barrosasaurus.description: Barrosasaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur, first described by paleontologists Leonardo Salgado and Rodolfo Coria in 2009. The fossils, consisting of three fossil dorsal (back) vertebrae, are well-preserved but incomplete. They were discovered in the Anacleto Formation of the Neuquén province of western Argentina. The type species is Barrosasaurus casamiquelai. The genus name is named after the Sierra Barrosa in Neuquén. The specific epithet honors the Argentinian paleontologist Rodolfo Magín Casamiquela. It has been estimated to be 18 meters (60 ft) in length and 13.5 tonnes (14.9 short tons) in weight.
diagnostic_features: Posterior dorsal vertebrae bearing paired, short spinal laminae nearly parallel to the prespinal lamina (relictual spinoprezygapophyseal laminae).
Well-developed anterior spinodiapophyseal laminae in posterior dorsal vertebrae, more strongly developed than the posterior spinodiapophyseal laminae in the posteriormost dorsal.
Anterior spinodiapophyseal lamina divided into at least two, and up to three, branches in the posteriormost dorsal vertebrae.
Aliform processes with broad, planar, and rugose laterodorsal surfaces.
Portion of neural spine distal to the aliform process is longer than the portion proximal to the aliform process, at least in the posterior dorsals.

Barsboldia.etymology: Named after Rinchen Barsbold, a well-known Mongolian paleontologist, with the Latin suffix -ia; overall meaning 'of Barsbold'.
Barsboldia.description: Barsboldia is a genus of large hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Maastrichtian Nemegt Formation of Ömnogöv, Mongolia. It is known from a partial vertebral column, partial pelvis, and some ribs.

Baryonyx.etymology: From Greek 'barys' meaning 'heavy' and 'onyx' meaning 'claw', referring to the large, heavy thumb claw that is characteristic of this dinosaur.
Baryonyx.description: Baryonyx is a genus of theropod dinosaur which lived in the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous period, about 130-125 million years ago. The first skeleton was discovered in 1983 in the Smokejack Clay Pit, of Surrey, England, in sediments of the Weald Clay Formation, and became the holotype specimen of Baryonyx walkeri, named by paleontologists Alan J. Charig and Angela C. Milner in 1986. The genus name Baryonyx comes from Ancient Greek βαρύς (barús), meaning "heavy" or "strong", and ὄνυξ (ónux), meaning "claw", alluding to the animal's very large claw on the first finger; the specific name, walkeri, refers to its discoverer, amateur fossil collector William J. Walker. The holotype specimen is one of the most complete theropod skeletons from the UK (and remains the most complete spinosaurid), and its discovery attracted media attention. Specimens later discovered in other parts of the United Kingdom and Iberia have also been assigned to the genus, though many have since been moved to new genera.
diagnostic_features: Prenarial rostrum extremely narrow with a spatulate, horizontal expansion at its tip, slightly downturned in lateral view
Unusually high tooth count (~double typical theropods: dentary 32), crowns lightly fluted lingually with very fine serrations (~7 per mm) on anterior and posterior keels
Long, strongly opisthocoelous cervical vertebrae with well-developed epiphyses and short neural spines; apposed centra do not produce the typical theropod upward neck curvature
Humerus with both ends broadly expanded and extremely flattened, offset ~35° against each other, with a massive nearly straight shaft
Small median knob at posterior end of conjoined nasals, cruciform in dorsal view, with anterior limb drawn forward into a low thin median crest
At least one pair of exceptionally large ungual phalanges (huge talons), probably on the manus, far exceeding typical theropod ungual proportions

Bashanosaurus.etymology: From Bashan (巴山, an ancient name for the Chongqing/Sichuan region of China, where the fossils were found) + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'Bashan lizard'.
Bashanosaurus.description: Bashanosaurus is an extinct genus of stegosaurian dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic (Bathonian age) Shaximiao Formation of Yunyang County, China. The genus contains a single species, Bashanosaurus primitivus, known from incomplete skeletons belonging to three individuals. It is one of the basalmost stegosaurs, as well as one of the oldest known stegosaurs, along with Adratiklit, Isaberrysaura, and Thyreosaurus.
diagnostic_features: Parapophyses of dorsal vertebrae elevated on stalks at the base of the transverse process, clearly visible in anterior and posterior views.
Scapula blade is slender and flares distally (ratio of maximum to minimum blade height ~3.4), unlike other stegosaurs where the blade does not expand distally.
Acromial process of the scapula is small, triangular, and poorly developed, less developed than in Huayangosaurus.
Fourth trochanter of the femur is positioned below the middle of the shaft, distinct from stegosaurs where it is at midshaft or poorly developed.
Bases of dermal plates are strongly convex and transversely thickened, separated from the anterior/posterior plate margins by a distinct groove.

species.name: Bashanosaurus primitivus
species.etymology: References the fact that Bashanosaurus is among the earliest diverging stegosaurians.

Batyrosaurus.etymology: From Kazakh batyr meaning 'hero warrior' combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'Batyr (Kazakh hero warrior) lizard'.
Batyrosaurus.description: Batyrosaurus is an extinct genus of herbivorous basal hadrosauroid dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous Bostobe Formation (Santonian to Campanian stage) of central Kazakhstan. It contains a single species, Batyrosaurus rozhdestvenskyi. It is possible that Batyrosaurus represents the same taxon as the doubtful Arstanosaurus akkurganensis as both were found from the same formation.

Lateral side of rostral process of jugal bearing a deep horizontal sulcus below the lacrimal facet.
Glenoid surface of surangular perforated by a foramen.

Baurutitan.etymology: From Bauru (the Bauru Group, the geological unit in Brazil where fossils were found) + Greek Titan meaning 'giant'; overall meaning 'Bauru giant'. No explicit etymology provided in the article.
Baurutitan.description: Baurutitan is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Brazil. The type species, Baurutitan britoi, was described in 2005 by Kellner and colleagues, although the fossil remains had already been discovered in 1957. Baurutitan is classified as a lithostrotian titanosaur, and is distinguished from related genera based on its distinctive caudal vertebrae. This South American dinosaur was found in the Serra da Galga Formation near Uberaba, in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais.

Bayannurosaurus.etymology: Named for the Bayin-Gobi (Bayannur) region of China where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Bayannurosaurus.description: Bayannurosaurus is a non-hadrosauriform ankylopollexian ornithopod described in 2018 by Xu Xing. It lived during the early Aptian period, being found in the Bayin-Gobi Formation of China. The genus includes the type species Bayannurosaurus perfectus. A phylogenetic analysis of Bayannurosaurus indicates that it is more derived than Hypselospinus, yet less derived than Ouranosaurus and just outside of the Hadrosauriformes. It was a large iguanodontian, measuring up to 9 meters (30 ft) in total body length. The genus name Bayannurosaurus comes from Bayannur, the area where it was found, while the species name perfectus comes from the "perfect" preservation of the holotype specimen (IMMNH PV00001).

Markedly bifurcated anterior maxilla with an elevated anterodorsal process
Denticulate anteromedial premaxillary oral margin with a shallow peripheral groove

Beg.etymology: Named after Beg-tse, a Himalayan deity and god of war in Mongolian culture, whose rugose appearance echoes the preserved skull.
Beg.description: Beg is a genus of neoceratopsian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Ulaanoosh Formation of Mongolia. The type and only species is Beg tse, described in 2020.
diagnostic_features: 'L-shaped' lacrimal with anterior and posterior rami of nearly equal length, unlike other basal neoceratopsians that lack the anterior ramus.
Small foramen on medial surface of anterior third of jugal anterior ramus, near contact with maxilla.
Premaxilla with four enlarged cylindrical premaxillary teeth, unique among ceratopsians (others have three or fewer).
Five equally spaced tubercles on lateral surface of surangular lateral ridge, not observed in any other ceratopsian or dinosaur.
Large deep pit (groove) on ventral exposure of jugal, opening anteriorly at posterior corner of antorbital fossa, absent in other ceratopsians.

Beibeilong.etymology: From Mandarin Chinese beibei (贝贝) meaning 'baby' and long (龙) meaning 'dragon'. Full meaning: 'baby dragon'.
Beibeilong.description: Beibeilong is a genus of large caenagnathid dinosaurs that lived in China during the Late Cretaceous epoch, about 96 million to 88 million years ago. The genus contains a single species, Beibeilong sinensis. The species was named and described in 2017 through analysis of an embryonic skeleton (nicknamed Baby Louie) and partial nest with large eggs that were discovered in the Gaogou Formation of China (Henan Province) between 1992 and 1993.

Beipiaognathus.description: Beipiaognathus is a dubious genus of coelurosaurian theropod from the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China. The type species is Beipiaognathus jii and it was named and described by Hu et al. in 2016.
diagnostic_features: Teeth are conical-like and un-serrated (lacking serrations on posterior carinae unlike other compsognathids)
Forelimb relatively long with forelimb/hindlimb ratio of 55%, highest among compsognathids, due to relatively long ulna (femur/ulna = 1.09)
Metacarpal I short and rectangular-shaped, about 24% the length of metacarpal II (distinctly shorter than in other Chinese compsognathids)
Phalanx II-1 is the most robust and longest manual phalanx, wider than the radius (unique among reported compsognathids)
Pedal digit III is longest, followed by digit IV then digit II (digit II shorter than digit IV, unlike Huaxiagnathus and Sinocalliopteryx)
Tail relatively short with no more than 40 caudal vertebrae (fewer than Sinosauropteryx with 64 and Sinocalliopteryx with 49)

Beipiaosaurus.etymology: Named for Beipiao City in Liaoning Province, China, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Beipiaosaurus.description: Beipiaosaurus is a genus of therizinosauroid theropod dinosaurs that lived in China during the Early Cretaceous in the Yixian Formation. The first remains were found in 1996 and formally described in 1999. Before the discovery of Yutyrannus, Beipiaosaurus were among the heaviest dinosaurs known from direct evidence to be feathered. Beipiaosaurus is known from three reported specimens. Numerous impressions of feather structures were preserved that allowed researchers to determine the feathering color which turned out to be brownish.

Shallow anterior iliac process
Long manus approximately 10% longer than the femur
Elongated lateral articular surface on the palmar side of manual phalanx I-1
Proximally compressed metatarsals III and IV

Berberosaurus.etymology: From Berber (referring to the Berber people of Morocco, near where the fossils were found) + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'Berber lizard'.
Berberosaurus.description: Berberosaurus is a genus of neotheropod dinosaur, possibly a ceratosaur, from the Toarcian-age (Lower Jurassic) "Toundoute Continental Series" (Azilal Formation) found in the Central High Atlas of Toundoute, Ouarzazate, Morocco. The type species of the genus Berberosaurus is B. liassicus, in reference to the Lias epoch. Berberosaurus might be the oldest known ceratosaur, and is based on partial postcranial remains. This genus represents the oldest formally identified theropod from the North of Africa, as well one of the few from the region in the Early Jurassic.

Femoral anterior trochanter reaches proximally to mid-point of femoral head with large femoral trochanteric shelf
Oblique ridge that proximally caps the medial sulcus of the fibula; tibia with subtriangular distal profile

Bicharracosaurus.description: Bicharracosaurus is a genus of macronarian sauropod dinosaur, possibly a brachiosaurid, that existed during the Late Jurassic of Cañadón Calcáreo Formation in what is now Argentina. The genus is monotypic with the type species being Bicharracosaurus dionidei.

Bistahieversor.etymology: From Bistahi (the Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness area in New Mexico, where fossils were found; from Navajo bistahi meaning 'among the adobe formations') + Latin eversor meaning 'destroyer'; overall meaning 'Bistahi destroyer'.
Bistahieversor.description: Bistahieversor, also known as the "Bisti Beast", is a genus of basal eutyrannosaurian theropod dinosaur. The genus contains only a single known species, B. sealeyi, described in 2010, from the Late Cretaceous of New Mexico. The holotype and a juvenile were found in the Hunter Wash Member of the Kirtland Formation, while other specimens came from the underlying Fossil Forest member of the Fruitland Formation. This dates Bistahieversor approximately 75.5 to 74.5 million years ago during the Campanian age, found in sediments spanning a million years.

Bisticeratops.etymology: From Bisti (the Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness area in New Mexico, where fossils were found; from Navajo bistahi meaning 'among the adobe formations') + Greek keras (κέρας) meaning 'horn' + ops (ὤψ) meaning 'face'; overall meaning 'Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness horned face'.
Bisticeratops.description: Bisticeratops is a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsian from outcrops of the Campanian age Kirtland Formation found in the Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness in northwestern New Mexico, United States. The type and only species is B. froeseorum, known from a nearly complete skull.
diagnostic_features: Snout in lateral view has a characteristic stepped margin (absent in Pentaceratops sternbergi).
Premaxilla with deeply inserted narrow sulcus located between the base of the triangular process and the posteroventral process.

Posterior end of the posteroventral process of the premaxilla with two distinct projections separated by a deep notch; dorsal projection narrow and peg-like, ventral projection transversely expanded and flange-like.
Maxilla with a strongly reduced jugal process and absence of pocket-like fossa between the ventral jugal process on the lateral surface.
Maxilla with two small antorbital fenestrae and lateral surface bearing two elongated, low ridges paralleling each other beneath the antorbital fenestra.
Postorbital horncore strongly anteriorly-curved.

It is known from a partial skull and skeleton found in late Maastrichtian-age rocks of Spain. The type species is Blasisaurus canudoi, described in 2010 by Penélope Cruzado-Caballero, Xabier Pereda-Suberbiola and José Ignacio Ruiz-Omeñaca, a group of researchers from Spain.

Blikanasaurus.etymology: Named for the Blikana locality in South Africa where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', meaning 'lizard from Blikana'.
Blikanasaurus.description: Blikanasaurus is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur from the late Triassic of South Africa. The generic name Blikanasaurus is derived from Greek, meaning "lizard from Blikana". The species name cromptoni is taken from the surname of A.W. "Fuzz" Crompton, an American paleontologist who led numerous field expeditions in Elliot Formation outcrop localities in South Africa. Blikanasaurus is only known from partial hindlimb bones that were recovered from the lower Elliot Formation (LEF) in the Eastern Cape.

Two distal tarsals medially placed between astragalus and metatarsals I-III, with reduced calcaneum contacting metatarsal IV
Metatarsal II and III uniquely massive in lateral/medial view; metatarsal V much reduced with marked distal taper

Bonapartenykus.etymology: Named after José F. Bonaparte, the prominent Argentine paleontologist, combined with Greek onyx/onykhos (ὄνυξ/ὄνυχος) meaning 'claw'; overall meaning 'José F. Bonaparte's claw'.
Bonapartenykus.description: Bonapartenykus is an extinct genus of alvarezsauroid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian-Maastrichtian) of what is now the Allen Formation of the Río Negro Province, Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Bonapartenykus ultimus, known from a partially articulated, incomplete skeleton that was found in close association to two incomplete eggs and several clusters of eggshells belonging to the oogenus Arriagadoolithus. Bonapartenykus was named in 2012. It has an estimated length of 2.5-3.3 m (8.2-10.8 ft) and weight of 43-72 kg (95-159 lb), making it the largest member of the clade Alvarezsauroidea. Additional skeletons referrable to this genus have subsequently been described.

Ventral portion of coracoid strongly medially deflected and decorated with delicate but profuse grooves

Scapula with a very wide notch on the posterior margin of the bone
Ilium and pubis fused

Bonitasaura.etymology: Named after the La Bonita fossil quarry in Argentina where remains were found, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'La Bonita lizard'.
Bonitasaura.description: Bonitasaura is a genus of titanosaurian dinosaur hailing from uppermost layers of the Late Cretaceous (Santonian) Bajo de la Carpa Formation, Neuquén Group of the eastern Neuquén Basin, located in Río Negro Province, Northwestern Patagonia, Argentina. Borealopelta.etymology: From Greek boreas meaning 'northern/north wind' and Greek pelta meaning 'shield'. Full meaning: 'northern shield', referring to its armored body and Canadian (northern) origin.
Borealopelta.description: Borealopelta is an extinct genus of herbivorous nodosaurid ankylosaur from the Lower Cretaceous of what is today Alberta, Canada. It contains a single species, B. markmitchelli, named in 2017 by Caleb Brown and colleagues from a well-preserved specimen known as the Suncor nodosaur. Discovered at an oil sands mine north of Fort McMurray, Alberta, the specimen is remarkable for being among the best-preserved dinosaur fossils of its size ever found. It preserved not only the armor (osteoderms) in their life positions, but also remains of their keratin sheaths, overlying skin, and stomach contents from the animal's last meal. Melanosomes were also found that indicate the animal had a reddish pinkish skin tone.

Borogovia.description: Borogovia is a troodontid theropod dinosaur genus which lived during the Late Cretaceous Period, in what is now Mongolia. It contains one species, Borogovia gracilicrus.

Phalanx II-2 extremely short, only about one-third the length of phalanx II-1
Third toe markedly thinner and more slender than both the second and fourth toes
Tibiotarsus exceptionally long and slender relative to pes size, exceeding proportions of all other known troodontids

Bothriospondylus.etymology: From Greek bothrion ("trench" or "pit") and spondylos ("vertebra"); meaning "trench vertebra", referring to the deep lateral excavations (pleurocoels) of the vertebral centra.
Bothriospondylus.description: Bothriospondylus is a dubious genus of possibly neosauropodan sauropod dinosaur. It lived during the Late Jurassic in England and the type (and only) species is B. suffossus.
diagnostic_features: Sacral vertebral centra strongly horizontally flattened (depressed), not due to posthumous pressure
Deep elongated lateral fossae on centrum sides, continuing from sacral into dorso-lumbar vertebrae and undermining the neural arch support plates
Pre- and post-parapophyses present on each side of sacral centra, with expanded rough syndesmotic articular surfaces
Dorso-lumbar (trunk) vertebrae opisthocoelan (fore end feebly convex, hind end concave), lacking transverse processes
Centrum substance highly cancellous (large unossified lacunae); neurapophyses anchylosed to centrum

Brachiosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'brachion' (arm) and 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'arm lizard', referring to its proportionally long forelimbs (the humerus is longer than the femur).
Brachiosaurus.description: Brachiosaurus is the type genus of Brachiosauridae and the iconic giraffe-postured Late Jurassic North American sauropod. The single valid species, Brachiosaurus altithorax, was erected by Elmer S. Riggs in 1903 on a partial postcranial skeleton (FMNH P 25107) from Riggs Quarry No. 13 in the Grand River valley near Grand Junction, Colorado, on the basis of forelimbs longer than hindlimbs and an unusually deep thorax. For nearly a century the African Tendaguru material described by Janensch (1914) as 'Brachiosaurus brancai' was treated as a second species, but Taylor (2009) formally separated it as Giraffatitan brancai on the basis of at least 26 osteological differences across the dorsal vertebrae, caudals, coracoids, humeri, ilia, and femora; the holotype itself is now understood to represent a subadult individual (the coracoid is unfused to the scapula). The Felch Quarry skull (USNM 5730) is tentatively retained in the hypodigm but cannot be confirmed without overlapping material with the holotype. Subsequent splits have separated additional brachiosaurid material into Lusotitan (Portugal) and Vouivria (France), leaving Brachiosaurus monospecific and restricted to the Morrison Formation of the western United States.
diagnostic_features: Humerus longer than femur, producing the distinctive giraffe-like upward- sloping body posture.
Posterior dorsal centra subcircular in cross-section; postspinal lamina absent from the dorsal vertebrae.
Posterior dorsal neural spines triangular in lateral view and progressively expand mediolaterally to a petal- or paddle-shaped distal end.
Spinodiapophyseal and spinopostzygapophyseal laminae of middle and posterior dorsal vertebrae contact each other.
Anterior caudal vertebrae bear hyposphenes, have transversely widened neural spines, and lack lateral fossae.
Coracoid elongate along the scapular-suture axis with a glenoid surface directed laterally and mediolaterally broad on a thick buttress.
Tubercle on the dorsal margin of the postacetabular lobe of the ilium.
Femur with tibial and fibular condyles equal in width, fourth trochanter extending to mid-shaft height, and a straight lateral shaft margin.

species.name: Brachiosaurus altithorax
species.etymology: From Latin 'altus' (deep) and Greek 'thorax' (chest), referring to the unusually deep thoracic cavity.

holotype.material: Partial postcranial skeleton of a subadult individual comprising the last seven dorsal vertebrae, the sacrum, the first two caudal vertebrae, the right humerus, ilium, and femur, the left coracoid, fragments of the left ilium, and dorsal ribs.

Brachyceratops.etymology: From Greek brachys (βραχύς) meaning 'short', Greek keras (κέρας) meaning 'horn', and Greek ops (ὤψ) meaning 'face'. Full meaning: 'short horned face'.
Brachyceratops.description: Brachyceratops is a dubious genus of ceratopsian dinosaur from the late Cretaceous Period of Montana, United States. Brachyceratops has historically been known from juvenile remains, with one specimen having since been re-classified as Rubeosaurus ovatus.
diagnostic_features: Nasal horn core divided longitudinally by median suture, representing outgrowth from nasal bones rather than separate ossification center
Facial portion of skull greatly abbreviated (shortened) and deep vertically compared with other ceratopsians
Frill fenestrae of comparatively small size and situated entirely within the median (interparietal) element
Frill margin scalloped with series of prominences but without separate marginal ossifications (no epoccipital bones)
Supraorbital (postorbital) horn cores small, with antero-posterior diameter greatly exceeding transverse diameter
Dentition greatly reduced relative to Triceratops, with only about 20 maxillary alveoli versus 40 in Triceratops

species.name: Brachyceratops montanensis
species.etymology: Named for the provenance of the holotype from Montana, United States.

holotype.institution: National Museum of Natural History, Smithsonian Institution
holotype.material: Disarticulated skull (nasals, prefrontals, postfrontals, postorbitals, premaxillaries, maxillaries, alisphenoid) with provisionally associated fragmentary frill, right dentary, and predentary

Brachylophosaurus.etymology: From Greek brachys meaning 'short', Greek lophos meaning 'crest', and Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'short-crested lizard', referring to its reduced flat crest.
Brachylophosaurus.description: Brachylophosaurus is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period of western North America. It was first named in 1953 by Charles Mortram Sternberg for a skull and skeleton he discovered in 1936 in the Oldman Formation of Alberta, Canada, for which he named the new taxon Brachylophosaurus canadensis. While this single specimen was the only known material of Brachylophosaurus for a long time, extensive discoveries in the Judith River Formation of Montana, USA have uncovered not only additional skulls and skeletons with extensive impressions of skin, but also a bonebed of 800 specimens. The earliest of these discoveries in Montana was named Brachylophosaurus goodwini by John R. Horner, but it is now believed that there was only a single species of Brachylophosaurus, with B. goodwini as either a junior synonym of B. canadensis or an indeterminate member of Brachylophosaurini.
diagnostic_features: Nasals extend back over the frontals as a broad, flat, Saurolophus-like crest overhanging the parietals
Broad upper beak subrectangular and down-turned anteriorly, the anterior edge not reflected
Forearm greatly elongated, with the radius (650 mm) and ulna (725 mm) longer than the humerus (590 mm) - unusual among flat-headed hadrosaurs
Maxilla relatively high in front, with a long anterior maxillary process fitting into a groove in the premaxilla
Vertical tooth rows more numerous in the maxilla (about 49) than in the dentary (about 39)
Premaxillary upper limbs nearly erect, giving a higher snout than in other hadrosaurs; lateral temporal fossa about three times as high as wide

species.name: Brachylophosaurus canadensis
species.etymology: Named for Canada, where the holotype specimen was discovered in the Oldman Formation of Alberta.

holotype.material: Skull, cervical and anterior dorsal vertebrae and ribs, scapulae, coracoids, humeri, left ulna, and radius

species.authors: Sternberg, C. M.

Brachytrachelopan.etymology: From Greek 'brachys' meaning 'short', 'trachelos' meaning 'neck', and 'pan' referencing the god Pan, a homage to the short-necked sauropod and the pastoral deity.
Brachytrachelopan.description: Brachytrachelopan is a genus of short-necked sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian to Tithonian) of Argentina. The holotype and only known specimen (Museo Paleontológico Egidio Feruglio MPEF-PV 1716) was collected from an erosional exposure of fluvial sandstone within the Cañadón Calcáreo Formation on a hill approximately 25 kilometers (16 mi) north-northeast of Cerro Cóndor, Chubut Province, in west-central Argentina, South America. Though very incomplete, the skeletal elements recovered were found in articulation and include eight cervical, twelve dorsal, and three sacral vertebrae, as well as proximal portions of the posterior cervical ribs and all the dorsal ribs, the distal end of the left femur, the proximal end of the left tibia, and the right ilium. Much of the specimen was probably lost to erosion many years before its discovery. The type species is Brachytrachelopan mesai. The specific name honors Daniel Mesa, a local shepherd who discovered the specimen while searching for lost sheep. The genus name translates as "short-necked Pan", Pan being the god of the shepherds.
diagnostic_features: Very short neck, with individual cervical vertebrae as long as, or shorter in anteroposterior length than, high posteriorly.
Pronounced, pillarlike centropostzygapophyseal lamina in the cervical vertebrae.
Pronounced anterior inclination of the mid-cervical neural spines, with the tip of the spine extending beyond the anterior end of the centrum.
Anterior dorsal neural spines one to six with vertical bases and anteriorly flexed tips.

species.name: Brachytrachelopan mesai
species.etymology: Named for Daniel Mesa, a local shepherd who discovered the specimen while searching for lost sheep.

holotype.material: Articulated partial skeleton including 8 cervical, 12 dorsal, and 3 sacral vertebrae, proximal parts of posterior cervical and all dorsal ribs, right ilium, distal part of left femur, and proximal end of left tibia.

Bradycneme.description: Bradycneme is a genus of theropod dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous-aged (Maastrichtian) Sânpetru Formation of the Hațeg Basin, Transylvania, Romania. The type species is Bradycneme draculae, known only from a partial right lower leg (specimen BMNH A1588), which its original describers believed it came from a giant owl.

Distal projection of external condyle beyond internal condyle very marked.
Internal and external condyles projecting anteriorly to same extent; projection of internal condyle also directed internally to some extent.
Anterior intercondylar fossa transverse and deep.
Well-developed groove on external side terminating at large external ligamental prominence, proximally situated on external surface of external condyle.

Brasilotitan.description: Brasilotitan is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (early Maastrichtian) Adamantina Formation of Brazil. The type species is Brasilotitan nemophagus. Brasilotitan was a small titanosaur with a squared-off snout, and may be closely related to another Brazilian titanosaur, Uberabatitan.

Bravasaurus.description: Bravasaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Ciénaga del Río Huaco Formation of La Rioja, Argentina. It contains one species, Bravasaurus arreirosorum.

Nasals constricted behind epinasal forming hourglass shape in dorsal view, with very shallow dorsoventral depth of nasal bridge
Bifurcated squamosal process on quadratojugal, such that quadratojugal contributes to ventral rim of laterotemporal fenestra

Brohisaurus.etymology: From the Brohi people of the Kirthar Range area of Balochistan and Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "Brohi lizard".
Brohisaurus.description: Brohisaurus is a problematic sauropod erected by Malkani (2003) on highly fragmentary, weathered, ferruginous-replaced remains (femoral shaft fragments, a proximal fibula, broken metapodials and ribs, and possible neural-arch laminae) from the Sembar Formation of the Kirthar Range, Balochistan, Pakistan. Malkani himself described the names as "purely tentative" and the material lacks unambiguous diagnostic features. Brohisaurus is generally regarded as a nomen dubium. A 2025 paper proposing an ankylosaurian reinterpretation appeared in a predatory-publisher venue and has not achieved community consensus; it is not adopted here.
diagnostic_features: Femoral shaft cross-section markedly elliptical (about 12 by 6 cm in the holotype suite).
Proximal fibula with a well-developed proximal scar; possible pneumatic cavities in the anterior ribs.

Brontomerus.etymology: From Greek bronte meaning 'thunder' and Greek meros meaning 'thigh'. Full meaning: 'thunder thigh', referring to its enormously muscled thighs.
Brontomerus.description: Brontomerus is a genus of camarasauromorph sauropod which lived during the early Cretaceous (Aptian or Albian age, approximately 110 million years ago). It was named in 2011 and the type species is Brontomerus mcintoshi. It is probably a fairly basal camarasauromorph, though the taxon is difficult to resolve due to incompleteness of the material. It is most remarkable for its unusual hipbones, which would have supported the largest thigh muscles, proportionally, of any known sauropod. The specific name is in honor of physicist and North American sauropod expert John Stanton McIntosh.

Preacetabular lobe directed anterolaterally at 30° to the sagittal, but straight in dorsal view and vertically oriented.
Postacetabular lobe reduced to near absence.
Ischiadic peduncle reduced to a very low bulge.
Ilium proportionally taller than in any other sauropod, 52% as high as long.

Brontosaurus.etymology: From Greek bronte (βροντή) meaning 'thunder' and Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'thunder lizard'.
Brontosaurus.description: Brontosaurus is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur that lived in present-day United States during the Late Jurassic period. It was described by American paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh in 1879, the type species being dubbed B. excelsus, based on a partial skeleton lacking a skull found in Como Bluff, Wyoming. In subsequent years, two more species of Brontosaurus were named: B. parvus in 1902 and B. yahnahpin in 1994. Brontosaurus lived about 156 to 146 million years ago (mya) during the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian ages in the Morrison Formation of what is now Utah and Wyoming. For decades, the animal was thought to have been a taxonomic synonym of its close relative Apatosaurus, but a 2015 study by Emmanuel Tschopp and colleagues found it to be distinct. It has seen widespread representation in popular culture, being the archetypal "long-necked" dinosaur in general media.

Sacrum comparatively light due to extensive cavities in the vertebrae with very thin walls
Lumbar vertebrae with constricted centra containing large cavities
Caudal vertebrae nearly or quite solid

Brontotholus.etymology: From Greek 'brontē' (thunder) and 'tholos' (dome); in homage to the 1985 film Mad Max Beyond Thunderdome and the paratype locality name Beyond Thunder Dome.
Brontotholus.description: Brontotholus is an extinct genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian stage) Two Medicine and Oldman formations of Montana, United States, and Alberta, Canada, respectively. The genus contains a single species, Brontotholus harmoni, known from multiple partial domes.

Bruhathkayosaurus.etymology: From Sanskrit bruhath (बृहत्) meaning 'huge, great' + kaya (काय) meaning 'body' + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'huge-bodied lizard'.
Bruhathkayosaurus.description: Bruhathkayosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur found in the Kallamedu Formation of India. The fragmentary remains were originally described as a theropod, but it was later determined to be a titanosaur sauropod. Length estimates by researchers exceed those of the titanosaur Argentinosaurus, as longer than 35 meters (115 ft) and weighing over 80 tonnes. A 2023 estimate placed Bruhathkayosaurus as potentially weighing 110-170 tonnes (110-170 long tons; 120-190 short tons), with paleontologist Michael Benton, estimating a length of 45 meters (148 ft). If the upper estimates of the 2023 records are accurate, Bruhathkayosaurus may have rivaled the blue whale as one of the largest animals to ever exist. However, all of the estimates are based on the dimensions of the fossils described in 1987, but these fossils have since disintegrated and no longer exist, making it impossible to affirm these estimates.
diagnostic_features: Gigantic body size with heavy, robust limb bones
Large tibia, measuring 2000 mm in length and 380 mm in shaft width, larger than that of any carnivorous dinosaur known at the time of description
Large ilium with a heavy, posteriorly massive puboischial peduncle
Ilial plate broad posteriorly (130 mm) and narrow anteriorly (100 mm), with prominent muscular attachment depressions on the dorsal surface

Burianosaurus.etymology: Named in honor of Czech palaeoartist Zdeněk Burian, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Burianosaurus.description: Burianosaurus is an extinct genus of ornithopod dinosaur that lived during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous period in what is now the Czech Republic, being the first validly named dinosaur from that country. The type species, B. augustai, was named in 2017; the genus name honors the Czech palaeoartist Zdeněk Burian, and the species name honors the Czech paleontologist Josef Augusta. The holotype specimen is a femur discovered in sediments belonging to the Peruc-Korycany Formation in 2003, which was described as possibly belonging to an iguanodont in 2005.

In medial view the distal condyles do not extend the shaft anteriorly

Buriolestes.description: Buriolestes is a genus of early sauropodomorph dinosaurs from the Late Triassic Santa Maria Formation of the Paraná Basin in southern Brazil. Calamosaurus.etymology: From Greek kalamos (κάλαμος) meaning 'reed' + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'reed lizard', likely referring to the slender, hollow vertebrae.
Calamosaurus.description: Calamosaurus is a genus of small theropod dinosaur, from the Early Cretaceous of the Isle of Wight, England. It is based on two cervical vertebrae (NHMUK PV R 901), collected by Reverend William Fox. These fossils come from sedimentary rocks of the Wessex Formation and are Barremian in age. The type species of Calamosaurus, named Calamospondylus foxi by Richard Lydekker, was named in honor of Fox. Calamospondylus, however, was a preoccupied name, forcing Lydekker to change the genus name to Calamosaurus. This has subsequently led to immense confusion, with some authors believing the two genera to be synonymous. The systematic position of Calamosaurus within theropods has been controversial, and placements within Compsognathidae and Ornithomimosauria have been suggested. More recently, researchers have suggested affinities with the Tyrannosauroidea and Alvarezsauroidea.
diagnostic_features: Cervical vertebrae shorter than those of Coelurus (C. daviesi)
All cervicals probably opisthocœlous (vs. amphicœlous middle and posterior cervicals in Coelurus)
Cervical vertebrae with pneumatic foramina, indicating highly pneumatic skeleton
Characteristic brown coloration distinguishing them from black-stained Coelurus daviesi and Aristosuchus pusillus types

Calamospondylus.etymology: From Greek kalamos (reed) and spondylos (vertebra), in reference to the hollow, reed-like nature of the vertebrae.
Calamospondylus.description: Calamospondylus is a dubious genus of theropod dinosaur. It lived during the Early Cretaceous and its fossils were found on the Isle of Wight in southern England. The type species is C. oweni, named in 1866 in an anonymous publication written largely by its discoverer, the Reverend William Fox. The description given by Fox was brief and listed no unique diagnostic characteristics; between this and the fact that the specimen has been lost, C. oweni is now considered a nomen dubium. The presence of expansive hollows in the bone led Fox to speculate that it was arboreal, leaping from tree to tree, or alternatively that it was a hopping animal.
diagnostic_features: Vertebrae hollow, smooth, and compact like a reed (hollow neural canal giving the genus its name)
Bones more hollow, light, and compact in structure than bird bones, comparable to pterodactyl bones
Foramina for admission of air into the bones, analogous to pneumatized pterodactyl bones
Small body size relative to contemporary Wealden dinosaurs (sacrum only six inches long)

species.name: Calamospondylus oweni
species.etymology: Named in honor of Sir Richard Owen, who examined the holotype.

The genus contains a single species, Calvarius rapidus, known from a single metatarsal. The slender morphology of this bone may indicate Calvarius had a cursorial (adapted to run) ecology, in contrast to its slower-moving relatives.

Camarasaurus.etymology: From Greek kamara (καμάρα) meaning 'vaulted chamber' or 'anything with an arched cover' + Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'; overall meaning 'chambered lizard', referring to the hollow pleurocoels in its cervical vertebrae.
Camarasaurus.description: Camarasaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic in what is now the United States. Its fossils are primarily known from the Morrison Formation dating to the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian ages of the Jurassic, between 155 and 145 million years ago (mya). It was named by Edward Drinker Cope in 1877; it definitively contains three species, C. supremus, the type species, C. grandis, and C. lentus, while some researchers consider C. lewisi to be in its own genus, Cathetosaurus. The generic name means "chambered lizard", referring to the hollow chambers, known as pleurocoels, in its cervical vertebrae (Greek καμαρα [kamara] meaning 'vaulted chamber', or anything with an arched cover, and σαυρος [sauros] meaning 'lizard'). Hundreds of specimens have been excavated to date, including some nearly complete skeletons. It is among the best understood dinosaurs, with detailed studies of its anatomy, paleobiology, paleoecology, and more.
diagnostic_features: Dorsal vertebral centra hollow with two large internal chambers separated by a thin longitudinal median septum, communicating with exterior via a large lateral foramen below the diapophysis base.
Neural arches extraordinarily elevated with neural spines set transversely to the vertebral axis; spine of anterior dorsal strongly emarginate/bifurcate.
Cervical centra very elongate, exceeding proportions known in other Dinosauria and Crocodilia, with a deep linear lateral foramen running most of the centrum length.
Anterior zygapophyses of neural arches separated by a deep median fissure; posterior zygapophyses united, bearing a pendant hyposphen that locks into the anterior fissure of the succeeding vertebra.
Scapula relatively very large (1.517 m long) with a prominent mesoscapular process absent in Cetiosaurus; sacrum short, only four coossified centra.
Caudal vertebrae amphicoelous and lacking the lateral pneumatic fossae present in dorsal centra; composed of finely spongy rather than hollow bone.

Camelotia.etymology: Named after Camelot, the legendary castle and court of King Arthur, referring to the discovery location in southwest England (near the supposed location of Camelot); overall meaning 'from Camelot'.
Camelotia.description: Camelotia is a large-bodied sauropodomorph from the latest Triassic (Rhaetian) of southwest England. It is best known from a partial postcranial skeleton found in the Westbury Formation and named by Peter M. Galton in 1985. Subsequent work has generally placed Camelotia as a relatively derived sauropodomorph close to the origin of Sauropoda, although its exact position among early non-sauropod sauropodomorphs remains debated. It is sometimes placed in Melanorosauridae as a close relative of Melanorosaurus. With a body length and mass estimated at 8-10 meters (26-33 ft) and 3.8 tonnes (8,400 lb), respectively, it is one of the largest sauropodomorphs known from the Triassic.

Carcharodontosaurus.etymology: From Greek Carcharodon (the great white shark genus, itself from Greek karcharos meaning 'jagged/sharp' and odous meaning 'tooth') and Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'shark-toothed lizard'.
Carcharodontosaurus.description: Carcharodontosaurus is a genus of large theropod dinosaur that lived in Northwest Africa from about 100 to 94 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage of the Cretaceous. The taxon was first described in 1925 by French paleontologists Charles Depéret and Justin Savornin as Megalosaurus saharicus, based on two fossil teeth discovered in Algeria, which are now lost. A partial skeleton was discovered in Egypt as early as 1914 by crews of German paleontologist Ernst Stromer, although he did not report the find until 1931. Based on this specimen, together with the teeth previously described by Depéret and Savornin, Stromer established the genus Carcharodontosaurus and its type species (species a genus in named for) C. saharicus. Although the Egyptian skeleton was destroyed during World War II, it was subsequently redescribed as the holotype (name-bearing) specimen of a distinct carcharodontosaurid genus, Tameryraptor. In 1995, a large incomplete skull attributed to C. saharicus was discovered in the Kem Kem Beds of Morocco, which was officially proposed as the neotype (replacement holotype) in 2007. In the same year, fossils unearthed from the Farak Formation of Niger were described and named as another species, C. iguidensis, though this taxon might belong to a different genus.

Carnotaurus.etymology: From Latin caro/carnis meaning 'flesh/meat' and Latin taurus meaning 'bull'. Full meaning: 'meat-eating bull' or 'flesh bull', referring to its bull-like horns and carnivorous diet.
Carnotaurus.description: Carnotaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived in South America during the Late Cretaceous period, between 69 and 66 million years ago. The only species is Carnotaurus sastrei. Known from a single well-preserved skeleton, it is one of the best-understood theropods from the Southern Hemisphere. The skeleton, found in 1984, was uncovered in the Chubut Province of Argentina from rocks of the La Colonia Formation. Carnotaurus is a derived member of the Abelisauridae, a group of large theropods that occupied the large predatorial niche in the southern landmasses of Gondwana during the late Cretaceous. Within the Abelisauridae, the genus is often considered a member of the Brachyrostra, a clade of short-snouted forms restricted to South America.

Cathartesaura.etymology: From Cathartes (the New World vulture genus) + Greek saura ('lizard', feminine). The name also alludes to the turkey vulture Cathartes aura, whose Spanish name 'buitre' named the 'La Buitrera' locality where the fossils were found.
Cathartesaura.description: Cathartesaura is a genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaur from Late Cretaceous strata of the Huincul Formation, at the "La Buitrera" locality, in the Neuquén Basin of Río Negro Province, Argentina. The fossil remains, described by Gallina and Apesteguía in 2005, consist of a partial skeleton including vertebrae and limb bones. These were found at the base of the formation, which dates back to the Cenomanian and Turonian epochs, in mudstone and sandstone levels.
diagnostic_features: Posterior cervical vertebra with accessory lamina (AL2) arising from mid-length of prezygodiapophysial lamina and reaching the centrum
Anterior caudal transverse processes thin and wing-like, mostly supported by ventral bar framing a deep triangular fossa bounded by diapoprezygapophyseal and centroprezygapophyseal laminae
Anterior caudal neural spine lateral lamina formed by junction of spinoprezygapophyseal, lateral spinopostzygapophyseal, and spinodiapophyseal laminae (unique triple junction)

species.name: Cathartesaura anaerobica
species.etymology: Named for the Argentinian adhesive company Anaeróbicos, which provided field and laboratory support during the extraction and preparation of the fossils.

holotype.material: Posterior cervical vertebra, dorsal vertebra, anterior caudal, mid caudal vertebra, left scapula, left ilium, right femur; poorly preserved dorsal vertebra, humerus, and metatarsal also collected.

Caudipteryx.etymology: From Latin cauda ('tail') + Greek pteryx ('feather' or 'wing'), meaning 'tail feather'.
Caudipteryx.description: Caudipteryx is a genus of small oviraptorosaurian dinosaurs that lived in China during the Early Cretaceous, around 124.6 million years ago. They were feathered and extremely bird-like in their overall appearance, to the point that some paleontologists suggested it was a bird. Two species have been described: C. zoui (the type species), in 1998, and C. dongi, in 2000. Caudipteryx had a stout trunk, long legs, and was probably a swift runner. Its discovery has led to many intensive studies and debate over the relationship between birds and dinosaurs.
diagnostic_features: Elongate, hooked premaxillary teeth with broad roots; maxilla and dentary edentulous.
Tail short, comprising approximately 22 vertebrae and equal to about one-quarter of total body length.
Arm long relative to other non-avian theropods; hindlimb-to-forelimb ratio approximately 2.5.
Short manual unguals, less than 70% the length of the penultimate phalanx.
Remiges attached to second digit (second metacarpal, phalanx II-1, and base of phalanx II-2), with symmetrical vanes.

species.name: Caudipteryx zoui
species.etymology: Named for Zou Jiahua for his prominent support to the scientific community as the vice premier of China.

holotype.material: An articulated, largely complete skeleton with skull and a 22-vertebra tail, with remiges on the second digit, tail rectrices, downy body feathers, and gastroliths

Cedarosaurus.etymology: From Cedar (referring to the Cedar Mountain Formation where it was discovered) + Greek sauros ('lizard'), meaning 'Cedar lizard'.
Cedarosaurus.description: Cedarosaurus is a genus of nasal-crested macronarian sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Period (Valanginian). The fossils were discovered in 1996 in eastern Utah within the rocks of the Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation. It was officially named and described by Tidwell, Carpenter and Brooks in 1999. It shows similarities to the brachiosaurid Eucamerotus from the Wessex Formation of southern England, as well as to Brachiosaurus from the Morrison Formation.
diagnostic_features: Anterior caudal vertebrae possess deeply concave anterior faces, lacking the posterior ball of titanosaurs; posterior faces of anterior caudal vertebrae are flat to concave.
Anterior caudal vertebrae lack well-developed hyposphenes (only caudal 8 shows a small hyposphene).
Mid-caudal vertebrae bear a sharp ridge extending axially along the sides of the neural arch.
Deltopectoral crest of humerus placed closer to midshaft than in Brachiosaurus, Pleurocoelus nanus, or SMU 61732; humerus proportionally more robust than Brachiosaurus.
Radius slender with two ridges beginning at midshaft; distal end subrectangular and flat rather than oval as in Pleurocoelus.
Ulna with prominent posterior condyle separated from the lateral wall by a distinct groove, contrasting with Pleurocoelus nanus and SMU 61732.

species.etymology: Named for the late Carol Weiskopf, in recognition of her hard work in the field and laboratory.

Cedarpelta.etymology: Named for the Cedar Mountain Formation of Utah where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'pelta' meaning 'shield', referring to its ankylosaurid armor.
Cedarpelta.description: Cedarpelta is an extinct genus of basal ankylosaurid dinosaur from Utah that lived during the Early Cretaceous period in what is now the Mussentuchit Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation. The type and only species, Cedarpelta bilbeyhallorum, is known from multiple specimens including partial skulls and postcranial material. It was named in 2001 by Kenneth Carpenter, James Kirkland, Don Burge, and John Bird. Cedarpelta has an estimated length of 7 meters (23 feet) and weight of 5 tonnes (11,023 lbs). The skull of Cedarpelta lacks extensive cranial ornamentation and is one of the only known ankylosaurs with individual skull bones that are not completely fused together.
diagnostic_features: Paired premaxillae parallel-sided, not diverging posterolaterally as in other ankylosaurids; six alveoli in premaxilla
Occipital condyle on a long neck projecting horizontally, not obliquely downward as in all other known ankylosaurids and nodosaurids
Pterygoids anteroposteriorly elongated and vaulted; well-developed trochlear-like process along lateral edge of pterygoid
Basitubera as a very large, ventral-projecting wedge (unpaired, unlike paired condition in all other ankylosaurs)
Large oval process for adductor tendon on medial side of coronoid process of surangular
Ischium with large knob on medial side near pubic peduncle

Cedrorestes.etymology: From Latin 'cedrus' meaning 'cedar' and Greek 'oros' meaning 'mountain' (after the Cedar Mountain Formation where the fossil was found), with Greek suffix '-etes' meaning 'dweller'.
Cedrorestes.description: Cedrorestes is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Utah. It is based on an incomplete skeleton which was found in the Valanginian-age Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation.
diagnostic_features: Deep, iguanodontid-like ilium with a prominent lateral process ('antitrochanter') dorsal to the ischial peduncle, a character otherwise diagnostic of Hadrosauridae.
Poorly developed, bosslike ischial peduncle on the ilium.
Preacetabular process of the ilium laterally compressed and slightly deflected ventrally, terminating in a rounded point with a ventrolaterally divergent keel.
Postacetabular process elongated and tapering, with an overhanging lateral process above the postacetabular notch on the dorsolateral border.

Centrosaurus.etymology: From Greek kentron (κέντρον) meaning 'point' and Greek sauros (σαῦρος) meaning 'lizard'. Full meaning: 'pointed lizard', referring to the small hornlets along the margin of its frill.
Centrosaurus.description: Centrosaurus is a genus of centrosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur from the Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous of Canada. Its remains have been found in the Dinosaur Park Formation, dating from 76.5 to 75.5 million years ago. The type and only species seen as valid today is Centrosaurus apertus.
diagnostic_features: Fontanelles of the crest included entirely within the parietal part of the expansion (not bounded laterally by the squamosal)
Posterior border of crest bears a pair of greatly modified hooked epoccipital processes (large hook-like spurs of bone) on the hinder border
Crest broadly expanded laterally, broader than long, with a robust transverse posterior bar that is concave in outline behind
Squamosals confined to the antero-lateral edge of the frill, contributing little to its overall formation
Large oval fontanelles one on either side of the median line, bounded behind by the transverse bar and laterally/anteriorly by thin side extensions

species.etymology: From Latin 'apertio' meaning 'an opening' or 'aperture', referring to the two large, open fenestrae in the frill that distinguish it from other ceratopsians.

Cerasinops.etymology: From Greek kerasos meaning 'cherry' and Greek ops meaning 'face'. Full meaning: 'cherry face', likely referring to the shape or color of its facial features.
Cerasinops.description: Cerasinops was a small ceratopsian dinosaur. It lived during the Campanian of the late Cretaceous Period. Its fossils have been found in Two Medicine Formation, in Montana. The type species of the genus Cerasinops is C. hodgskissi.
diagnostic_features: Prootic extends further caudodorsally on the paroccipital process than in either Protoceratops or Montanoceratops.
Horizontal jugal crest oriented at ninety degrees from the main dorsoventral jugal crest, unique among basal neoceratopsians.
Extremely robust surangular with a thick buttress of bone at the contact with the coronoid process of the dentary.
Pronounced medial bend of the distal ulna, more extreme than in other North American basal neoceratopsians.
Forelimb to hindlimb ratio of 0.60, lower than in any other basal neoceratopsian.
Forelimb bones have longitudinal vascular canal structure in cortical bone, contrasting with the circumferential pattern in the hindlimb elements of the same individual.

Ceratonykus.etymology: From Greek keras/keratos ('horn') + onyx/nykos ('claw'), meaning 'horned claw'.
Ceratonykus.description: Ceratonykus is a monospecific genus of alvarezsaurid dinosaur from Mongolia that lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) in what is now the Barun Goyot Formation. The type and only species, Ceratonykus oculatus, is known from a fragmentary skeleton, including an incomplete skull, of an adult individual. It was named and described in 2009 by Vladimir Alifanov and Rinchen Barsbold. Its describers questioned the traditional placement of alvarezsaurs in Theropoda, instead suggesting they were ornithischians, but this has not been accepted since. Ceratonykus has an estimated length of 75 centimeters (2.46 feet) and weight of 760 grams (1.68 pounds). It has been considered as a possible junior synonym of Parvicursor.
diagnostic_features: Femora strongly curved and nearly half as long as tibiotarsus (shorter than in all other parvicursorids)
Tarsometatarsals 3.5 times as long as third metatarsals (third metatarsals more reduced than in other parvicursorids)
Carpometacarpus bears spikelike bones (interpreted as possible ungual phalanges of additional digits)
Natural endocast lacks vertical flexure at brain floor; optic lobes displaced ventrally; acoustic tubercles unusually wide
Deep proximodorsal notch between second and fourth metatarsals; dorsal and palmar surfaces of these bones ridgelike with deep grooves between them
Frontals each nearly four times as long as wide; narrowing rostrally into a narrow wedge; prefrontals adjoining each other medially

species.etymology: From Latin word meaning 'sharp-sighted' or 'big-eyed', in reference to the large orbits of the skull.
