Lucianovenator.etymology: Named for Don Luciano Leyes, who first reported the fossil remains, combined with Latin 'venator' meaning 'hunter'.
Lucianovenator.description: Lucianovenator is an extinct genus of coelophysid theropod dinosaur which lived in Argentina during the Triassic. The genus name Lucianovenator translates to "Luciano's hunter", in reference to Don Luciano Leyes, who first reported the remains. The species name bonoi refers to Tulio del Bono, a local scientific authority who collaborated on the describers' research. It is one of the few neotheropods known from South America.
diagnostic_features: Cervical neural arches with three deep fossae: two blind pockets in prezygapophyseal centrodiapophyseal fossa and a third communicating with internal neural cavity in centropostzygapophyseal fossa
Anteroposteriorly elongated fossa on posterior centrodiapophyseal lamina edge progressively deepening and enlarging from C3 to C9
Length of anterior cervical ribs equivalent to five cervical centra
Cervical vertebrae extremely elongated (>3× longer than posterior articular surface height)
Deeply concave posterior articular face of cervical centra

species.name: Lucianovenator bonoi
species.etymology: Named for Tulio del Bono, a local scientific authority in Argentina who collaborated on the research that described this species.

Lufengosaurus.description: Lufengosaurus is a genus of massospondylid dinosaur which lived during the Early Jurassic period in what is now southwestern China.

Skull approximately 3-5 times the length of anterior tail vertebrae
Neck comparatively long
Belongs to Plateosauridae, similar to Plateosaurus grayianus but about one-fourth smaller

Luoyanggia.etymology: Named after Luoyang, a city in Henan Province, China, near the fossil locality; meaning "from Luoyang"
Luoyanggia.description: Luoyanggia is a genus of oviraptorid dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous Haoling Formation of the Ruyang Basin in Henan Province, central China. The type species is L. liudianensis.

Mandibular symphysis V-shaped in dorsal view.
Both mandibular rami bent posterolaterally.
Shaft of ischium slightly concave caudally.
Pubic peduncle of ilium much deeper than ischial peduncle.
Anterior margin of ischial shaft sharply transferred to anterodorsal margin of obturator process.

Lurdusaurus.etymology: From Latin 'lurdus' meaning 'heavy' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', hence 'heavy lizard', in reference to its massive proportions. The species name 'arenatus' is Latin for 'sandy', as it was found in a desert.
Lurdusaurus.description: Lurdusaurus is a genus of massive and unusually shaped iguanodont dinosaur from the Elrhaz Formation in Niger. It contains one species, L. arenatus. The formation dates to the Early Cretaceous, roughly 112 million years ago.
diagnostic_features: Massively proportioned iguanodontid with unusually robust skeletal construction throughout
Cervical centra approximately equal in length to dorsal centra (unlike European species where cervicals are 60-90% of dorsal length)
Radius approximately 54.5% the length of humerus (much shorter than typical iguanodontids)
Metacarpals approximately 17% the length of humerus (short and robust, graviporteur type)
Quadrate extremely short, approximately twice the average length of dorsal centra
Tibia 84.5% the length of femur (very short hindlimb relative to body size)
Forelimbs and hindlimbs short relative to dorsal centrum length (60-70% shorter than in European species)

synonyms.name: Gravisaurus

species.etymology: From Latin 'arenatus' meaning 'sandy', because the holotype was found in a desert environment at the Gadoufaoua site of Niger.

holotype.material: Nearly complete skeleton, missing portions of midsection cranium, sacrum, and much of pes.

Lusotitan.etymology: From 'Luso-' (the Latin term for an inhabitant of Lusitania, i.e., Portugal) combined with Greek 'Titan' (a mythological giant); meaning 'Portuguese titan' or 'Lusitanian titan'
Lusotitan.description: Lusotitan is a genus of herbivorous brachiosaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of Portugal.

Mid-dorsals with very large pleurocoels
Anterior caudals with well-developed transverse processes

Posterior caudal centra with convex anterior face
Mid- and posterior caudal centra wider than high
Slender pelvis with notch at posterodorsal margin of ilium
Postacetabular process of ilium bulky without notch between process and ischial peduncle
Obturator foramen of pubis closed
Distal end of pubis anteroposteriorly expanded
Tibia bowed laterally
Proximal end of fibula angular not rounded

Lusovenator.etymology: From Latin Luso- (Portuguese, referring to Lusitania/Portugal) combined with Latin venator (hunter); meaning "Portuguese hunter"
Lusovenator.description: Lusovenator is a genus of carcharodontosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian) Praia de Amoreira Porto-Novo Member and the Late Jurassic-Early Cretaceous (Tithonian-Berriasian) Assenta Member of the Lourinhã Formation in present-day Portugal. Absence of ventral keel on anterior dorsal vertebrae

Lythronax.etymology: From Greek 'lythron' (λύθρον) meaning 'gore' and 'anax' (ἄναξ) meaning 'king', hence 'gore king'. The species name is from Greek 'argestes' (ἀργεστής), Homer's name for the wind from the southwest, referring to where the specimen was found in North America.
Lythronax.description: Lythronax is a genus of tyrannosaurid dinosaur that lived in North America around 81.9-81.5 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous period. The only known specimen was discovered in Utah in the Wahweap Formation of the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument in 2009, and it consists of a partial skull and skeleton. In 2013, it became the basis of the new genus and species Lythronax argestes; the generic name Lythronax means "gore king", and the specific name argestes originates from the Greek poet Homer's name for the wind from the southwest, in reference to the specimen's geographic provenance in North America.

prefrontal and postorbital contact surfaces on frontal separated only by narrow dorsoventral groove

11 maxillary alveoli (vs 14-16 in other tyrannosaurids)
concave lateral margin of dentary with broad postorbital process of jugal
laterally expanded caudal skull with rostrodorsally directed orbits
large distally expanded pubic boot with anteroposterior length at least 60% of total pubic length
dorsally expanded ascending process of astragalus

Macrogryphosaurus.description: Macrogryphosaurus is a genus of elasmarian dinosaur from the Coniacian age Upper Cretaceous Sierra Barrosa Formation (Neuquén Group) of Argentina in Patagonia. It was described by Jorge Calvo and colleagues in 2007, with M. gondwanicus as the type and only species.

Macrurosaurus.etymology: From Greek makros (large) and oura (tail); meaning "large-tailed lizard"

Magnamanus.etymology: From Latin 'magna' (large) and 'manus' (hand); meaning 'large hand', likely referring to its broad hand morphology
Magnamanus.description: Magnamanus is an extinct genus of herbivorous iguanodontian dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now Spain in the Golmayo Formation. It contains a single species, Magnamanus soriaensis.

Magyarosaurus.etymology: From Hungarian 'Magyar' meaning 'Hungarian' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; named for Hungary, the country that controlled the Transylvanian region where it was found at the time of discovery.
Magyarosaurus.description: Magyarosaurus is a genus of dwarf sauropod dinosaur from late Cretaceous Period (early to late Maastrichtian) in today's Transylvania. It is one of the smallest-known adult sauropods, measuring less than 3 m (9.8 ft) long and weighing less than 1,000 kg (2,200 lb). The type and only species is Magyarosaurus dacus. It has been found to be a close relative of Rapetosaurus in the family Saltasauridae in the sauropod clade Titanosauria in a 2005 study.

Mahakala.etymology: Named after Mahakala, a deity common to Hinduism and Buddhism.
Mahakala.description: Mahakala is a genus of halszkaraptorine theropod dinosaur from the Campanian-age (about 80 million years ago) Upper Cretaceous Djadokhta Formation of Ömnögovi, Mongolia. It is based on a partial skeleton found in the Gobi Desert. Mahakala was a small dromaeosaurid, and its skeleton shows features that are also found in early troodontids and avialans. Despite its late appearance, it is among the most basal dromaeosaurids. Its small size, and the small size of other basal deinonychosaurians, suggests that small size appeared before flight capability in birds.

Maleriraptor.etymology: From the Upper Maleri Formation, where the holotype was collected, and Latin 'raptor' (thief, robber); meaning 'Maleri thief'.
Maleriraptor.description: Maleriraptor is an extinct genus of early-diverging herrerasaurian saurischian dinosaur from the early Norian (Late Triassic) Upper Maleri Formation of the Pranhita-Godavari Valley, Telangana, south-central India. The single species, Maleriraptor kuttyi, is known from a partial pelvis and associated sacral and caudal vertebrae (ISIR 282), originally described by Novas et al. (2010) as indeterminate Dinosauriformes; Ezcurra et al. (2025) re-evaluated the material and recovered it as a herrerasaurian outside the South American Herrerasauridae, filling a stratigraphic gap between Carnian South American herrerasaurids and middle-Norian-to-Rhaetian North American herrerasaurs.

Mamenchisaurus.etymology: Named after Mamenchi (a transliteration of the Chinese place name for a ferry crossing, Maming Creek), where the first fossils were found near Yibin, Sichuan, China, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Mamenchi lizard'
Mamenchisaurus.description: Mamenchisaurus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaurs known for their remarkably long necks, which made up nearly half the total body length. Numerous species have been assigned to the genus; however, the validity of these assignments has been questioned. Fossils have been found in the Sichuan Basin and Yunnan Province in China. Several species from the Upper Shaximiao Formation, whose geologic age is uncertain, have been described. However, evidence suggests this formation to be no earlier than the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic. M. sinocanadorum dates to the Oxfordian stage (161.2 to 158.7 mya), and M. anyuensis to the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous (around 114.4 mya). Most species were medium-large to large sauropods, measuring roughly 15 to 26 meters (49 to 85 ft) in length-possibly up to 35 meters (115 ft), based on two undescribed vertebrae.

Manipulonyx.etymology: From Latin 'manipulare' (to manipulate, to handle) and Greek 'onyx' (claw), referring to the specialized forelimb interpreted as a tool for handling eggs.
Manipulonyx.description: Manipulonyx is an extinct genus of parvicursorine alvarezsaurid theropod from the Maastrichtian Nemegt Formation of the Khermeen Tsav locality, Govi-Altai Province, southern Mongolia. The single species, Manipulonyx reshetovi, is known from a fragmentary skeleton (PIN 3142/364) that preserves the most complete forelimb of any parvicursorine yet described, including the first documented complete set of proximal carpals (ulnare, intermedium, radiale) and a series of dermal carpal spikes (medial, lateral, and palmar) articulated with the carpometacarpus. Averianov, Lopatin and Atuchin (2025) interpret these spikes, together with the rudimentary third and fourth digits and the absence of a flexor tubercle on ungual II-2, as adaptations for gripping and piercing dinosaur eggs with the hypertrophied manual claw — a hypothesis supported by eggshell fragments associated with the holotype on its 1979 field label.

Mantellisaurus.etymology: Named for Gideon Mantell, the English geologist and paleontologist who first described Iguanodon, combined with Greek '-saurus' meaning 'lizard'.
Mantellisaurus.description: Mantellisaurus is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur that lived in the Barremian and early Aptian ages of the Early Cretaceous Period of Europe. Its remains are known from Belgium (Bernissart), England, Spain and Germany. The type and only species is M. atherfieldensis. Formerly known as Iguanodon atherfieldensis, the new genus Mantellisaurus was erected for the species by Gregory Paul in 2007. According to Paul, Mantellisaurus was more lightly built than Iguanodon and more closely related to Ouranosaurus, making Iguanodon in its traditional sense paraphyletic. It is known from many complete and almost complete skeletons. The genus name honors Gideon Mantell, the discoverer of Iguanodon.

Mapusaurus.etymology: From Mapudungun 'mapu' (earth or land) and Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'earth lizard'
Mapusaurus.description: Mapusaurus is a genus of giant carcharodontosaurid carnosaurian dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Cenomanian-Turonian ages of the Late Cretaceous. It is known from a bonebed of between seven and nine specimens, excavated from the strata of the Huincul Formation between 1997 and 2001 as part of the Argentinian-Canadian Dinosaur Project. In 2006, Rodolfo Coria and Philip J. Currie scientifically described Mapusaurus. Only one species of Mapusaurus, M. roseae, has been described, named after the rose-colored rocks in which it was discovered and sponsor Rose Letwin.

Maraapunisaurus.etymology: From Ute 'maraapuni' meaning 'it is very large' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', giving the meaning 'very large lizard', named for the enormous estimated size of the specimen.
Maraapunisaurus.description: Maraapunisaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation of western North America. It contains one species, Maraapunisaurus fragillimus, which was originally named Amphicoelias fragillimus. It has sometimes been estimated to be the largest dinosaur specimen ever discovered. Based on surviving descriptions of a single fossil bone, scientists have produced numerous size estimates over the years; the largest estimate M. fragillimus to have been the longest known animal at 58 meters (190 ft) in length with a mass of 150 tonnes (150 long tons; 170 short tons). However, because the only fossil remains were lost at some point after being studied and described in the 1870s, evidence survived only in contemporary drawings and field notes.

Martharaptor.etymology: Named in honor of Martha C. Hayden, the paleontologist assistant who helped discover the Hayden-Corbett site in the Cedar Mountain Formation of Utah where the specimen was found, combined with Latin 'raptor' meaning 'thief'.
Martharaptor.description: Martharaptor is a genus of therizinosauroid theropod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous of the Cedar Mountain Formation in Utah. They can be distinguished from other therizinosauroids by means of several features of the skeleton (particularly the hands and feet) which were intermediate between early therizinosaurs such as Falcarius and Beipiaosaurus, and more "advanced" members of the group like therizinosaurids. The deep and homogeneous hand claws clearly differ from the case in early therizinosauroids, but the foot has not yet acquired the robust morphology of therizinosaurids.

Masiakasaurus.etymology: From Malagasy 'masiaka' meaning 'vicious' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'vicious lizard'.
Masiakasaurus.description: Masiakasaurus is a genus of small predatory theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous of Madagascar. In Malagasy, masiaka means "vicious"; thus, the genus name means "vicious lizard". The type species, Masiakasaurus knopfleri, was named after the musician Mark Knopfler, whose music inspired the expedition crew. It was named in 2001 by Scott D. Sampson, Matthew Carrano, and Catherine A. Forster. Unlike most theropods, the front teeth of Masiakasaurus projected forwards instead of straight down. This unique dentition suggests that they had a specialized diet, perhaps including fish and other small prey. Other bones of the skeleton indicate that Masiakasaurus were bipedal, with much shorter forelimbs than hindlimbs. It was a small theropod, reaching 1.8-2.1 m (5.9-6.9 ft) long and weighing 20 kg (44 lb). Masiakasaurus lived from 72.1 to 66 million years ago, along with animals such as Majungasaurus, Rapetosaurus, and Rahonavis. Masiakasaurus was a member of the group Noasauridae, small predatory ceratosaurs found primarily in South America.

Massospondylus.etymology: From Greek 'massos' meaning 'longer' and 'spondylos' meaning 'vertebra', referring to what Richard Owen identified as elongated tail vertebrae.
Massospondylus.description: Massospondylus is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Early Jurassic of southern Africa. It was described by Richard Owen in 1854 from remains discovered in South Africa, and is thus one of the first dinosaurs to have been named. The name Massospondylus means 'longer vertebra', alluding to what Owen identified as tail vertebrae; these vertebrae are now known to be from the neck. Although the original fossils were destroyed in London during The Blitz, a plethora of specimens have since been assigned to the genus, making it one of the best-known sauropodomorphs from the Early Jurassic. The genus lived during the Hettangian, Sinemurian, and Pliensbachian ages, which lasted from ca. 201 to 184 million years ago. Most fossils come from the upper Elliot and Clarens formations of South Africa and Lesotho, but the genus is also found in the Forest Sandstone and the Mpandi Formation of Zimbabwe. Material from the US, India, and Argentina was previously assigned to the genus, but the US and Argentinian specimens are now assigned to their own genera (Sarahsaurus and Adeopapposaurus). Because of their great abundance, Massospondylus fossils have been used to date rocks, and a biozone, the Massospondylus Range Zone, is named after the genus.

Matheronodon.etymology: Named after French paleontologist Philippe Matheron, combined with Greek 'odon' (tooth); meaning 'Matheron's tooth'.
Matheronodon.description: Matheronodon is a genus of rhabdodontid ornithopod dinosaur from the late Cretaceous Period of the Grès à Reptiles Formation in France. The genus contains a single species, M. provincialis, which is known from a single maxilla and associated teeth. It was named by Pascal Godefroit and colleagues in 2017. The teeth of Matheronodon are large but few in number. The teeth are also in an unusual arrangement, emerging alternatingly from one of a pair of fused tooth sockets in its mouth. In life, the teeth would have functioned like a pair of scissors, allowing Matheronodon to feed on the tough leaves of monocot plants.

Mercuriceratops.etymology: From Latin 'Mercurius' (the Roman messenger god, whose winged helmet is evoked by the rod-and-flange shape of the squamosal) and Greek 'keras' (horn) and 'ops' (face); meaning 'Mercury's horned face'.
Mercuriceratops.description: Mercuriceratops is an extinct genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsid from the late Campanian of northern Laramidia, with the holotype recovered from the upper Judith River Formation of Fergus County, Montana, and a paratype squamosal from the lower Dinosaur Park Formation of Dinosaur Provincial Park, Alberta. The single species, Mercuriceratops gemini, is diagnosed by a uniquely rod-shaped posterior ramus of the squamosal — constricted into a mediolaterally compressed bar instead of the tapering triangle typical of chasmosaurines — with a hatchet-shaped lateral margin bearing four tab-shaped episquamosals. The "twin" species name refers to the two right squamosals from two formations on either side of the Canada-Montana border.

Anterolateral flange bears four large, tab-shaped, well-fused episquamosals on its lateral margin.
Elongate episquamosals extending along the lateral margin of the posteriorly projecting rod-shaped squamosal bar.
Deeply incised longitudinal grooves on the medioventral surface of the posterior squamosal shaft forming a robust, tightly interdigitating sutural contact for the parietal.

Metriacanthosaurus.description: Metriacanthosaurus is a genus of metriacanthosaurid dinosaur from the Oxford Clay Formation of England, dating to the Late Jurassic period, about 160 million years ago (lower Oxfordian). It is the only metriacanthosaurid currently named from outside of Asia.
diagnostic_features: Elevated neural spines of dorsal vertebrae, inclined slightly forward
Ilium with abrupt change in inclination of superior margin, blade relatively deeper at that point
Pubic foot expanded, originally ~18 cm long
Femora relatively more slender than M. bucklandi
Lesser trochanter more proximally placed
Cnemial process of tibia projects strongly upward

Mexidracon.etymology: From 'Mexi-' (referring to Mexico) and Greek 'drakon' (dragon or serpent); meaning 'Mexican dragon'.
Mexidracon.description: Mexidracon is an extinct genus of ornithomimid theropod dinosaurs from the late Cretaceous Cerro del Pueblo Formation of Coahuila, Mexico. The genus contains a single species, M. longimanus, known from a partial skeleton. Mexidracon is the second ornithomimosaur to be named from this formation, following the deinocheirid Paraxenisaurus in 2020.
diagnostic_features: Extreme elongation of metacarpus: metacarpal III length is 1.1 times humeral length, 1.072 times metatarsal II length, and 1.018 times metatarsal IV length.
Proximal end of metacarpal II with a narrow subtriangular outline.
Iliac pubic peduncle with a flared, zig-zag shaped articular margin that is wider anteriorly than posteriorly.
Distal end of pubis with distal margin of anterior expansion separated from shaft by a deep notch.
Ilium with ischiadic peduncle slightly longer proximodistally than pubic peduncle.
Deeply concave iliac brevis fossa expanded posteriorly, overhanging the lateral surface of the postacetabular process.

species.name: Mexidracon longimanus
species.etymology: From Latin 'longimanus' meaning 'long hand', referring to the extreme elongation of the metacarpals in the holotype.

holotype.material: Partially articulated skeleton: several dorsal, sacral, and caudal vertebrae, haemal arches, left humerus, left metacarpals I-III, partial left and right pelvic girdles, complete left and partial right femur, complete left tibia and proximal right tibia, proximal left and right fibulae, distal tarsals 3-4, left metatarsals II-IV, four pedal phalanges.

Microceratus.description: Microceratus is a genus of small ceratopsian dinosaur that lived in the Cretaceous period of Mongolia. It walked on two legs, had short front arms, a characteristic ceratopsian frill and beak-like mouth, and was around 60 cm (2.0 ft) long. It was one of the most primitive ceratopsians, or horned dinosaurs, along with Psittacosaurus, which was also discovered in Mongolia.
diagnostic_features: Atlas not reduced as in Leptoceratops/Protoceratops; instead enlarged, carrying at least 2/3 of bowl-shaped articular surface for occipital condyle
Lower jaw: last tooth cuts gums at base of ascending ramus, with no groove separating tooth row from ascending ramus (unlike Protoceratops)
Lower jaw: outer ridge runs in middle and swells to a convexity reaching the lower border of the dentary (vs. higher up with concavity below in Protoceratops andrewsi)
Lower jaw: anterior end twisted inwards in inferior view (vs. straight in Protoceratops andrewsi)
Femoral head with broad vertical groove posteriorly giving semilunar outline in superior view; absent in ?Psittacosaurus

Microcoelus.etymology: From Greek 'mikros' (small) and 'koilos' (hollow); meaning 'small hollow', a reference to the shallow lateral pit on the holotype dorsal vertebra.
Microcoelus.description: Microcoelus is a dubious genus of small titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Santonian stage) Bajo de la Carpa Formation, Argentina. It is known from only a single dorsal vertebra, although a left humerus was formerly referred to this taxon, but it is now considered to belong to Neuquensaurus. The type (and only known) species is M. patagonicus, described by British paleontologist Richard Lydekker in 1893.
diagnostic_features: Anterior dorsal vertebrae opisthocoeolous with well-marked rib-facets on fore part of arch lamina
Lateral pits (shallow, somewhat circular depressions) on dorsal vertebrae, apparently without communication with interior of bone
Caudal vertebrae amphicoelous (or platycoeolous), differing from procoeolous caudals of Titanosaurus and Argyrosaurus
Humerus short and broadly expanded, with large swollen deltoid crest extending lower on shaft than in Titanosaurus australis or Argyrosaurus
Zygapophyses of caudal vertebrae very slightly developed and scarcely articulated with one another

synonyms.name: Microsaurops
synonyms.reason: Replacement name proposed by Kuhn (1963) under the mistaken belief that the original Microcoelus Lydekker, 1893 had been preoccupied. The supposed preoccupier "Microsaurus" (cited from Hatcher 1900; Lull 1910) was itself only a misspelling of Microcoelus, so the replacement was unnecessary. Listed by Olshevsky (1991).

species.name: Microcoelus patagonicus
species.etymology: From Patagonia, the region of Argentina where the type material was collected.

holotype.material: An anterior dorsal vertebra. Lydekker provisionally associated a left humerus and the posterior half of a caudal vertebra from the same locality; the humerus is now considered to belong to Neuquensaurus.

Microhadrosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'mikros' meaning 'small' and 'hadros' meaning 'bulky', plus Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'small bulky lizard', reflecting its small size compared to other hadrosaurs.
Microhadrosaurus.description: Microhadrosaurus is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian or Maastrichtian) Nanxiong Formation of Guangdong, China. Although its name identifies it as a small hadrosaurid, it is based on juvenile remains, and the adult size is unknown.

species.name: Microhadrosaurus nanshiungensis
species.etymology: Named for the Nanxiong Basin in Guangdong Province, China, where the holotype was discovered.

holotype.institution: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology
holotype.material: Partial lower jaw (dentary) from a juvenile

Micropachycephalosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'mikros' (small), 'pachys' (thick), 'kephale' (head), and 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'small thick-headed lizard'.
Micropachycephalosaurus.description: Micropachycephalosaurus is an extinct genus of basal marginocephalian dinosaur, containing only the type species, Micropachycephalosaurus hongtuyanensis. It lived in China during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) and was found in the Jiangjunding Formation. It has the longest name of any dinosaur, with 23 letters in the genus name alone, while the full binomial contains 37 letters.

Supratemporal fenestra not closed
No prominent sagittal crest on the skull
Teeth slender, arranged in a single row, with central ridge on outer surface and symmetrical small cusps on anterior and posterior edges
Six fused sacral vertebrae with neural spines connected into a plate-like structure
Quadrate with small anterior inclination angle

Microraptor.etymology: From Greek 'mikros' (small) and Latin 'raptor' (one who seizes); meaning 'small thief' or 'small raptor'
Microraptor.description: Microraptor is a genus of small, four-winged dromaeosaurid dinosaurs. Numerous well-preserved fossil specimens have been recovered from Liaoning, China. They date from the early Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation (Aptian stage), 125 to 120 million years ago. Three species have been named (M. zhaoianus, M. gui, and M. hanqingi), though further study has suggested that all of them represent variation in a single species, which is properly called M. zhaoianus. Cryptovolans, initially described as another four-winged dinosaur, is usually considered to be a synonym of Microraptor.
diagnostic_features: Anterior serrations absent on all teeth
Posterior teeth have basal constriction between crown and root
Middle caudal vertebrae about 3-4 times as long as anterior dorsal vertebrae
Accessory crest of femur at the base of the lesser trochanter
Tail with less than 26 vertebrae
Strongly recurved and slender pedal unguals with prominent flexor tubercle

Microvenator.etymology: From Greek 'mikros' meaning 'small' and Latin 'venator' meaning 'hunter'; translates as 'small hunter', named for its small size.
Microvenator.description: Microvenator is a genus of oviraptorosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Cloverly Formation in what is now south central Montana. The holotype fossil is an incomplete skeleton, most likely a juvenile with a length of 1.3 m (4.3 ft), and consequently, the adult size remains uncertain. Microvenator is primitive and may be the "sister taxon to all other oviraptorosaurs."
diagnostic_features: Very small, delicately built coelurid with hollow thin-walled vertebrae and limb bones
Cervicals without neural spines and with double pleurocoels
Dorsal neural arches low and highly sculpted; neural spines low and rectangular
Astragalus with very high and broad ascending process
Pubis profile concave anteriorly with only moderate distal expansion
Short but prominent lesser trochanter on femur with depression at fourth trochanter site
Femur-tibia ratio indicating swift running capabilities
Absence of cervical neural spines (unlike most other theropods)
Relatively long forearms approaching tibia length

Mierasaurus.etymology: Named for Bernardo de Miera y Pacheco, an eighteenth-century Spanish cartographer and explorer of the American Southwest, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Mierasaurus.description: Mierasaurus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Utah, United States. The taxon was first described and named in 2017 by Rafael Royo-Torres and colleagues, from a mostly complete skeleton including a disarticulated partial skull and mandible, teeth, multiple vertebrae from along the length of the body, both scapulae, radius and ulna bones, a left manus, a complete pelvis, both femora and the entire left hindlimb. Additionally, they referred a lower jaw and femur from juvenile individuals, which were found nearby, to the genus. Collectively, Mierasaurus is among the most completely known North American sauropods. The genus name honors Bernardo de Miera y Pacheco, the first European scientist to enter what is now Utah. The type species for Mierasaurus is Mierasaurus bobyoungi, named after Robert Glen Young, a paleontologist who researched the Early Cretaceous of Utah.
diagnostic_features: Otosphenoidal ridge extends from anterior surface of paroccipital process near its ventral margin and restricted to medialmost part of latter process
Occipital condyle has pair of rounded ridges extending dorsoventrally on either lateral face of condylar articular surface
Atlantal intercentrum bears pair of depressions in medial surface facing posteromedially, each receiving anterolateral margin of odontoid process
Cervical ribs bear ridge or bulge on lateral surface of tuberculum immediately posterior to base of anterior process
Lateral depression on distal ramus of haemal arches
Metacarpal I longer than metacarpal IV
Very short ischium compared to pubis (ischium:pubis length ratio 0.75)
Fourth trochanter placed in proximal part of femur
Femur with subequal distal condyles
Pedal unguals 2 and 3 compressed dorsoventrally

Minotaurasaurus.etymology: Named after the Minotaur of Greek mythology (the bull of Minos) combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Minos's bull reptile'.
Minotaurasaurus.description: Minotaurasaurus is a monospecific genus of ankylosaurid dinosaur that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous (late Campanian stage, ~75-71 Ma) in what is now the Djadochta Formation. The type and only species, Minotaurasaurus ramachandrani, is known from two skulls, a cervical vertebra and a cervical half ring. It was named and described in 2009 by Clifford Miles and Clark Miles. The holotype of Minotaurasaurus has been suspected to be illegally exported out of Mongolia. It has been suggested to be a synonym of Tarchia but more recent publications consider it as a distinct genus.

Miragaia.etymology: Named for Miragaia, a parish in Porto, Portugal near where the fossil was discovered; the Wikipedia article retrieved is about the Portuguese locality itself.
Miragaia.description: Miragaia is a genus of long-necked stegosaurid dinosaur. Its fossils have been found in Upper Jurassic rocks in Portugal (Lourinhã Formation, Sobral Unit) and possibly also Wyoming and Utah, United States (Morrison Formation). Miragaia has the longest neck known for any stegosaurian, which included at least seventeen vertebrae. Some researchers consider this taxon to be a junior synonym of Dacentrurus.

Mongolostegus.etymology: From 'Mongol' (Mongolia, where it was found) and Greek 'stegos' (roof); meaning 'Mongolian roof', referencing Mongolia and its classification as a stegosaur.
Mongolostegus.description: Mongolostegus is an extinct genus of stegosaurian dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian-Albian ages) Dzunbain Formation of Mongolia. The genus contains a single species, Mongolostegus exspectabilis, known from a fragmentary single specimen representing the first stegosaur named from Mongolia. It is one of the youngest known stegosaurs, along with Yanbeilong and an unnamed species from the Hekou Group of China. In contrast to these taxa, which are members of the late-diverging stegosaur subfamily Stegosaurinae, Mongolostegus may have affinities to more basal taxa such as the Huayangosauridae.

Monkonosaurus.etymology: Named for Markam County (also known as Monko), the region of Tibet where the holotype was found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Monkonosaurus.description: Monkonosaurus is a dubious genus of herbivorous stegosaurian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic/Early Cretaceous-aged Loe-ein Formation of Tibet (or the Early Cretaceous Lura Formation of China). Some sources place it as alive during the Oxfordian - Albian stages, around 163 - 100 million years ago, although Monkonosaurus was probably only alive during the Late Jurassic (163 - 152.1 ± 0.9 million years ago), making it among the earliest known stegosaurs along with Chungkingosaurus and Bashanosaurus.

Mononykus.etymology: From Greek 'monos' (one) and 'onyx' (claw); meaning 'one claw', referring to its single functional forelimb claw.
Mononykus.description: Mononykus is a genus of alvarezsaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Mongolia, specifically the Nemegt Formation. Mononykus was a very small theropod, estimated around 1 to 1.2 meters (3.3 to 3.9 ft) in length with a weight of 3.5 kilograms (7.7 lb). As in Shuvuuia, Mononykus likely developed a shaggy feathering. It was lightly built with long, thin legs and highly reduced and specialized forelimbs that were likely used for foraging termite mounds or other insect colonies.

Mosaiceratops.description: Mosaiceratops is a genus of ceratopsian dinosaur that lived in the upper Cretaceous Xiaguan Formation in what is now the Henan Province of China. It was described by Zheng, Jin, and Xu in 2015 as the type species Mosaiceratops azumai. Although phylogenetic analyses have found it to be the basalmost neoceratopsian, the authors noted that several features in the premaxilla and nasal bones are shared with Psittacosaurus, indicating that neoceratopsians evolved premaxillary teeth twice and that the latter is not as primitive as previously thought.

Muttaburrasaurus.etymology: Named for Muttaburra, a town in Queensland, Australia near where the fossil was discovered, combined with Greek '-saurus' meaning 'lizard'.
Muttaburrasaurus.description: Muttaburrasaurus was a genus of herbivorous iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur that lived in what is now north-eastern Australia sometime between 112 and 103 million years ago during the early Cretaceous period. After Kunbarrasaurus, it is Australia's most completely known dinosaur from skeletal remains. It was named after Muttaburra, the site in Queensland, Australia, where it was found. The dinosaur was selected from twelve candidates to become the official fossil emblem of the State of Queensland.

Muyelensaurus.description: Muyelensaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Argentina. It was more slender than other titanosaurs. Mymoorapelta.etymology: Named after the Mygatt-Moore Quarry (combining the names of its discoverers) combined with Greek 'pelta' (shield); meaning 'shield from the Mygatt-Moore Quarry'.
Mymoorapelta.description: Mymoorapelta is a nodosaurid ankylosaur from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian-Tithonian, around 155 to 150 million years ago) Morrison Formation (Brushy Basin Member) of western Colorado and central Utah, USA. The animal is known from a single species, Mymoorapelta maysi, and few specimens are known. The most complete specimen is the holotype individual from the Mygatt-Moore Quarry, which includes osteoderms, a partial skull, vertebrae, and other bones. It was initially described by James Kirkland and Kenneth Carpenter in 1994. Along with Gargoyleosaurus, it is one of the earliest known nodosaurids.

Nagatitan.etymology: From Nāga, the mythological serpent-like creature of various Asian cultures (especially northeastern Thailand), and Greek 'titan' meaning 'giant'.
Nagatitan.description: Nagatitan is an extinct genus of euhelopodid sauropod dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian–Albian) Khok Kruat Formation of Thailand. The genus contains a single species, Nagatitan chaiyaphumensis, known from a partial postcranial skeleton. With an estimated body length of about 27 meters and a mass of 25–28 tonnes, it is the largest dinosaur currently known from Southeast Asia.

Distal end of pubis transversely expanded along the lateral surface relative to the shaft.
Proximal third of femur with anteroposteriorly narrowed lateral margin forming a flange-like trochanteric shelf bounded medially by a vertical ridge.

Nankangia.etymology: Named after Nankang County (now Nankang District), Ganzhou City, Jiangxi Province, China, where the specimen was found
Nankangia.description: Nankangia is an extinct genus of caenagnathoid oviraptorosaurian dinosaur known from the Upper Cretaceous Nanxiong Formation of Nankang County, Ganzhou City of Jiangxi Province, southeastern China. It contains a single species, Nankangia jiangxiensis. N. jiangxiensis coexisted with at least four other caenagnathoids, including but not limited to Corythoraptor, Banji, Ganzhousaurus and Jiangxisaurus. The relatively short dentary and non-downturned mandibular symphysis of Nankangia suggest that it may have been more herbivorous than carnivorous. Its diet consisted of leaves and seeds.

Nanosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'nanos' (small or dwarf) and 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'small or dwarf lizard'.
Nanosaurus.description: Nanosaurus is an extinct genus of neornithischian dinosaur that lived about 155 to 148 million years ago, during the Late Jurassic in North America. Its fossils are known from the Morrison Formation of the south-western United States. The type and only species, Nanosaurus agilis, was described and named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1877. The taxon has a complicated taxonomic history, largely the work of Marsh and Peter M. Galton, involving the genera Laosaurus, Hallopus, Drinker, Othnielia, and Othnielosaurus, the latter three now being considered to be synonyms of Nanosaurus. It had historically been classified as a hypsilophodont or fabrosaur, types of generalized small bipedal herbivore, but more recent research has abandoned these groupings as paraphyletic and Nanosaurus is today considered a basal member of Neornithischia.

Nanotyrannus.etymology: Originally proposed by Bakker, Williams and Currie (1988) as Latin nano ("small") plus tyrannus ("tyrant"); the derivation is now usually corrected to Greek nanos ("dwarf" or "pygmy") and tyrannos ("king"), in reference to the small body size relative to other tyrannosauroids.
Nanotyrannus.description: Nanotyrannus is a genus of tyrannosauroid dinosaur that lived in what is now western North America during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous, 67 to 66 million years ago. Its fossils are known from the Hell Creek Formation. It was one of the last-known non-avian dinosaurs and lived until the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event. The first named species, N. lancensis, was described as a new species of Gorgosaurus in 1946 by Charles W. Gilmore based on a single skull. Re-examination of the specimen in 1988 by Robert T. Bakker, Michael Williams and Philip J. Currie moved the species to a new genus of tyrannosaurid, named Nanotyrannus in reference to its small body size compared to other tyrannosaurids.
Nanotyrannus.dispute: The validity of Nanotyrannus is actively contested. After the 1988 erection of the genus, Carr (1999) and Woodward et al. (2020) argued that the holotype CMNH 7541 is an immature Tyrannosaurus rex, citing tooth-grain immaturity and femoral osteohistology. Longrich and Saitta (2024), Zanno and Napoli (2025) — who erected a second species, N. lethaeus — and Griffin et al. (2025, ceratobranchial histology) reaffirmed Nanotyrannus as a distinct, skeletally mature taxon. No broad consensus yet.
diagnostic_features: Muzzle width greatly constricted, only one fourth the width of the temporal region.
Extraordinarily wide basicranium between basitubera and basipterygoid processes.
Two large pneumatic foramina placed one behind the other near the midline of the basisphenoid.
Dorsal surface of the nasal lacks strong ridges and striae.
Parietal wing of the occiput with a sharp angle between dorsal and lateral edges.
Basicranial boxwork with flat ventral floor.

synonyms.name: Gorgosaurus lancensis
synonyms.reason: Original combination established by Gilmore (1946) for CMNH 7541, based on apparent affinities with G. sternbergi and G. libratus. Bakker, Williams and Currie (1988) reassigned the species to a new genus Nanotyrannus, yielding Nanotyrannus lancensis (Gilmore, 1946).

synonyms.name: Clevelanotyrannus
synonyms.reason: Name appearing on the original submitted manuscript and mentioned by Currie (1987) before peer-review feedback led the authors to rewrite the description; the published 1988 paper used Nanotyrannus instead and Clevelanotyrannus was never validly published.

species.etymology: From Latin lancensis ("of the Lance"), referring to the Lance Formation — Gilmore's (1946) original (and mistaken) attribution of the holotype's geological context; the actual horizon is the Hell Creek Formation.

holotype.material: A nearly complete skull with tightly articulated lower jaws (~57 cm premaxilla-to-quadrate); the right squamosal, postfrontal, quadratojugal and upper half of the right quadrate are missing, and many teeth are incomplete.

Nanshiungosaurus.etymology: Named after Nanxiong (formerly romanized as Nanshiung), a city in Guangdong Province, China, where it was discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Nanxiong's lizard'.
Nanshiungosaurus.description: Nanshiungosaurus is a genus of therizinosaurid that lived in what is now Asia during the Late Cretaceous of South China. The type species, Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus, was first discovered in 1974 and described in 1979 by Dong Zhiming. It is represented by a single specimen preserving most of the cervical and dorsal vertebrae with the pelvis. A supposed and unlikely second species, "Nanshiungosaurus" bohlini, was found in 1992 and described in 1997. It is also represented by vertebrae but this species however, differs in geological age and lacks authentic characteristics compared to the type, making its affinity to the genus unsupported.

Napaisaurus.etymology: From 'Napai' (the Napai Basin in Fusui County, Guangxi, where the holotype was discovered) and Greek 'sauros' (lizard).
Napaisaurus.description: Napaisaurus is an extinct genus of basal iguanodontian ornithopod from the Aptian (Early Cretaceous) second member of the Xinlong Formation, Napai Basin, Fusui County, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, southern China. The single species, Napaisaurus guangxiensis, is known from a partial right pelvis (right ilium and ischium of a single individual). Ji and Zhang (2022) identify it as the first formally named basal iguanodontian dinosaur from southern China.
diagnostic_features: Preacetabular process of the ilium strongly curved ventrally and slightly inclined laterally, with a very long pubic peduncle extending anteroventrally, forming a narrow and deep U-shaped preacetabular notch with nearly parallel lateral margins.
Depth-to-length ratio of the iliac body is approximately 1; postacetabular process length is approximately 0.7 times the iliac body length.
Supraacetabular process expanded and thickened dorsoventrally, with its anteroposterior length occupying approximately the anterior half of the total postacetabular process length.
Posterior portion of the postacetabular process expands significantly medially in the transverse direction, forming a short, wide brevis shelf on the ventral surface.
Articular surface of the ischial peduncle of the ilium is broad and concave.
Iliac peduncle of the ischium shows significant lateral thickening toward the distal end, with a strongly convex distal articular surface.

Narambuenatitan is known from the holotype MAU-Pv-N-425, an incomplete skeleton. It was collected in 2005 and 2006 from the Anacleto Formation (Neuquén Group) in northern Patagonia. Nasutoceratops.etymology: From Latin 'nasutus' meaning 'large-nosed' and Latinized Greek 'ceratops' meaning 'horned face'; translates as 'large-nosed horned face', referring to its distinctive enlarged nasal region.
Nasutoceratops.description: Nasutoceratops is a genus of ceratopsid dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous period, about 76.0-75.5 million years ago. The first known specimens were discovered in Utah in the Kaiparowits Formation of the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument (GSENM) from 2006 onwards, including a subadult skull with both a partial postcranial skeleton and rare skin impressions, and two other partial skulls. In 2013, the subadult was made the holotype of the new genus and species Nasutoceratops titusi; the generic name means "large-nosed horned face", and the specific name honors the paleontologist Alan L. Titus for his work at the GSENM. The dinosaur was noted for its large nose in news reports, and later featured in Jurassic World films.

Natovenator.description: Natovenator is a genus of halszkaraptorine dromaeosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Barun Goyot Formation of Mongolia. The genus is known from a single species, N. polydontus. Natovenator is crucial to the understanding of halszkaraptorines due to it providing more support for the semi-aquatic lifestyle that has been proposed for this clade. This discovery is important as the semi-aquatic lifestyles of halszkaraptorines (mainly Halszkaraptor) was contested in early 2022.

Nebulasaurus.description: Nebulasaurus is an extinct genus of basal eusauropod dinosaur known from the early Middle Jurassic Zhanghe Formation (Aalenian or Bajocian stage) of Yunnan Province, China. This discovery is significant paleontologically because it represents a clade of basal eusauropods previously unknown from Asia.

Nedoceratops.etymology: From Russian 'nedo' (insufficient) and Greek 'keratops' (horned face); meaning 'insufficient horned face', in reference to the absence of a prominent nasal horn on the holotype skull.
Nedoceratops.description: Nedoceratops is a controversial genus of ceratopsid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period Lance Formation of North America. It is known only from a single skull discovered in Wyoming. Its status is the subject of ongoing debate among paleontologists: some authors consider Nedoceratops a valid, distinct taxon, while others consider it to be an unusual specimen of Triceratops.
Nedoceratops.dispute: The validity of Nedoceratops is actively contested. Scannella and Horner (2010, 2011) and Scannella et al. (2014) treated USNM 2412 as a transitional or ontogenetic morph within Triceratops, arguing that Triceratops, Torosaurus, and Nedoceratops together represent different growth stages of a single anagenetic lineage. Farke (2011) and Maiorino et al. (2013) rebutted this, treating Nedoceratops as a distinct chasmosaurine genus diagnosed by an undifferentiated nasal horncore, near-vertical postorbital horncores, and small parietal fenestrae. No broad consensus has been reached.
diagnostic_features: Nasal horncore nearly completely undifferentiated from the nasal bone, appearing as a poorly defined swelling rather than a discrete horn or knob.
Greater portion of the procurved postorbital horncores forms approximately a 90-degree angle with the tooth row.
Parietal fenestrae extremely small, occupying less than five percent of the total surface area of the parietal.
Ventral extremity of the squamosal positioned well above the alveolar process of the maxilla.

Nemegtomaia.etymology: Named for the Nemegt Basin of Mongolia where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'maia' meaning 'good mother', in reference to the brooding behavior of oviraptorids.
Nemegtomaia.description: Nemegtomaia is a genus of oviraptorid dinosaur from what is now Mongolia that lived in the Late Cretaceous Period, about 72 to 70 million years ago. The first specimen was found in 1996, and became the basis of the new genus and species N. barsboldi in 2004. The original genus name was Nemegtia, but this was changed to Nemegtomaia in 2005, as the former name was preoccupied. The first part of the generic name refers to the Nemegt Basin, where the animal was found, and the second part means "good mother", in reference to the fact that oviraptorids are known to have brooded their eggs. The specific name honors the paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold. Two more specimens were found in 2007, one of which was found on top of a nest with eggs, but the dinosaur had received its genus name before it was found associated with eggs.

Nemegtosaurus.etymology: Named for the Nemegt Basin in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia where the skull was discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Nemegtosaurus.description: Nemegtosaurus was a sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period of what is now Mongolia. Measuring an estimated 12-13 m (39-43 ft) long and weighing 20 t (44,000 lb), it was named after the Nemegt Basin in the Gobi Desert, where the remains - a single skull - were found. The skull resembles diplodocoids in being long and low, with pencil-shaped teeth. However, recent work has shown that Nemegtosaurus is in fact a titanosaur, closely related to animals such as Saltasaurus, Alamosaurus, and Rapetosaurus.

Neosodon.description: Neosodon was a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the late Tithonian-aged (Upper Jurassic) Sables et Gres a Trigonia gibbosa of Pas-de-Calais department, France. It has never been formally given a species name, but is often seen as N. praecursor, which actually comes from a different animal. Often in the past, it had been assigned to the wastebasket taxon Pelorosaurus, but restudy has suggested that it could be related to Turiasaurus, a roughly contemporaneous giant Spanish sauropod. It is only known from six teeth.

Neovenator.etymology: From Latin neo- ('new') and venator ('hunter'), meaning 'new hunter'
Neovenator.description: Neovenator is an extinct genus of carcharodontosaurian theropod dinosaur. It is known primarily from several skeletons found in the Early Cretaceous (Hauterivian-Barremian) Wessex Formation on the south coast of the Isle of Wight, southern England. The first remains of Neovenator were discovered in 1978 alongside those of the ornithopod Brighstoneus, after the collapse of part of Grange Chine. In 1996, Steve Hutt, David Martill and Michael Barker named the genus Neovenator. One species is known: the type species, N. salerii, after the Salero family who owned the site on which its remains were discovered.

Newtonsaurus.etymology: From 'Newton' (honoring British paleontologist Edwin Tully Newton, 1840-1930, of the Geological Survey, who first described the holotype) and Greek 'sauros' (lizard).
Newtonsaurus.description: Newtonsaurus is an extinct genus of large neotheropod dinosaur from the Rhaetian (Late Triassic) Cotham Member of the Lilstock Formation, Penarth Group, recovered at Stormy Down near Bridgend in South Wales. The single species, Newtonsaurus cambrensis, is known from a natural mold of a left dentary preserved as two blocks of sandstone (basionym 'Zanclodon' cambrensis Newton 1899); Evans, Howells, Wintle and Benton (2025) re-evaluated the holotype and erected the new genus, recovering the taxon tentatively as a coelophysoid with morphological affinity to Dilophosaurus, although a stem-averostran position cannot be excluded. The estimated body length of 5-7 m, derived from a ~28 cm preserved dentary representing roughly half the mandible, makes Newtonsaurus a candidate for the largest known Late Triassic theropod. The genus name had been used as a nomen nudum in private compilations since 1999 and is formally established by this paper.

Lateral foramina along the labial groove anteroposteriorly elongated (elliptical, ~1.5 cm long) rather than circular.
Single Meckelian foramen at the anterior terminus of the Meckelian groove, level with the third alveolus.
Unfused, sub-pentagonal interdental plates separated from the medial dentary wall by a narrow paradental groove open for its entire length.
Relative mandible depth (depth/length ratio ~17.8%) intermediate between that of shallow coelophysoid forms and deeper-jawed forms.

Nigersaurus.etymology: Named after Niger, the African country where it was discovered, combined with Latin 'saurus' (lizard); meaning 'Niger reptile'.
Nigersaurus.description: Nigersaurus is a genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaur that lived during the middle Cretaceous period, about 115 to 105 million years ago. It was discovered in the Elrhaz Formation in an area called Gadoufaoua, in Niger. Fossils of this dinosaur were first described in 1976, but it was only named Nigersaurus taqueti in 1999 after further and more complete remains were found and described. The genus name means "Niger reptile", and the specific name honors the paleontologist Philippe Taquet, who discovered the first remains.

Ningyuansaurus.etymology: Derived from Ningyuan, an ancient name for Xingcheng City in western Liaoning Province, China, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'
Ningyuansaurus.description: Ningyuansaurus is a pennaraptoran dinosaur genus. It contains the single species Ningyuansaurus wangi, known from a fossil specimen from the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation (Aptian stage, 124.6 Ma ago) of Jianchang, western Liaoning Province, People's Republic of China. It was originally thought to be the basalmost species of oviraptorosaur, based on its long skull and a greater number of teeth in comparison to any other known oviraptorosaur. However, later research showed that it is a member of Halszkaraptorinae. The generic name Ningyuansaurus is derived from Ningyuan, an ancient name for Xingcheng City. The specific name honors Wang Qiuwu, the private owner of the specimen who donated it for scientific study. The specimen is now in the Confuciusornis Museum in Xingcheng.

Niobrarasaurus.etymology: Named after the Niobrara Formation of Kansas where its fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Niobrara lizard'.
Niobrarasaurus.description: Niobrarasaurus is an extinct genus of nodosaurid ankylosaurian dinosaur which lived during the Late Cretaceous, around 87 to 82 million years ago. Its fossils were found in the Smoky Hill Chalk Member of the Niobrara Formation, in western Kansas, which would have been near the middle of the Western Interior Seaway during the Late Cretaceous. It was probably closely related to Nodosaurus.

Nipponosaurus.etymology: Named for Nippon (Japan), the country that controlled Sakhalin Island where the fossils were found at the time of description, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Nipponosaurus.description: Nipponosaurus is a lambeosaurine hadrosaur from sediments of the Yezo Group, in Sinegorsk on the island of Sakhalin, which was part of Japan at the time of the species' classification. The type and only species is N. sachalinensis, known only from a single juvenile specimen discovered in 1934 and named in 1936, by Takumi Nagao, with further material of the same individual found in 1937. Since then, the taxon has been largely ignored, and its validity has been doubted, with synonymy with other Asian hadrosaurs or status as a nomen dubium being suggested. Redescriptions from 2004 and 2017, however, have supported recognition as a distinct species. Dating the only specimen has been difficult, but based on associated mollusc taxa, the species likely lived sometime in the upper Santonian or lower Campanian, around 80 million years ago.

Noasaurus.etymology: Named after the Noroeste Argentino (northwestern Argentina) region, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Northwestern Argentina lizard'.
Noasaurus.description: Noasaurus is a genus of ceratosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Maastrichtian (Late Cretaceous) of Argentina. The type and only species is N. leali. The fragmentary holotype specimen of Noasaurus, PVL 4061, consisting of a few cranial and postcranial bones, was discovered from strata from the Lecho Formation of Southern Salta in 1975 by a team led by José Fernando Bonaparte. When described by Bonaparte and in PhD student Jaime Powell in 1980, it was believed to be a coelurosaur theropod and assigned to a family of its own; this family, Noasauridae, still exists, though has been reassigned to Ceratosauria.

Nodocephalosaurus.etymology: From Latin 'nodus' (knob), Greek 'kephale' (head), and Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'knob headed lizard', referring to the nodular ornamentation on its skull.
Nodocephalosaurus.description: Nodocephalosaurus is a monospecific genus of ankylosaurid dinosaur from New Mexico that lived during the Late Cretaceous (late Campanian to early Maastrichtian stage, 73.49 to 72 Ma) in what is now the De-na-zin member of the Kirtland Formation. The type and only species, Nodocephalosaurus kirtlandensis, is known only from a partial skull. It was named in 1999 by Robert M. Sullivan. Nodocephalosaurus has an estimated length of 4.5 meters (15 feet) and weight of 1.5 tonnes (3,306 lbs). It is closely related and shares similar cranial anatomy to Akainacephalus.

Nothronychus.etymology: From Greek 'nothros' meaning 'slothful' and 'onyx' meaning 'claw'; translates as 'slothful claw', a reference to its therizinosaur-like elongated claws and presumed slow-moving herbivorous habits.
Nothronychus.description: Nothronychus is a genus of therizinosaurid theropod dinosaurs that lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous period. The type species, Nothronychus mckinleyi, was described by James Kirkland and Douglas G. Wolfe in 2001. It was recovered near New Mexico's border with Arizona, in an area known as the Zuni Basin, from rocks assigned to the Moreno Hill Formation, dating to the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous. A second specimen, described in 2009 as a second species, Nothronychus graffami, was found in the Tropic Shale of Utah, dating to between one million and 500,000 years older than N. mckinleyi.

Notoceratops.description: Notoceratops is a dubious genus of extinct ornithischian dinosaur. The genus was described based on an incomplete, toothless left dentary (now lost) from the Late Cretaceous of Patagonia (in Argentina), probably dating to the Campanian or Maastrichtian. Initially classified as a putative ceratopsian found in the Lago Colhué Huapi Formation, the lost fragmentary holotype precludes confident referral of this taxon within ornithischians, with some researchers suggesting that it belongs to a hadrosaur instead.

Tibia with marked anteromedial longitudinal enlargement in proximal third
Fibula with abrupt anteroposterior narrowing in mid-shaft

Nqwebasaurus.etymology: From Xhosa 'Nqweba', the local name for the Kirkwood district in the Eastern Cape of South Africa where the specimen was found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Nqwebasaurus.description: Nqwebasaurus is a probable ornithomimosaurian theropod from the Early Cretaceous of South Africa. The genus contains a single species, Nqwebasaurus thwazi, representing the oldest known coelurosaur in Africa and the evidence for basal coelurosaurian dinosaurs inhabiting Gondwana since the earliest Cretaceous period.

Manual ungual phalanx of digit I elongate (four times proximal depth) and mediolaterally compressed
Fibular shaft reduced distally to thin splint
Metatarsal IV reduced in width to approximately half that of metatarsal III

Nullotitan.etymology: Named in honor of geologist Francisco Nullo, combined with Greek 'titan' (giant); meaning 'Nullo's giant'.
Nullotitan.description: Nullotitan is an extinct genus of lithostrotian titanosaur dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Chorrillo Formation of Santa Cruz Province, Argentina. The genus contains a single species, Nullotitan glaciaris. It was a contemporary of the ornithopod Isasicursor, which was described in the same paper.

All caudal vertebrae centra lacking pneumatization
Mid-caudals with deep ventral longitudinal furrow surrounded by thick longitudinal ridges
Fibula with pronounced sigmoid curvature in anterior or posterior view
Distal tibia end strongly anteroposteriorly compressed and more transversely expanded than other titanosaurs

Nuthetes.etymology: From Koine Greek 'nouthetes' meaning 'one who admonishes' or 'a monitor', referring to the similarity of its teeth to those of a modern monitor lizard.
Nuthetes.description: Nuthetes is a genus of coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur, either a dromaeosaurid or tyrannosauroid, known only from fossil teeth and jaw fragments found in rocks of the middle Berriasian age (Early Cretaceous) in the Cherty Freshwater Member of the Lulworth Formation in England and also the Angeac-Charente bonebed in France. If it was a dromaeosaurid, Nuthetes would have been a small predator.
diagnostic_features: Teeth with enamelled crowns that are moderately long, slender, compressed, pointed, and slightly recurved, with well-marked serrated margins both before and behind
Teeth thickest towards the anterior part, closely resembling in miniature the teeth of Megalosaurus
Inner alveolar ridge of jaw not more developed than in modern Varani, with no rudiments of alveolar divisions
Bases of teeth anchylosed to the outer wall and completely exposed on the inner side of the jaw
Ramus compressed, scarcely 2 lines across at thickest part, with exterior surface smooth and polished, impressed by fine longitudinal linear markings

species.name: Nuthetes destructor
species.etymology: From Latin 'destructor' meaning 'destroyer', a reference to the adaptations of the teeth for piercing, cutting, and lacerating prey.

Obelignathus.etymology: Named for Obelix, the fictional character from the Asterix and Obelix cartoon, combined with Greek 'gnathos' meaning 'jaw'; refers to the robust morphology of the holotype dentary likened to the strength of that character.
Obelignathus.description: Obelignathus is an extinct genus of rhabdodontomorph ornithopod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous 'Grès à Reptiles' Formation of France. The genus contains a single species, O. septimanicus, known from a right dentary. The species was initially classified as a species of the coeval Rhabdodon.

Absence of buccal platform lateral to alveolar row
Absence of horizontal buccal crest due to poorly developed anterolateral ridge of coronoid process
Coronoid process placed directly posterior to alveolar row, not laterally separated
Coronoid process rotated lateroposteriorly; lateral and coronoid surfaces face more posteriorly and anteriorly respectively
Meckelian canal mediolaterally and dorsoventrally deep, reaching 50% of dentary height (vs. 22-38% in other rhabdodontomorphs)

Oblitosaurus.etymology: From Latin 'oblitus' (forgotten or obsolete) and Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'forgotten lizard', referring to how its fossils were long overlooked.
Oblitosaurus.description: Oblitosaurus is a genus of ankylopollexian ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Villar del Arzobispo Formation of Spain. The type species is Oblitosaurus bunnueli.

Metatarsal IV with sub-triangular or ellipsoid proximal articulation facet

Oceanotitan.etymology: From Latin 'oceanus' meaning 'ocean', because the fossil was found at the base of a coastal cliff overlooking the Atlantic Ocean, combined with 'Titan' from Greek mythology meaning 'giant'.
Oceanotitan.description: Oceanotitan is a genus of sauropod dinosaur known from the Upper Jurassic (latest Kimmeridgian stage, about 149 million years ago) Lourinhã Formation of Portugal. It is represented by a single specimen consisting of several tail vertebrae and appendicular bones. It contains one species, Oceanotitan dantasi. Oceanotitan is classified as possibly one of the earliest members of the Somphospondyli, a group of sauropods that includes the titanosaurs.

Lateral depressions on distal tips of anterior to middle caudal neural spines, dorsally connected posteriorly
Anterior caudal vertebrae with medial accessory articulation on prezygapophysis
Transverse furrow on chevron articulations

Ischium shorter than pubis

Ohmdenosaurus.etymology: Named after the village of Ohmden in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, near where the specimen was found, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Ohmden lizard'
Ohmdenosaurus.description: Ohmdenosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Early Jurassic epoch in what is now Germany. The only specimen - a tibia (shinbone) and ankle - was discovered in rocks of the Posidonia Shale near the village of Ohmden. The specimen, which was originally identified as a plesiosaur, is exhibited in a local museum, the Urweltmuseum Hauff. In the 1970s, it caught the attention of German paleontologist Rupert Wild, who recognized it as the remains of a sauropod. Wild named Ohmdenosaurus in a 1978 publication; the only known species is Ohmdenosaurus liasicus.

Ojoceratops.description: Ojoceratops is a genus of ceratopsian dinosaur which lived in what is now New Mexico, United States. Ojoceratops fossils have been recovered from strata of the Ojo Alamo Formation (Naashoibito Member), dating to the late Cretaceous period (late Maastrichtian age, 66 million years ago). The type species is Ojoceratops fowleri.

Ojoraptorsaurus.etymology: Combines a reference to the Ojo Alamo Formation (where it was found) with Latin raptor ('plunderer') and Latinised Greek sauros ('lizard'); meaning 'Ojo Alamo plunderer lizard'
Ojoraptorsaurus.description: Ojoraptorsaurus is a dubious genus of oviraptorosaurian dinosaur from the late Cretaceous. Ojoraptorsaurus is only known from pubic bones found at the Naashoibito Member of the Ojo Alamo Formation dating to the late Maastrichtian, about 66 million years ago. It was first named by Robert M. Sullivan, Steven E. Jasinski and Mark P.A. van Tomme in 2011 and the type species is Ojoraptorsaurus boerei. The generic name combines a reference to the formation with a Latin raptor, "plunderer", and a Latinised Greek saurus, "lizard". The specific name honors oceanographer Arjan Boeré who found the specimen.

Oksoko.etymology: From Öksökö, a mythical two-headed bird in Yakut (Sakha) folklore of Siberia
Oksoko.description: Oksoko is a genus of oviraptorid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Nemegt Formation of Omnogov Province, Mongolia. The type and only species is Oksoko avarsan. It is notable for having only two functional fingers, having lost the third manual digit, suggesting a trend toward digit reduction within oviraptorosaurs.

Olorotitan.etymology: From Latin olor ('swan'), referencing the swan-like elongated neck and crest of this hadrosaur, combined with Greek Titan (a giant); meaning 'giant swan'
Olorotitan.description: Olorotitan is a monotypic genus of lambeosaurine duck-billed dinosaur, containing a single species, O. arharensis. It was among the last non-avian dinosaurs to go extinct during the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event, having lived from the middle to late Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period. The remains were found in the Udurchukan Formation beds of Kundur, Arkharinsky District, Amur Oblast, Eastern Russia, in the vicinity of the Amur River.

Oohkotokia.etymology: From Blackfoot 'ooh'kotoka' meaning 'large stone' and Latin suffix '-ia' meaning 'derived from', giving the meaning 'child of stone', referring to its extensive body armor; the name also honors the Blackfoot people on whose land the specimen was found.
Oohkotokia.description: Oohkotokia is a genus of ankylosaurid dinosaur within the subfamily Ankylosaurinae. It is known from the upper levels of the Two Medicine Formation (late Campanian stage, about 74 Ma ago) of Montana, United States. The discovery of Oohkotokia supports that Ankylosaurine dinosaurs existed and flourished continuously in Montana and/or Alberta throughout the late Campanian and early Maastrichtian stages in the Late Cretaceous period. It was a large, heavily built, quadrupedal, herbivore, that could grow up to 5 meters (16 ft) long and weigh up to 2 metric tons (2.2 short tons).

Opisthocoelicaudia.etymology: From Greek 'opisthen' (behind/posterior), 'koilos' (hollow), Latin 'cauda' (tail), and Latin '-ia' (suffix); meaning 'hollow-backed tail', referring to the opisthocoelouos (posteriorly hollowed) tail vertebrae.
Opisthocoelicaudia.description: Opisthocoelicaudia is a genus of sauropod dinosaur of the Late Cretaceous Period discovered in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia. The type species is Opisthocoelicaudia skarzynskii. A well-preserved skeleton lacking only the head and neck was unearthed in 1965 by Polish and Mongolian scientists, making Opisthocoelicaudia one of the best known sauropods from the Late Cretaceous. Tooth marks on this skeleton indicate that large carnivorous dinosaurs had fed on the carcass and possibly had carried away the now-missing parts. To date, only two additional, much less complete specimens are known, including part of a shoulder and a fragmentary tail. A relatively small sauropod, Opisthocoelicaudia measured about 11.4-13 m (37-43 ft) in length. Like other sauropods, it would have been characterized by a small head sitting on a very long neck and a barrel shaped trunk carried by four column-like legs. The name Opisthocoelicaudia means "posterior cavity tail", alluding to the unusual, opisthocoel condition of the anterior tail vertebrae that were concave on their posterior sides. This and other skeletal features lead researchers to propose that Opisthocoelicaudia was able to rear on its hindlegs.

Oplosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'hoplon' (weapon or armor) and 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'armed or weapon lizard' or 'armored lizard'.
Oplosaurus.description: Oplosaurus was a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous (Barremian stage) Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight, England. It is known from a single tooth usually referred to the contemporaneous "wastebasket taxon" Pelorosaurus, although there is no solid evidence for this.

Orkoraptor.etymology: From Aoniken 'Orr-Korr', the local name for the La Leona River near the fossil site, combined with Latin 'raptor' meaning 'thief'; translates as 'Toothed River thief'.
Orkoraptor.description: Orkoraptor is a genus of medium-sized megaraptoran theropod dinosaur from the late Cretaceous Period of Argentina. It is known from incomplete fossil remains including parts of the skull, teeth, tail vertebrae, and a partial tibia. The specialized teeth resemble those of some maniraptoriform theropods, namely the deinonychosaurs and compsognathids. This and other anatomical features led the authors who described it (Novas, Ezcurra, and Lecuona) to suggest that it was a maniraptoran coelurosaur. However, subsequent studies found it to be a megaraptoran. Found in the Cerro Fortaleza Formation of Southern Patagonia, it is one of the southernmost carnivorous dinosaurs known from South America.

Median depression flanked by two longitudinal and narrow furrows on lingual tooth surface (autapomorphy)
Postorbital with wide jugal process and obtuse orbital margin devoid of suborbital flange

Ornitholestes.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'ornis' (bird) and 'lestes' (robber); meaning 'bird robber'.
Ornitholestes.description: Ornitholestes is a small theropod dinosaur of the late Jurassic (Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation, middle Kimmeridgian age, about 154 million years ago) of Western Laurasia (the area that was to become North America).

Ornithomimoides.etymology: From Greek 'ornis' (bird), 'mimos' (mimic), and '-oides' (resembling); meaning 'bird mimic-like', indicating resemblance to ornithomimosaurs.
Ornithomimoides.description: Ornithomimoides is a dubious genus of theropod dinosaur, from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian stage, sometime between 70 and 66 mya) Lameta Formation of India. Two species have been identified, the type species O. mobilis and O. barasimlensis, were named by von Huene in 1932 and were described by Matley in 1933 though they are known only from isolated vertebrae. O. barasimlensis is known from five dorsal vertebrae, and O. mobilis from four smaller vertebrae, found at the same location.

Ornithomimus.description: Ornithomimus is a genus of ornithomimid theropod dinosaurs from the Campanian and Maastrichtian ages of the Late Cretaceous in western North America. Ornithomimus was a swift, bipedal dinosaur which was covered in feathers and equipped with a small toothless beak that may indicate an omnivorous diet. It is usually classified into two species: the type species, Ornithomimus velox, and a referred species, Ornithomimus edmontonicus.

Ornithopsis.etymology: From Greek 'ornis' (bird) and 'opsis' (likeness or appearance); meaning 'bird-likeness'.
Ornithopsis.description: Ornithopsis is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of England and possibly Germany. The type species, which is the only species seen as valid today, is O. hulkei, which is only known from fragmentary remains.

Oryctodromeus.etymology: From Ancient Greek 'oruktēs' meaning 'digger' and 'dromaios' meaning 'runner'; translates as 'digging runner', reflecting its unique status as the first non-avian dinosaur with evidence of burrowing behavior.
Oryctodromeus.description: Oryctodromeus is an extinct genus of small orodromine thescelosaurid dinosaur. Fossils are known from the Late Cretaceous Blackleaf Formation of southwestern Montana and the Wayan Formation of southeastern Idaho, USA, both of the Cenomanian stage, roughly 105-96 million years ago. A member of the small, presumably fast-running herbivorous family Thescelosauridae, Oryctodromeus is the first non-avian dinosaur published that shows evidence of burrowing behavior.

Ouranosaurus.etymology: From Tuareg 'ouranou' meaning 'brave' or 'valiant' (the local name for the monitor lizard) and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', giving the meaning 'brave lizard' or 'valiant lizard'.
Ouranosaurus.description: Ouranosaurus is a genus of herbivorous basal hadrosauriform dinosaur that lived during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous of modern-day Niger and Cameroon. Ouranosaurus measured about 7-8.3 meters (23-27 ft) long and weighed 2.2 metric tons (2.4 short tons). Two rather complete fossils were found in the Elrhaz Formation, Gadoufaoua deposits, Agadez, Niger, in 1965 and 1970, with a third indeterminate specimen known from the Koum Formation of Cameroon. The animal was named in 1976 by French paleontologist Philippe Taquet, the type species being Ouranosaurus nigeriensis. The generic name is a combination of ourane, a word with multiple meanings, and sauros, the Greek word for lizard. The specific epithet nigeriensis alludes to Niger, its country of discovery (in Latin, the adjectival suffix -iensis means "originating from"). As such, Ouranosaurus nigeriensis could be interpreted as "brave lizard originating from Niger".

Oviraptor.etymology: From Latin ovum ('egg') and raptor ('thief'), meaning 'egg thief', based on the initial (later revised) interpretation that it was stealing eggs
Oviraptor.description: Oviraptor is a genus of oviraptorid dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period. The first remains were collected from the Djadokhta Formation of Mongolia in 1923 during a paleontological expedition led by Roy Chapman Andrews, and in the following year the genus and type species Oviraptor philoceratops were named by Henry Fairfield Osborn. The genus name refers to the initial thought of egg-stealing habits, and the specific name was intended to reinforce this view indicating a preference over ceratopsian eggs. Despite the fact that numerous specimens have been referred to the genus, Oviraptor is only known from a single partial skeleton regarded as the holotype, as well as a nest of about fifteen eggs and several small fragments from a juvenile.

Pachycephalosaurus.etymology: From Greek pachys (παχύς, 'thick'), kephalon (κεφαλή, 'head'), and sauros (σαῦρος, 'lizard'), meaning 'thick-headed lizard'
Pachycephalosaurus.description: Pachycephalosaurus is a genus of pachycephalosaurid ornithischian dinosaur. The type species, P. wyomingensis, is the only known definitive species. The possibly synonymous taxon, Stygimoloch, might represent a distinct genus or a second species, P. spinifer. It lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period in what is now western North America. Remains have been excavated in Montana, South Dakota, Wyoming, and Alberta. Mainly known from a single skull and a few extremely thick skull roofs (at 22 cm (8.7 in) thick), Pachycephalosaurus is estimated to have reached 4.5 m (15 ft) long and weighed 370-450 kg (820-990 lb). More complete fossils would come to be found in the following years.
