Panoplosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'panoplos' meaning 'fully armored' or 'well-armored' and '-saurus' meaning 'lizard', referring to its extensive armor plating.
Panoplosaurus.description: Panoplosaurus is a genus of armored dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Alberta, Canada. Few specimens of the genus are known, all from the middle Campanian of the Dinosaur Park Formation, roughly 76 to 75 million years ago. It was first discovered in 1917, and named in 1919 by Lawrence Lambe, named for its extensive armor, meaning "well-armored lizard". Panoplosaurus has at times been considered the proper name for material otherwise referred to as Edmontonia, complicating its phylogenetic and ecological interpretations, at one point being considered to have existed across Alberta, New Mexico and Texas, with specimens in institutions from Canada and the United States. The skull and skeleton of Panoplosaurus are similar to its relatives, but have a few significant differences, such as the lumpy form of the skull osteoderms, a completely fused shoulder blade, and regularly shaped plates on its neck and body lacking prominent spines. It was a quadrupedal animal, roughly 5 m (16 ft) long and 1,600 kg (3,500 lb) in weight. The skull has a short snout, with a very domed surface, and bony plates directly covering the cheek. The neck had circular groups of plates arranged around the top surface, both the forelimb and hindlimb were about the same length, and the hand may have only included three fingers. Almost the entire surface of the body was covered in plates, osteoderms and scutes of varying sizes, ranging from large elements along the skull and neck, to smaller, round bones underneath the chin and body, to small ossicles that filled in the spaces between other, larger osteoderms.

Dorsal neck armor formed by transversely paired, low-keeled plate-like scutes in a longitudinal series
Principal lateral scutes of neck and trunk strongly keeled, arranged in longitudinal rows

Panphagia.etymology: From Greek 'pan' meaning 'all' and 'phagein' meaning 'to eat', referring to its interpreted omnivorous diet as a basal sauropodomorph.
Panphagia.description: Panphagia is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur described in 2009. It lived around 231 million years ago, during the Carnian age of the Late Triassic period in what is now northwestern Argentina. Fossils of the genus were found in the La Peña Member of the Ischigualasto Formation in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin. The name Panphagia comes from the Greek words pan, meaning "all", and phagein, meaning "to eat", in reference to its inferred omnivorous diet. Panphagia is one of the earliest known dinosaurs, and is an important find which may mark the transition of diet in early sauropodomorph dinosaurs.

Paralititan.etymology: From Greek parali (tidal, of the sea) and titan (giant); meaning "tidal giant".
Paralititan.description: Paralititan is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in present-day Egypt during the Late Cretaceous period. It was described by American paleontologist Joshua B. Smith and colleagues in 2001. The genus contains a single species, Paralititan stromeri, named based on a fragmentary skeleton including vertebrae and limb bones. These fossils were unearthed by an American expedition to the Bahariya Oasis in western Egypt in rock layers of the Bahariya Formation. This formation dates to the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, which lasted 101 to 94 million years ago. An incomplete dorsal (back) vertebra that had been described by German paleontologist Ernst Stromer in 1932 was also assigned to Paralititan. However, this vertebra had been destroyed during the Bombing of Munich in World War II.

Pararhabdodon.etymology: From Greek 'para' meaning 'near' or 'beside' combined with the genus name Rhabdodon (meaning 'fluted tooth'); translates as 'near fluted tooth', indicating its close relationship to Rhabdodon.
Pararhabdodon.description: Pararhabdodon is a genus of tsintaosaurin hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Maastrichtian-aged (Late Cretaceous) Tremp Group of Spain. The first remains were discovered from the Sant Romà d'Abella fossil locality and assigned to the genus Rhabdodon, and later named as the distinct species Pararhabdodon isonensis in 1993. Known material includes assorted postcranial remains, mostly vertebrae, as well as maxillae from the skull. Specimens from other sites, including remains from France, a maxilla previously considered the distinct taxon Koutalisaurus kohlerorum, an additional maxilla from another locality, the material assigned to the genera Blasisaurus and Arenysaurus, and the extensive Basturs Poble bonebed have been considered at different times to belong to the species, but all of these assignments have more recently been questioned. It was one of the last non-avian dinosaurs known from the fossil record that went extinct during the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event.

Parasaurolophus.etymology: From Greek para (beside, near) and the genus name Saurolophus (crested lizard); meaning "beside crested lizard", reflecting Parks's view that the new genus's affinities lay with Saurolophus from the Edmonton Formation.
Parasaurolophus.description: Parasaurolophus is one of the most recognizable lambeosaurine hadrosaurs, distinguished by an elongate hollow cranial crest formed of paired tubes of nasal and frontal that project well posterior to the occiput. Parks erected the genus in 1922 on a skull and partial articulated skeleton (ROM 768) collected by a University of Toronto expedition in 1920 from the Belly River beds of the Red Deer River, Alberta — strata now assigned to the lower Dinosaur Park Formation. Parks himself raised the question of whether the hollow tubes carried air, anticipating the long-running interpretation that the crest housed elongated nasal passages and may have functioned as a resonating chamber for vocal display. Three further species are recognized today — P. tubicen and P. cyrtocristatus from the San Juan Basin and Kaiparowits regions of the southwestern United States, and the disputed Asian P. jiayinensis (often referred to its own genus, Charonosaurus). Material remains rare across the entire range, and Evans, Bavington and Campione (2009) documented that even the Alberta type material likely represents a subadult, with the crest not yet at its fully developed adult expression.
diagnostic_features: Elongate, posteriorly directed hollow tubular cranial crest formed of nasal and frontal, length on the order of 875 mm from the postorbital notch in the holotype.
Crest interior comprises four parallel thin-walled bony tubes continuous with the external nares.
Lachrymal positioned far anteriorly and excluded from the orbital rim, overlapping the maxillary.
Frontal sutural surface for the nasal thickened and steeply angled, extending along the base of the crest and overhanging the supratemporal fenestra.
Frontal contribution to the dorsal skull roof severely reduced or absent posterior to the base of the crest.
Anteriorly extended pubic peduncle of the ilium strongly decurved distally and forming an externally overlapping joint with the pubis.
Cervical postzygapophyses on vertebrae 8-13 strongly elongate and curved ventrally, reaching ~110 mm in length.

Paraxenisaurus.etymology: From Greek para (near, beside) and xenos (strange) and sauros (lizard); meaning "strange lizard".
Paraxenisaurus.description: Paraxenisaurus is an extinct genus of ornithomimosaurian theropod from the Late Cretaceous Cerro del Pueblo Formation of Coahuila in Mexico. The genus contains a single species, P. normalensis, which is known from a few bones of tail, hips, hands, and feet. The specific epithet was given in honor of the Benemérita Normal School of Coahuila, a teacher training institution, where the fossils were reposited. It is a member of the family Deinocheiridae and is the only member of that clade known from Laramidia.

Parksosaurus.etymology: Named after Canadian paleontologist William A. Parks, who discovered the specimen, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Parks's lizard'
Parksosaurus.description: Parksosaurus is a genus of neornithischian dinosaur from the early Maastrichtian-aged (Upper Cretaceous) Horseshoe Canyon Formation of Alberta, Canada. It is based on most of a partially articulated skeleton and partial skull, showing it to have been a small, bipedal, herbivorous dinosaur. It is one of the few described non-hadrosaurid ornithopods from the end of the Cretaceous in North America, existing around 70 million years ago.

Patagonykus.etymology: Named for Patagonia, the region of Argentina where it was found, combined with Greek 'onyx' meaning 'claw'; translates as 'Patagonian claw'.
Patagonykus.description: Patagonykus is a genus of alvarezsauroid theropod dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of Argentina. It was discovered in exposures of the Portezuelo Formation (Turonian-Coniacian) of the Rio Neuquén Subgroup in the Neuquén Basin, Neuquén Province. The holotype consists of an incomplete but well-preserved skeleton, lacking a skull, but including many vertebrae, the coracoids, a partial forelimb, pelvic girdle, and hindlimbs. Patagonykus has been classed with the Alvarezsauridae, a family which includes such taxa as the Mongolian Mononykus and the also Argentinian Alvarezsaurus. In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at 1 meter (3.3 ft) and its weight at 3.5 kilograms (7.7 lb).

Patagopelta.etymology: Named after Patagonia, the region in Argentina where it was found, combined with Latin pelta (shield); meaning "Patagonian shield".
Patagopelta.description: Patagopelta is an extinct genus of ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (upper Campanian-lower Maastrichtian) Allen Formation of Argentina. The genus contains a single species, P. cristata, known from several partial skeletons, isolated bones, and osteoderms. While originally described as a member of the family Nodosauridae, later discoveries provided support for parankylosaurian affinities. Patagopelta is a small armored dinosaur, comparable in size to the 'dwarf' nodosaurid Struthiosaurus, at about 2 m (6.6 ft) long. It is larger, more robust, and more heavily armored than other paranklyosaurs such as Stegouros.

Patagosaurus.etymology: Named for Patagonia, the region of Argentina where it was found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; translates as 'Patagonia lizard'.
Patagosaurus.description: Patagosaurus is an extinct genus of eusauropod dinosaur from the middle Toarcian of Patagonia, Argentina. It was first found in deposits of the Cañadón Asfalto Formation, which date to around 178 million years ago. Although originally twelve specimens were assigned to the taxon, at least one of them may belong to a different genus. Patagosaurus probably lived alongside genera such as Piatnitzkysaurus, Condorraptor, and Volkheimeria.

Sacrum with 5 vertebrae, elevated neural spines, and large dilation of the neural canal forming a neural cavity.
Pelvis with pubis showing distal and proximolateral expansions more developed than in Barapasaurus, and less expanded pubic symphysis than in Amygdalodon.
Ischium slightly transversely compressed with ventromedial ridge of sublaminar type and clear distal expansion.
Tibia-femur length ratio of 1:1.5 in juveniles, reaching 1:1.7 in adults.

Patagotitan.etymology: Named for Patagonia, the region of Argentina where it was discovered, combined with Greek 'titan' meaning 'giant', referencing its enormous size.
Patagotitan.description: Patagotitan is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Albian stage) Cerro Barcino Formation in Chubut Province, Patagonia, Argentina. The genus contains a single species known from at least six young adult individuals, Patagotitan mayorum, which was first announced in 2014 and then named in 2017 by José Carballido and colleagues. Originally thought to be the largest known titanosaur and land animal overall, preliminary studies and press releases suggested that Patagotitan had an estimated length of 37 m (121 ft) and an estimated weight of 69 tonnes (76 short tons). Later research revised the length estimate down to 31 m (102 ft) and weight estimates down to approximately 50-60 tonnes (55-66 short tons), suggesting that Patagotitan was of a similar size to, if not smaller than, its closest relatives Argentinosaurus and Puertasaurus. Still, Patagotitan is one of the best-known titanosaurs, and so its interrelationships with other titanosaurs have been relatively consistent in phylogenetic analyses. This led to its use in a re-definition of the group Colossosauria by Carballido and colleagues in 2022.

Paulodon.etymology: Named in honor of iguanodont researcher Gregory S. Paul, plus Greek odon ("tooth") in keeping with the Iguanodontia naming convention.
Paulodon.description: Paulodon is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur from the early Barremian (Early Cretaceous) of Galve in Teruel, Spain. It was erected by Sancarlo, Mandorlo and Ford (2025) for material previously described as Iguanodon galvensis by Verdú et al. (2015).
Paulodon.dispute: Paleontologists have informally disagreed with the methodology behind Sancarlo et al.'s 2025 erection of Paulodon. An independent 2026 study by Rotatori et al. concluded that "I." galvensis requires a new generic name within Iguanodontidae, but did not mention or endorse Paulodon — leaving the taxonomic situation unresolved.

Rugose, inflated ridge on the lateral side of the femur shaft near the lateral condyle.

Prominent tuberosity on the articular surface of the iliac peduncle of the ischium.
Ischiatic peduncle forms a step on the lateral face of the ilium.
Distal end of the ischium D-shaped in cross section, with a rounded expansion 0.45-0.50 the proximal width.
Dentary with a short, abrupt convexity on the dorsal margin near the symphyseal region.

It is possibly older than Archaeopteryx, though the age of the Daohugou Beds where it was found is debated. A majority of studies suggest that the beds probably date from between the late Middle Jurassic (168 million years ago) and early Late Jurassic Period (164-152 million years ago).

Pegomastax.etymology: From Greek pego- (πηγός, 'strong' or 'stout') and mastax (μάσταξ, 'jaw' or 'mouth'), meaning 'strong jaw', referring to its robust lower jaw
Pegomastax.description: Pegomastax is a genus of heterodontosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Early Jurassic of South Africa. The only known specimen was discovered in a 1966-1967 expedition in Transkei District of Cape Province, but was not described until 2012 when Paul Sereno named it as the new taxon Pegomastax africana. The genus name is derived from the Greek for "strong jaw", and the species name describes the provenance of Africa; it was originally spelled africanus, was corrected to africana to align with the gender of the genus name.

Pelecanimimus.description: Pelecanimimus is an extinct genus of basal ("primitive") ornithomimosaurian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Spain. It is notable for possessing more teeth than any other member of the Ornithomimosauria (or any other theropod), most of which were toothless.

Pelorosaurus.etymology: From Greek pelor ("monster") and sauros ("lizard"); meaning "monstrous lizard". Mantell explicitly chose the name to indicate the enormous magnitude of the type humerus.
Pelorosaurus.description: Pelorosaurus is a genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur. Remains referred to Pelorosaurus date from the Early Cretaceous period, about 140-125 million years ago, and have been found in England. Thomas Holtz estimated its length at 24 m (79 ft). The name Pelorosaurus was one of the first to be given to any sauropod. Many species have been assigned to the genus historically, but most are currently considered to belong to other genera. Problematically, the first named species of Pelorosaurus, P. conybeari, is a junior synonym of Cetiosaurus brevis (now Pelorosaurus brevis).

Anterior caudal vertebrae with subquadrangular articulating facets and notably short antero-posterior diameter relative to transverse and vertical diameters
Neural arch anchylosed to anterior half of centrum only, leaving posterior part of upper surface of body uncovered
Anterior oblique processes project directly forwards over the body of the adjacent vertebra; posterior oblique processes absent, replaced by depressions on the spinous process
Distal caudal vertebra with chevron bone (haemapophysis) anchylosed (confluent) to the centrum rather than articulated by distinct facets

The replacement Pelorosaurus appeared in Mantell (1850); Colossosaurus was never validly published.

Pendraig.description: Pendraig is a genus of coelophysoid theropod dinosaur from South Wales. It contains one species, Pendraig milnerae, named after Angela Milner. The specimen was discovered in the Pant-y-Ffynnon quarry. In life it would have measured 1 m (3.3 ft) in length.

Pentaceratops.etymology: From Greek 'pente' meaning 'five', 'keras' meaning 'horn', and 'ops' meaning 'face'; translates as 'five-horned face', referring to the five horn-like projections on its skull.
Pentaceratops.description: Pentaceratops is a genus of herbivorous ceratopsid dinosaur from the late Cretaceous Period of what is now North America. Fossils of this animal were first discovered in 1921, but the genus was named in 1923 when its type species, Pentaceratops sternbergii, was described. Pentaceratops lived around 76-73 million years ago, its remains having been mostly found in the Kirtland Formation in the San Juan Basin in New Mexico. Another species, P. aquilonius, was named by Nick W. Longrich in 2014, but it is debated if it belongs to that genus or a separate taxon. About a dozen skulls and skeletons have been uncovered, so anatomical understanding of Pentaceratops is fairly complete. One exceptionally large specimen later became its own genus, Titanoceratops, due to its more derived morphology, similarities to Triceratops, and lack of unique characteristics shared with Pentaceratops.

Petrobrasaurus.etymology: Named after Petrobras, the Brazilian state oil company that operated in the region where the fossil was found, combined with Greek sauros meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Petrobras lizard'
Petrobrasaurus.description: Petrobrasaurus is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur. It is a titanosaur which lived during the upper Cretaceous period (Coniacian-Santonian age) in what is now Rincón de los Sauces, Patagonia, Argentina. It is known from the holotype MAU-Pv-PH-449 - a partial disarticulated skeleton recovered from the Plottier Formation (Neuquén Basin), Argentina. This genus was named by Leonardo S. Filippi, José Ignacio Canudo, Leonardo J. Salgado, Alberto C. Garrido, Rodolfo A. Garcia, Ignacio A. Cerda and Alejandro Otero in 2011, and the type species is Petrobrasaurus puestohernandezi. The generic name is derived from "Petrobras" (oil company) and saurus, "lizard". The specific name refers to the Puesto Hernández oil field, where the fossil remains were found.

Phuwiangosaurus.etymology: Named after the Phu Wiang area of Thailand where the fossil was discovered, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "Phu Wiang lizard".
Phuwiangosaurus.description: Phuwiangosaurus is a genus of titanosauriform dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Valanginian-Hauterivian) Sao Khua Formation of Thailand. The type species, P. sirindhornae, was described by Martin, Buffetaut, and Suteethorn in a 1993 press release and was formally named in 1994. The species was named to honor Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn of Thailand, who was interested in the geology and paleontology of Thailand, while the genus was named after the Phu Wiang area, where the fossil was discovered. The precise affinities of Phuwiangosaurus among titanosauriform sauropods are uncertain, though several studies have classified it as a euhelopodid.

Hyposphene-hypantrum system present
Femur flattened anteroposteriorly with fourth trochanter crest-shaped, located medially above midlength of shaft
Very developed lateral epicondyle at distal end of femur

Phyllodon.etymology: From Greek 'phyllon' meaning 'leaf' and 'odon' meaning 'tooth'; translates as 'leaf tooth', named for the leaf-shaped teeth.
Phyllodon.description: Phyllodon is a genus of small ornithischian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian) Camadas de Guimarota Formation of Leiria, Portugal and possibly also the Middle Jurassic (Bathonian) Chipping Norton Limestone of England. It may have been closely related to contemporaneous ornithischian dinosaurs from North America. This genus is known from teeth and possibly partial lower jaws. The name is also in use for a genus of modern moss, but this is not considered to be a problem because the two organisms are in two different kingdoms.
diagnostic_features: Tooth crowns fully and uniformly enamelled, bucco-lingually compressed, and higher than long along the entire tooth row.
Anterior premaxillary crowns broadly triangular, weakly recurved, without definite marginal denticles; distal margin straight and sharp.
Posterior premaxillary crowns with small denticles on mesial margin appearing before distal margin — unique among hypsilophodontids (reverse of all other known genera).
Cheek crowns lozenge-shaped with bluntly rounded marginal denticles deflected to the rear; largest denticles near crown mid-height, decreasing toward cervix and occlusal tip.
Occlusal tip of cheek crown formed by a cluster of several small denticles (not a single large denticle as in relatives).
Cingula absent; some cheek crowns bear a few small denticles at the postero-internal (lingual) margin only.

Pilmatueia.etymology: Named after the Pilmatué locality in Neuquén Province, Argentina, where the fossils were discovered.
Pilmatueia.description: Pilmatueia is a genus of diplodocoid sauropods belonging to the family Dicraeosauridae that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now Argentina. Its type and only species is Pilmatueia faundezi. Pilmatueia was probably closely related to other South American dicraeosaurids such as Amargasaurus. Like other dicraeosaurids, Pilmatueia was relatively small for a sauropod. The vertebrae of Pilmatueia were more extensively hollowed out by air sacs than in other dicraeosaurids, which otherwise were characterized by a reduction in the air sac system compared to other sauropods. Pilmatueia dates to the Valanginian, an age of the Cretaceous period for which dinosaur faunas are poorly known.

Pisanosaurus.etymology: Named in honor of Argentine paleontologist Juan Pisano (Museo de La Plata), with Greek 'sauros' (lizard); meaning 'Pisano's lizard'.
Pisanosaurus.description: Pisanosaurus is an extinct genus of early dinosauriform, likely an ornithischian or silesaurid, from the Late Triassic of Argentina. It was a small, lightly built, ground-dwelling herbivore, that could grow up to an estimated 1 m (3.3 ft) long. Only one species, the type, Pisanosaurus mertii, is known, based on a single partial skeleton discovered in the Ischigualasto Formation of the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin in northwestern Argentina. This part of the formation has been dated to the late Carnian, approximately 229 million years ago.

Plateosaurus.etymology: From Greek platys (broad, flat) and sauros (lizard); probably meaning "broad lizard" (often mistranslated as "flat lizard").
Plateosaurus.description: Plateosaurus is a genus of plateosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Triassic epoch of the Triassic period, around 214 to 204 million years ago, in what is now Central and Northern Europe. Plateosaurus is a basal (early) sauropodomorph dinosaur, a so-called "prosauropod". The type species is Plateosaurus trossingensis; before 2019, that honor was given to Plateosaurus engelhardti, but it was ruled as undiagnostic (i.e. indistinguishable from other dinosaurs) by the ICZN. Currently, there are three valid species; in addition to P. trossingensis, P. longiceps and P. gracilis are also known. However, others have been assigned in the past, and there is no broad consensus on the species taxonomy of plateosaurid dinosaurs. Similarly, there are a plethora of synonyms (invalid duplicate names) at the genus level.

Pneumatoraptor.etymology: From Greek 'pneuma' meaning 'air' or 'breath', combined with Latin 'raptor' meaning 'thief', likely referring to pneumatic (air-filled) features in the bones.
Pneumatoraptor.description: Pneumatoraptor is a genus of small paravian, possibly a dromaeosaurid, dinosaur that lived in Hungary. It is known from a single complete left shoulder girdle (scapulocoracoid) found in the Csehbánya Formation of the Iharkút locality in the Bakony Mountains of western Hungary. This formation dates to the late Cretaceous period (Santonian age) about 85 million years ago.
diagnostic_features: Large, circular pneumatic foramen (2 mm diameter) located ventral to the coracoid foramen, opening towards the coracoid tubercle.
Pneumatic foramen connects to the hollow interior of the scapular blade, as confirmed by cross-section during preparation.
Scapulocoracoid is L-shaped with a deeply concave glenoid fossa oriented laterally and slightly ventrally.
Coracoid displays a prominent reverse flexure of approximately 70° between its glenoid portion and the ventral coracoid blade.
Coracoid foramen forms an almost anteroposteriorly oriented canal.

Podokesaurus.etymology: From Greek podoces (πόδας ὠκύς, podas okys, 'swift-footed'), meaning 'swift-footed lizard', referring to its presumed agility
Podokesaurus.description: Podokesaurus is a genus of coelophysoid dinosaur that lived in what is now the eastern United States during the Early Jurassic Period. The first fossil was discovered by the geologist Mignon Talbot near Mount Holyoke, Massachusetts, in 1910. The specimen was fragmentary, preserving much of the body, limbs, and tail. In 1911, Talbot described and named the new genus and species Podokesaurus holyokensis based on it. The full name can be translated as "swift-footed lizard of Holyoke". This discovery made Talbot the first woman to find and describe a non-bird dinosaur. The holotype fossil was recognized as significant and was studied by other researchers, but was lost when the building it was kept in burned down in 1917; no unequivocal Podokesaurus specimens have since been discovered. It was made state dinosaur of Massachusetts in 2022.
diagnostic_features: Femur slender and nearly straight with fourth trochanter at distal end, length greater than tibia only in larger forms
Tibia notably longer than femur with metatarsals over half tibia length, indicating rapid bipedal locomotion
Pubis remarkably long (95mm) and thin, expanded at distal end, angled 40° to vertebral column
Ischium with narrow uniform shaft, well-rounded anteriorly, lacking postpubis
Hollow, light skeletal construction including hollow vertebrae with transverse cavities and hollow ribs

Poekilopleuron.etymology: From Greek poikilos (varied, diverse) and pleuron (rib); meaning "varied ribs".
Poekilopleuron.description: Poekilopleuron is a genus of carnosaurian theropod dinosaur, which lived during the middle Bathonian of the Jurassic, about 168 to 166 million years ago. The genus has been used under many different spelling variants, although only one, Poekilopleuron, is valid. The type species is P. bucklandii, named after William Buckland, and many junior synonyms of it have also been erected. Little material is currently known, as the holotype was destroyed in World War II, although many casts of the material still exist.

Polacanthus.etymology: From Ancient Greek polys (πολύς, 'many') and akantha (ἄκανθα, 'thorn' or 'prickle'), meaning 'many thorns', referring to the numerous spikes on its body
Polacanthus.description: Polacanthus is an extinct genus of ankylosaurian dinosaurs from the early Cretaceous (130-125 million years ago) of England. Several species have been named in the genus Polacanthus, but only the type species, Polacanthus foxii, is currently seen as valid. There are not many fossil remains of this dinosaur, and some important anatomical features, such as its skull, are poorly known. It grew to about 4-5 meters (13-16 ft) long. Its body was covered with armor plates and spikes. It may be a basal member of the Nodosauridae or part of a separate family, the Polacanthidae.

Pradhania.etymology: Named in honor of Dhuiya Pradhan, a fossil collector at the Indian Statistical Institute who contributed to paleontological work in India
Pradhania.description: Pradhania is a genus of massospondylid sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Sinemurian-age (Early Jurassic) Upper Dharmaram Formation of India. It was first named by T. S. Kutty, Sankar Chatterjee, Peter M. Galton and Paul Upchurch in 2007 and the type species is Pradhania gracilis. It was a sauropodomorph of modest size, only about four meters (13 ft) long, and is known from fragmentary remains. It was originally regarded as a basal sauropodomorph but new cladistic analysis performed by Novas et al., 2011 suggests that Pradhania is a massospondylid. Pradhania presents two synapomorphies of Massospondylidae recovered in their phylogenetic analysis.

Prenocephale.etymology: From Greek 'prenes' (sloping, inclined) and 'kephalē' (head), referring to the anteriorly inclined profile of the highly domed cranium.
Prenocephale.description: Prenocephale is an extinct genus of pachycephalosaurid ornithischian dinosaur from the Maastrichtian Nemegt Formation of southern Mongolia. The type and only species, Prenocephale prenes, was erected by Maryańska & Osmólska (1974) on a nearly complete skull with associated postcranial fragments (ZPAL MgD-I/104) recovered from the Nemegt locality of the Gobi Desert; Evans et al. (2018) referred three additional cranial specimens from Bugiin Tsav, Guriliin Tsav, and Tsagaan Khushuu and presented the first cranial bone histology for any Asian pachycephalosaur, demonstrating that the holotype was probably a not-yet-fully-mature individual. Several Late Cretaceous North American species (P. brevis, P. edmontonensis, P. goodwini) formerly attributed to this genus have since been transferred to Sphaerotholus or Foraminacephale; the Asian type species P. prenes is uncontroversially valid, and Evans et al. (2018) explicitly rejected the proposed synonymy of Homalocephale calathocercos with P. prenes on the basis of consistently distinct squamosal-node morphologies.

Supratemporal fenestra completely closed; infratemporal fenestra short and broad.
Occipital region overhung by strongly swollen squamosals with a deeply depressed central part; row of conspicuous nodes along posterolateral and posterior skull margins.

Prenoceratops.etymology: From Greek prene- (πρηνή, 'bent forwards' or 'prone'), cerat- (κερατ-, 'horn'), and ops (ωψ, 'face'), meaning 'bent or prone-horned face'
Prenoceratops.description: Prenoceratops, (meaning 'bent or prone-horned face' and derived from Greek prene-/πρηνη- meaning 'bent forwards' or 'prone', cerat-/κερατ- meaning 'horn' and -ops/ωψ meaning 'face') is a genus of herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period. It was a relatively small dinosaur, reaching 1.3 m (4.3 ft) in length and 20 kg (44 lb) in body mass. Its fossils have been found in the upper Two Medicine Formation in the present-day U.S. state of Montana, in Campanian age rock layers that have been dated to 74.3 million years ago. Fossils were also found in the Oldman Formation in the modern day Canadian province of Alberta, dating to around 77 million years ago.

Priconodon.etymology: From Greek prion (saw), konos (cone), and odon (tooth); meaning "saw cone tooth".
Priconodon.description: Priconodon is an extinct genus of ankylosaurian dinosaur (perhaps nodosaurid), mainly known from its large teeth. Its remains have been found in the Early Cretaceous (Aptian-Albian age) Arundel Formation of Muirkirk, Prince George's County, Maryland, USA, and possibly the Potomac Group, also located in Maryland. As an ankylosaur, Priconodon would have been a large armored quadrupedal herbivore, though no size estimation has been done due to the scarcity of described remains.

Probrachylophosaurus.etymology: From Greek pro- (πρό, 'before' or 'ancestral to') prefixed to Brachylophosaurus, indicating a suspected ancestral relationship; meaning 'before Brachylophosaurus'
Probrachylophosaurus.description: Probrachylophosaurus is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in North America. Fossils have been found in rocks of the Judith River Formation in Montana and the Foremost Formation in Alberta, and date to the Campanian age, c. 80.45-79 million years ago. The only recognized species is Probrachylophosaurus bergei. First discovered in Montana in 1981 and not fully excavated until 2008, it was initially suspected to be a new species of Brachylophosaurus. However, in 2015 it was named as a distinct genus, with its name reflecting a suspected ancestral relationship. Both an adult and subadult specimen were originally recognized, and in 2021 fragmentary remains would extend its known range into the Foremost Formation. Thought to be a close relative of the later Brachylophosaurus and Ornatops, and a possible descendant of the older Acristavus, it represents a possible transitional state in brachylophosaurin evolution. Nonetheless, whether this represents a single evolutionary lineage or a series of diverging or convergent branches remains unclear, as does its relation to the genus Maiasaura.
diagnostic_features: Solid nasal crest consisting entirely of nasals, overhanging supratemporal fenestrae by less than 2 cm in adults
Nasal crest extremely dorsoventrally thickened medially with strongly triangular frontal plane cross section

Postcranial material includes cervical, dorsal, caudal vertebrae, chevrons, ribs, ilia, pubes, ischia, tibiae, fibulae, astragali, metatarsals. Forelimbs and sacral vertebrae absent.

Proceratosaurus.etymology: From Greek pro- (πρό, 'before' or 'precursor of') prefixed to Ceratosaurus, as it was originally thought to be closely related to or ancestral to Ceratosaurus; meaning 'before Ceratosaurus'
Proceratosaurus.description: Proceratosaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived during the Middle Jurassic in what is now England. The holotype and only known specimen consists of a mostly complete skull with an accompanying lower jaw and a hyoid bone, found near Minchinhampton, a town in Gloucestershire. It was originally described in 1910 as a species of Megalosaurus, M. bradleyi, but was moved to its own genus, Proceratosaurus, in 1926. The genus was named for its supposed close relationship with Ceratosaurus, later shown to be erroneous, due to perceived resemblance of Proceratosaurus's incomplete cranial crest to Ceratosaurus's nasal horn.

Procompsognathus was a small-sized, lightly built, ground-dwelling, bipedal carnivore, that could grow up to 1 m (3.3 ft) long.

Prodeinodon.etymology: From Greek pro (before) and the genus name Deinodon; meaning "before Deinodon".
Prodeinodon.description: Prodeinodon is a wastebasket taxon and a dubious genus of theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian to Aptian stages) from the Xinlong Formation in the Napai Basin of China and from the Oosh Formation of Mongolia. Two species have been formally identified (with a third informal species), all three known only from tooth fragments, showing no diagnostic features, making them difficult to classify, though they may belong to a carnosaur. At least some of the referred species may represent basal carcharodontosaurid theropods similar to Acrocanthosaurus.

Propanoplosaurus.description: Propanoplosaurus is a genus of herbivorous nodosaurid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Patuxent Formation of Maryland, USA. Its type specimen is a natural cast and partial natural mold of a hatchling.

Prosaurolophus.etymology: From Greek pro (before) and the genus name Saurolophus (crested lizard); meaning "before Saurolophus", referring to it being an earlier dinosaur with a similar head crest.
Prosaurolophus.description: Prosaurolophus is a genus of hadrosaurid (or duck-billed) dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North America. It is known from the remains of at least 25 individuals, including skulls and skeletons, but this remains obscure. Its fossils have been found in the late Campanian-aged Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta, and the roughly contemporaneous Two Medicine Formation in Montana, dating to around 75.7 to 74.1 million years ago. Its most recognizable feature is a small solid crest formed by the nasal bones, sticking up in front of the eyes.

Protarchaeopteryx.etymology: From Greek protos (before) and the genus name Archaeopteryx; meaning "before Archaeopteryx".
Protarchaeopteryx.description: Protarchaeopteryx is a genus of turkey-sized feathered theropod dinosaur from China. Known from the Jianshangou bed of the Yixian Formation, it lived during the early Aptian age of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 124.6 million years ago. It was probably a herbivore or omnivore, although its hands were very similar to those of small carnivorous dinosaurs. It appears to be one of the most basal members of the Oviraptorosauria, closely related to Incisivosaurus, or a taxon slightly less closely related to birds than oviraptorosaurs were.

Protathlitis.description: Protathlitis is a potentially dubious and chimeric genus of theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) Arcillas de Morella Formation of Castellón, Spain. The type and only species is Protathlitis cinctorrensis, known from a partial skeleton. It was originally identified as a basal member of the Baryonychinae. If a spinosaurid identity of the material is correct, its discovery, as well as those of the spinosaurids Camarillasaurus, Iberospinus, Riojavenatrix, and the contemporary Vallibonavenatrix shows that the Iberian Peninsula held a diverse assemblage of these theropods during the Early Cretaceous.

Protoavis.etymology: From Greek protos (first) and Latin avis (bird); meaning "first bird".
Protoavis.description: Protoavis is a problematic taxon known from fragmentary remains from Late Triassic Norian stage deposits near Post, Texas. The animal's true classification has been the subject of much controversy, and there are many different interpretations of what the taxon actually is. When it was first described, the fossils were described as being from a primitive bird which, if the identification is valid, would push back avian origins some 60-75 million years.

Protoceratops.etymology: From Greek protos (first) and keratops (horned face); meaning "first horned face", chosen by Granger and Gregory to reflect their interpretation of the genus as an early, pre- ceratopsid member of the horned-dinosaur lineage.
Protoceratops.description: Protoceratops is a genus of small protoceratopsid dinosaurs that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous, around 75 to 71 million years ago. The genus Protoceratops includes two species: P. andrewsi and the larger P. hellenikorhinus. The former was described in 1923 with fossils from the Mongolian Djadokhta Formation, and the latter in 2001 with fossils from the Chinese Bayan Mandahu Formation. Protoceratops was initially believed to be an ancestor of ankylosaurians and larger ceratopsians, such as Triceratops and relatives, until the discoveries of other protoceratopsids. Populations of P. andrewsi may have evolved into Bagaceratops rozhdestvenskyi through anagenesis.
diagnostic_features: Skull broadly triangular in dorsal view, with wide lateral crests formed mainly by posteriorly and ventrally expanded jugals.
Orbits very large and not surmounted by supraorbital horns.
Hornless skull (or with at most an incipient nasal horn-core in adult males formed by upwardly arched nasals).
Two premaxillary teeth present.
Parietosquamosal frill fenestrated and supporting a strong median parietal crest; frill length increases continuously through ontogeny and can exceed basal skull length in mature adults.
Ectopterygoid large and extensively exposed on the palate, in contact with the jugal — a primitive condition lost in later ceratopsians.
Sacrum elongate and narrow, with the sacral vertebra count rising from seven in young individuals to eight in fully adult animals.
Forelimb scarcely more than half the length of the hindlimb, with the femur shorter than the tibia and a relatively large pes bearing a compact metatarsus.

Protohadros.etymology: From Greek 'protos' meaning 'first' and 'hadros' meaning 'thick' (as in Hadrosauridae), meaning 'first hadrosaur.' The specific name byrdi honors discoverer Gary Byrd.
Protohadros.description: Protohadros is a genus of basal hadrosaurid dinosaur from the early Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian stage, approximately 100-93.9 million years ago) of what is now Texas, United States. It is represented by the species Protohadros byrdi, known from a partially complete skull and associated postcranial remains recovered from the Woodbine Formation. Protohadros was one of the earliest derived hadrosaurs in North America.

Psittacosaurus.etymology: From Greek psittakos (parrot) and sauros (lizard); meaning "parrot lizard", a name suggested by W.K. Gregory and adopted by Osborn in reference to the deep, edentulous, parrot-like rostrum formed by the premaxillae and the unpaired rostral bone.
Psittacosaurus.description: Psittacosaurus is a genus of extinct ceratopsian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of what is now Asia, existing between 125 and 105 million years ago. It is notable for being the most species-rich non-avian dinosaur genus. Up to 13 species are known, from across China, Mongolia, Russia, and Thailand. The species of Psittacosaurus were obligate bipeds at adulthood, with a high skull and a robust beak. One individual was found preserved with long filaments on the tail, similar to those of Tianyulong. Psittacosaurus probably had complex behaviors, based on the proportions and relative size of the brain. It may have been active for short periods of time during the day and night, and had well-developed senses of smell and vision.
diagnostic_features: Skull short and deep, with a prominent parrot-like edentulous rostrum; preorbital skull length less than 40% of total skull length, shorter than in nearly all other ornithischians.
Unpaired median rostral bone forming the anterior keel of the snout, with rostral-nasal contact and the nasal contributing to the internarial bar ventral to the external naris.
Jugals projecting laterally well beyond the dorsal margin of the orbit, bearing a prominent dorsoventral crest on their lateral aspect.
Fenestra of the lacrimal canal present between premaxilla and lacrimal — a condition unique to Psittacosaurus among dinosaurs.
Pterygoid with a neomorphic secondary palatal lamina forming an akinetic basal plate that contacts its opposite at the midline, reinforcing the palate against transverse compression.
Laterally divergent palpebral with transverse posterior margin, projecting laterally to a width equal to the posterior skull table.
Predentary ventral process broad, expanding in width toward its proximal end.
Dentary teeth with a bulbous, cone-shaped primary ridge occupying approximately one third of the crown face, with secondary ridging.

Pteropelyx.etymology: From Greek pteron (wing) and pelyx (pelvis); meaning "winged pelvis".
Pteropelyx.description: Pteropelyx is a dubious genus of Late Cretaceous hadrosaurid dinosaur from the Judith River Formation of Montana, named by Edward Drinker Cope in 1889. Historically, several species were assigned to it, all based on extremely fragmentary remains, but there is no evidence to support these assignments, making the type species, P. grallipes, the only valid species. Most of these other species' remains likely belong to better-known hadrosaurs, such as Lambeosaurus and Gryposaurus. It is probable that the type material of Pteropelyx, a skeleton lacking a skull, is from Corythosaurus (making Pteropelyx its senior synonym) (Brett-Surman, 1989), but the lack of a skull makes such a synonymy impossible to determine with sure certainty as no certain evidence pertain to prove the organ to be present.

Pterospondylus.etymology: From Greek 'pteron' meaning 'wing' and 'spondylos' meaning 'vertebra', meaning 'winged vertebra.' The species name trielbae references the Triassic period and the Elbe River area.
Pterospondylus.description: Pterospondylus is a dubious genus of theropod dinosaur from the Late Triassic. It was a coelophysid theropod which lived in what is now Germany (Trossingen Formation). The type species, Pterospondylus trielbae, (derived from "Tri", in reference to the Triassic period, and "Elba", for the Elbe River area), was described by Jaekel in 1913-14 for a single back vertebra found inside the shell of the Proganochelys turtle. Sometimes, it is aligned with Procompsognathus, or even considered to be synonymous with it, despite being based on a vertebra that is twice the size of the corresponding bone in Procompsognathus. P. trielbae has no diagnostic features and is therefore considered a nomen dubium.
diagnostic_features: Transverse processes spread out like wings

Ptychotherates.etymology: From Greek 'ptycho' meaning 'fold', referring to the many challenging reorientation axes on the holotype skull elements, and Greek 'therates' meaning 'hunter', for the inferred carnivorous habits.
Ptychotherates.description: Ptychotherates is an extinct genus of saurischian dinosaur known from the Late Triassic (latest Norian or Rhaetian) Chinle Formation at the Coelophysis Quarry, Ghost Ranch, New Mexico. The genus contains a single species, Ptychotherates bucculentus, known from a partial skull whose jugal is the proportionally deepest of any known Triassic-aged dinosaur. The describing paper recovers Ptychotherates as a close relative of Tawa, Chindesaurus, and Daemonosaurus.

Puertasaurus.etymology: Named for Pablo Puerta, one of the field workers who discovered the fossil specimen, combined with Greek '-saurus' meaning 'lizard'.
Puertasaurus.description: Puertasaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in South America during the Late Cretaceous Period. It is known from a single specimen recovered from sedimentary rocks of the Cerro Fortaleza Formation in southwestern Patagonia, Argentina, which probably is Campanian or Maastrichtian in age. The only species is Puertasaurus reuili. Described by the paleontologist Fernando Novas and colleagues in 2005, it was named in honor of Pablo Puerta and Santiago Reuil, who discovered and prepared the specimen. It consists of four well-preserved vertebrae, including one cervical, one dorsal, and two caudal vertebrae. Puertasaurus is a member of Titanosauria, the dominant group of sauropods during the Cretaceous.

Pukyongosaurus.etymology: Named after Pukyong National University in South Korea, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "Pukyong lizard".
Pukyongosaurus.description: Pukyongosaurus is a genus of titanosauriform dinosaur that lived in South Korea during the Early Cretaceous Period (Aptian - Albian). It may have been closely related to Euhelopus, and is known from a series of vertebrae in the neck and back. The characteristics that were originally used to distinguish this genus have been criticized as being either widespread or too poorly preserved to evaluate, rendering the genus an indeterminate nomen dubium among titanosauriforms. A 2022 study noted that Pukyongosaurus is probably a somphospondylan.

Ventral side of cervical centrum slightly bent, either flat, with a narrow ventral ridge located on the posterior part.

Haemal canal of chevron open and not bridged over dorsally.

Pulanesaura.description: Pulanesaura is an extinct genus of basal sauropodiform known from the Early Jurassic (late Hettangian to Sinemurian) Upper Elliot Formation of the Free State, South Africa. It contains a single species, Pulanesaura eocollum, known from partial remains of at least two subadult to adult individuals.

Pulaosaurus.etymology: From Mandarin Chinese 'Pulao' (a dragon of Chinese mythology reputed for its loud cry, alluding to the genus's preserved ossified larynx) and Greek 'sauros' (lizard).
Pulaosaurus.description: Pulaosaurus is an extinct genus of early-diverging neornithischian ornithischian dinosaur from the Callovian-Oxfordian Tiaojishan Formation of Qinglong County, Hebei Province, northern China. Yang, King and Xu (2025) erected the genus on an immature articulated skeleton (IVPP V30936; total preserved length ~722 mm) that preserves paired ossified arytenoids and ceratobranchials of the larynx — making Pulaosaurus only the second non-avian dinosaur (after the ankylosaur Pinacosaurus grangeri) known to retain ossified laryngeal elements. Comparison with extant avian larynges led the authors to interpret the structure as a vocal modifier rather than the vocal source, suggesting bird-like acoustic capabilities. Cololites preserved in the abdominal cavity (3-8 mm oval impressions and flat pebbles) provide direct evidence of plant-seed ingestion. Pulaosaurus is the first neornithischian and the first ornithischian confidently recovered from the Yanliao Biota, and the phylogenetic analyses recover it as one of the earliest-diverging Neornithischia, close to Agilisaurus.
diagnostic_features: Robust fibular condyle forming a dorsoventrally extending crest on the tibia.
Three unfused distal tarsals present, with distal tarsal 3 being small and drop-shaped.
Distal tarsal 3 pierced by a foramen on its posterior surface.
Small bony boss on the caudoventral corner of the dorsal ramus of the jugal.
Obturator opening in the pubis is notch-shaped rather than a true enclosed foramen.
Paired arytenoid (laryngeal) elements are gracile and leaf-like in form with a L-shaped cross-section.

Pyroraptor.etymology: From Greek pyr (fire) and Latin raptor (thief); meaning "fire thief", named because the first fossils were found after a forest fire.
Pyroraptor.description: Pyroraptor is an extinct genus of paravian dinosaur, probably a dromaeosaurid or unenlagiid, from the Late Cretaceous Ibero-Armorican island, of what is now southern France. It lived during the late Campanian and early Maastrichtian stages, approximately 72 million years ago. It is known from a single partial specimen that was found in Provence in 1992, after a forest fire. The animal was named Pyroraptor olympius by Allain and Taquet in 2000.

It is known from the Suining Formation of China, which is of a debated age (reported as Late Jurassic or Early Cretaceous using different methods). The genus contains a single species, Qijianglong guokr, known from a partial skeleton including cranial bones, most of the neck and tail, and other associated elements.

Qingxiusaurus.etymology: Named for Qingxiu, a shortened form of the Chinese phrase meaning 'a picturesque scenery of mountains and water in Guangxi', combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Qingxiu lizard.'

The type species, described by Mo et al. in 2008, is Q. youjiangensis. Like other sauropods, Qingxiusaurus would have been a large quadrupedal herbivore. It is known from only limited remains collected in 1991: Two humeri, two sternal plates, and the neural spine of a single vertebra.

Qiupalong.etymology: From Chinese 'Qiupa' (the Qiupa Formation where it was found) + 'long' (dragon), meaning 'dragon from the Qiupa Formation'.
Qiupalong.description: Qiupalong is an extinct genus of ornithomimosaurian theropod that was discovered in the Late Cretaceous Qiupa Formation of Henan, China. The genus contains a single species, Q. henanensis, the specific epithet for which was named for the province of Henan. Uniquely, Qiupalong is one of the few Late Cretaceous non-avian dinosaurs known from both Asia and Laramidia. A specimen from Alberta has been referred to the genus without being assigned to the type species or suggested to be similar to it. A fossil of an ornithomimid similar to Qiupalong has also been described from Russian Far East.

Quaesitosaurus.etymology: From Latin 'quaesitus' (extraordinary, sought-after, unusual) + Greek 'sauros' (lizard), meaning 'extraordinary lizard'.
Quaesitosaurus.description: Quaesitosaurus is a genus of nemegtosaurid sauropod containing only the type species, Q. orientalis, described in 1983. It lived from 72 to 71 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous epoch in the Barun Goyot Formation. With long, low and horse-like with frontally located peg-teeth, the skull of Quaesitosaurus is similar enough to the skull of Diplodocus and its kin to have prompted informed speculation that the missing body was built like those of diplodocids.

Quilmesaurus.etymology: Named for the Quilmes, an indigenous people of northwestern Argentina, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Quilmesaurus.description: Quilmesaurus is a genus of carnivorous theropod dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian to Maastrichtian stages) Allen Formation of Argentina. It was a member of Abelisauridae, closely related to genera such as Carnotaurus. The only known remains of this genus are leg bones which share certain similarities to a variety of abelisaurids. However, these bones lack unique features, which may render Quilmesaurus a nomen vanum (more commonly known as a nomen dubium, or "dubious name").

Rahiolisaurus.etymology: Named after Rahioli, the village in Gujarat, India, near where the fossils were recovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard).
Rahiolisaurus.description: Rahiolisaurus is a genus of abelisaurid theropod dinosaur which existed in India during the Late Cretaceous period. It was described in 2010, based on fossils recovered from the Lameta Formation in the Indian state of Gujarat. These fossils include elements from at least seven different individuals and are believed to have been from the Maastrichtian stage, sometime between 70 and 66 million years ago, making it one of the last non-avian dinosaurs known in the fossil record. Despite representing a variety of different growth stages, all recovered fossils from the locality indicate a single species, the type species Rahiolisaurus gujaratensis.

Rahonavis.etymology: From Malagasy 'rahona' meaning 'cloud' or 'menace' and Latin 'avis' meaning 'bird', named for its bird-like nature and discovery in Madagascar.
Rahonavis.description: Rahonavis is a genus of bird-like theropod from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian, from about 70 to 66 mya) of what is now northwestern Madagascar. It is known from a partial skeleton (UA 8656) found by Catherine Forster and colleagues in Maevarano Formation rocks at a quarry near Berivotra, Mahajanga Province. Rahonavis was a small predator, at about 70 centimeters (2.3 ft) long and 0.45-2.27 kg (1-5 lbs), with the typical dromaesaurid-like raised sickle claw on the second toe. It was the first coelurosaur discovered in Africa, with Nqwebasaurus being the second.

Rajasaurus.description: Rajasaurus is a genus of carnivorous abelisaurid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of India, containing one species: Rajasaurus narmadensis. The bones were excavated from the Lameta Formation in the Gujarat state of Western India, probably inhabiting what is now the Narmada River Valley. It was formally described by paleontologist Jeffrey A. Wilson and colleagues in 2003 based on a partial skeleton comprising the braincase, spine, hip bone, legs, and tail-a first for an Indian theropod. The dinosaur likely measured 6.6 meters (22 ft), and had a single horn on the forehead which was probably used for display and head-butting. Like other abelisaurids, Rajasaurus was probably an ambush predator.

Rapetosaurus.description: Rapetosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived in Madagascar from 70 to 66 million years ago, at the end of the Cretaceous Period. Raptorex.description: Raptorex is a controversial genus of tyrannosaurid dinosaur. Its fossil remains consist of a single juvenile specimen probably uncovered in Mongolia, or possibly northeastern China. The type species is R. kriegsteini, described in 2009 by Sereno and colleagues. The genus name is derived from Latin raptor, "robber", and rex, "king". The specific name honors Roman Kriegstein, a survivor of the Holocaust, whose son Henry Kriegstein donated the specimen to the University of Chicago for scientific study.

Ratchasimasaurus.etymology: Named after Nakhon Ratchasima province in Thailand where the fossil was found, combined with Greek sauros (lizard); meaning "Nakhon Ratchasima lizard".
Ratchasimasaurus.description: Ratchasimasaurus is a genus of iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur from Early Cretaceous (Aptian stage) Khok Kruat Formation of Nakhon Ratchasima province in northeastern Thailand. The type and only species is R. suranareae, named after Thao Suranari, a 19th-century war heroine. Rebbachisaurus.description: Rebbachisaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in what is now Africa during the Late Cretaceous period, between 99 and 97 million years ago. The only valid species is R. garasbae. However, two other species have been assigned to the genus; R. tessonei, now Limaysaurus tessonei, and the nomen dubium R. tamesnensis. Regaliceratops.etymology: From Latin regalis (royal) and Greek keras (horn) and ops (face); meaning "Royal horned face".
Regaliceratops.description: Regaliceratops is a monospecific genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur from Alberta, Canada that lived during the Late Cretaceous (middle Maastrichtian stage, 68.5 to 67.5 Ma) in what is now the St. Mary River Formation. The type and only species, Regaliceratops peterhewsi, is known only from an adult individual with a nearly complete skull lacking the lower jaw, which was nicknamed "Hellboy". Regaliceratops was named in 2015 by Caleb M. Brown and Donald M. Henderson. Regaliceratops has an estimated length of 5 meters (16 ft) and body mass of 2 metric tons (2.2 short tons). The skull of Regaliceratops displays features more similar to centrosaurines, which suggests convergent evolution in display morphology in ceratopsids.

Rhabdodon.etymology: From Greek rhabdos (fluted, rod-like) and odon (tooth); meaning "fluted tooth".
Rhabdodon.description: Rhabdodon is a genus of ornithopod dinosaur that lived in Europe approximately 72-69 million years ago in the Late Cretaceous. The genus contains a single species, R. priscus. It is similar in build to a very robust "hypsilophodont" (non-iguanodont ornithopod), though all modern phylogenetic analyses find this to be an unnatural grouping, and Rhabdodon to be a basal member of Iguanodontia. It was large among its relatives, measuring 4 m (13 ft) long and weighing 250 kg (550 lb), with some specimens possibly reaching up to 6 m (20 ft) long.

Richardoestesia.etymology: Named in honor of paleontologist Richard Estes, with the Latinised possessive form 'Richardoestesia' combining his first name Richard with his surname Estes.
Richardoestesia.description: Richardoestesia is a morphogenus of theropod dinosaur teeth, originally described from the Late Cretaceous of what is now Canada, the United States, and possibly also Uzbekistan. It currently contains two species, R. gilmorei and R. isosceles, and a possible third, R. asiatica, although it has been classified in its own genus Asiamericana. It has been used as a morphotaxon to describe other theropod teeth widely displaced in time and space from the type species. If all teeth assigned to the genus are truly reflective of the animals biology and taxonomic state (as some teeth go as far back as the Late Jurassic), it would have been one of the longest lasting dinosaur genera, perhaps also being the most widely distributed.

Rocasaurus.etymology: Named for General Roca, a city in Río Negro Province, Argentina, near where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'General Roca lizard.'
Rocasaurus.description: Rocasaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod that lived in South America. Rocasaurus was discovered in Argentina in 2000, within the Allen Formation which is dated to be middle Campanian to early Maastrichtian in age (75 to 70 million years ago in the Late Cretaceous). This genus grew up to 8 meters (26 ft) long, making it one of the smaller sauropods. It seems to be closely related to saltasaurid dinosaurs, like Saltasaurus and Neuquensaurus. The type species, Rocasaurus muniozi, was formally described by Leonardo Salgado and Azpilicueta in 2000.

Neural spine wide and anteroposteriorly compressed in dorsal vertebrae

Ruehleia.etymology: Named for German paleontologist Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern, who collected paleontological material from the region.
Ruehleia.description: Ruehleia is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Late Triassic period of Germany. The type species is R. bedheimensis, described by Galton in 2001, and is named for the German paleontologist Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern. Discovered in 1952, the holotype consists of one nearly complete skeleton, including cervical (neck), dorsal (back), and caudal (tail) vertebrae; a partial sacrum; a scapulocoracoid; pelvic bones; most limb bones; and a partially complete manus (hands). The fossils were found in the Trossingen Formation of central Germany and date to the Norian stage, around 216 to 208 million years ago.

Rugops.etymology: From Latin 'ruga' (wrinkle) + Greek 'ops' (face, eye), meaning 'wrinkle face', referring to the pitted and rough surface of the skull.
Rugops.description: Rugops is a monospecific genus of basal abelisaurid theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period (Cenomanian stage, approximately 95 million years ago) in what is now the Echkar Formation in Niger. The type and only species, Rugops primus, is known only from a partial skull. It was named and described in 2004 by Paul Sereno, Jeffery Wilson and Jack Conrad. Rugops has an estimated length of 4.4-5.3 meters (14-17 ft) and weight of 410 kilograms (900 lb). The top of its skull bears several pits which correlates with overlaying scale and the front of the snout would have had an armor-like dermis.

The genus contains a single species, Ruixinia zhangi, known from a partial articulated skeleton. This specimen preserves the most complete series of caudal vertebrae known from any Asian titanosauriform.

Rukwatitan.etymology: Named for the Rukwa Rift Basin in Tanzania where it was found, combined with Greek 'titan' meaning 'giant'.
Rukwatitan.description: Rukwatitan is a genus of titanosaur sauropod dinosaur from the Galula Formation in Tanzania. It lived around 100 million years ago, during the middle Cretaceous. The species, which shared features with another southern African species, Malawisaurus dixeyi, measured 30 feet (9.1 m) from the head to the tip of the tail, and had forelimbs that were estimated around 6.5 feet (2.0 m) long. Its fossils were found embedded in a cliff face near Lake Rukwa in the Rukwa Valley, from which it gets its name.

Saltasaurus.etymology: Named after Salta Province in northwestern Argentina, where the fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard), meaning 'lizard from Salta'.
Saltasaurus.description: Saltasaurus is a genus of saltasaurid dinosaur of the Late Cretaceous period of Argentina. Small among sauropods, though still heavy by the standards of modern creatures, Saltasaurus was characterized by a short neck and stubby limbs. It was the first genus of sauropod known to possess armor of bony plates embedded in its skin. Such small bony plates, called osteoderms, have since been found on other titanosaurians.

Saltriovenator.etymology: Named for Saltrio, the town in northern Italy where the fossils were found in a marble quarry, combined with Latin 'venator' meaning 'hunter'; meaning 'Saltrio hunter.'
Saltriovenator.description: Saltriovenator is a genus of ceratosaurian dinosaur that lived during the Sinemurian stage of the Early Jurassic in what is now Italy. The type and only species is Saltriovenator zanellai; in the past, the species had been known under the informal name "saltriosaur". Although a full skeleton has not yet been discovered, Saltriovenator is thought to have been a large, bipedal carnivore similar to Ceratosaurus.

Sanxiasaurus.etymology: Named for Sanxia (Three Gorges) of the Yangtze River in China, near the type locality, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'Sanxia lizard.'
Sanxiasaurus.description: Sanxiasaurus is a genus of neornithischian dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Xintiangou Formation in the Chongqing Municipality of China. The type and only species is S. modaoxiensis. The holotype is a partial postcranial skeleton consisting of 55 bones including two cervical vertebrae, 11 dorsal vertebrae, 4 sacral vertebrae, 18 caudal vertebrae, both humeri, radii, and ulnas, partial right ilium, partial right ischium, both femora and tibiae, left fibula, 3 metatarsi and 4 phalanges. In a phylogenetic analysis, it was found to be a basal neornithischian, more derived than Lesothosaurus and less derived than Hexinlusaurus.

Sarcosaurus.description: Sarcosaurus is a genus of basal neotheropod dinosaur, roughly 3.5 meters (11 ft) long. It lived in what is now England and maybe Ireland and Scotland during the Hettangian-Sinemurian stages of the Early Jurassic, about 199-196 million years ago. Sarcosaurus is one of the earliest known Jurassic theropods, and one of only a handful of theropod genera from this time period. Along with Dracoraptor hanigani it is one of the two described neotheropods from the lowermost Jurassic of the United Kingdom.

Great trochanter small and peg-like, intermediate between Triassic and later Jurassic forms
Preacetabular notch narrower than in Megalosaurus, more similar to Ceratosaurus
Relatively large size of pubes and ischia, primitive character
Fourth trochanter forming prominent ridge on posterior face of femur shaft

Sarmientosaurus.etymology: Named after the town of Sarmiento in Chubut Province, Argentina, near where the fossils were discovered, combined with Greek 'sauros' (lizard).
Sarmientosaurus.description: Sarmientosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur belonging to the Titanosauria. It lived in what is now South America, specifically Argentina, during the Upper Cretaceous Period about 95 million years ago. The type species is Sarmientosaurus musacchioi.

Saturnalia.description: Saturnalia is an extinct genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur known from the Late Triassic Santa Maria Formation of Rio Grande do Sul, southern Brazil. It contains one species, Saturnalia tupiniquim. It is one of the earliest known dinosaurs.

Saurolophus.etymology: From Greek sauros (lizard) and lophos (crest); meaning "lizard crest".
Saurolophus.description: Saurolophus is a genus of large hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period of North America and Asia, in what is now the Horseshoe Canyon and Nemegt formations respectively (about 70 to 66 million years ago). It is one of the few dinosaur genera known from multiple continents. The type species, S. osborni, was described by Barnum Brown in 1912 from Canadian fossils. A second valid species, S. angustirostris, is represented by numerous specimens from Mongolia, and was described by Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky. Saurolophus is distinguished by a spike-like crest which projects up and back from the skull. It was a herbivorous dinosaur which could move either bipedally or quadrupedally.

Frontals rising upward at an obtuse angle to the parietals
Postfrontal divided posteriorly by a wedge-like process of the squamosal
Lacrimal triangular and elongate
Dentary teeth with a vertically elongate enamel face bearing a low median carina, the sides nearly flat and the borders smoothly arched

species.etymology: Named in honor of Henry Fairfield Osborn, American paleontologist and president of the American Museum of Natural History, who was a mentor to Barnum Brown.

Sauroniops.etymology: From Sauron, the fictional character created by J.R.R. Tolkien, and Greek 'ops' (eye); meaning 'eye of Sauron'.
Sauroniops.description: Sauroniops is a controversial genus of carnivorous carcharodontosaurid theropod dinosaurs known from the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian stage) of Morocco. It is known from the Gara Sbaa Formation of the Kem Kem beds and contains a single species, S. pachytholus.
Sauroniops.dispute: The validity of Sauroniops is actively contested. Ibrahim et al. (2020) argued that S. pachytholus is a junior synonym of Carcharodontosaurus saharicus, interpreting the holotype as an immature C. saharicus frontal and finding the diagnostic characters unconvincing. Paterna and Cau (2022) rebutted this, reaffirming the diagnosis and reporting additional Kem Kem carcharodontosaurid material distinct from C. saharicus. Kellermann, Cuesta and Rauhut (2025) declined the synonymy but treated Sauroniops as a nomen dubium, holding that erecting a taxon on a single frontal is inappropriate pending more material.
diagnostic_features: Dorsoventrally thickened frontal with body depth ranging 28% (medial suture) to 38% (anteromedial margin of supratemporal fossa) of bone length.
Thick dome-like eminence in the anterolateral corner of the dorsal surface of the frontal at the level of the prefrontal-lacrimal articulations.
Prefrontal facet of the frontal trapezoidal, mostly restricted to the anterodorsal margin of the lateral surface, not participating in the orbital fossa.
Frontal with interdigitate suture for prefrontal restricted to the anteroventral corner of the facet, formed by a low shelf and a small finger-like projection.
Hypertrophied 'D-shaped' lacrimal facet with maximum depth four times the depth of the anterior half of the postorbital facet.

Dorsal surface of frontal anterior to supratemporal fossa raised and facing anterodorsally, forming a saddle-shaped concavity with the anterolateral dome, confluent with anteromedial rugosities posterior to the nasal facet.

Sauropelta.etymology: From Greek 'sauros' (lizard) + 'pelte' (small shield), meaning 'lizard shield', referring to the bony armor covering the body.
Sauropelta.description: Sauropelta is a genus of nodosaurid dinosaur that existed in the Early Cretaceous Period of North America. One species (S. edwardsorum) has been named. Anatomically, Sauropelta is one of the most well-understood nodosaurids, with fossilized remains recovered in the U.S. states of Wyoming, Montana, and possibly Utah. It is also the earliest known genus of nodosaurine; most of its remains are found in a section of the Cloverly Formation dated to 108.5 million years ago.
diagnostic_features: Long mandibular tooth row with 25-27 alveoli extending close to symphysis, distinct from nodosaurs with fewer alveoli
Unfused atlas-axis with odontoid only fused to axis centrum, a primitive acanthopholid condition not seen in nodosaurs
Dermal armor consisting of hollow-based plates with concave to deeply hollowed inferior surfaces, more delicate than nodosaurs
Unfused ribs to dorsal vertebrae and unfused chevrons to caudal centra, distinct from nodosaur condition
Long slender femur relative to humerus with well-rounded internal condyles projecting far backward
Long narrow anterior iliac blade extending forward with long preacetabular process, characteristic of acanthopholids

Saurophaganax.etymology: From Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', 'phagein' meaning 'to eat', and 'anax' meaning 'ruler' or 'lord'; meaning 'lord of lizard-eaters.'
Saurophaganax.description: Saurophaganax is a dubious, chimeric genus of large saurischian dinosaur, possibly a sauropod, from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian) Morrison Formation of Oklahoma, United States. This taxon was historically considered to represent a species of Allosaurus or very large allosaurid. However, re-examinations of the attributed specimens suggested that it is a chimera of multiple dinosaur genera, since some specimens most likely belong to a diplodocid sauropod, while the other referred specimens could be reassigned to a novel species of Allosaurus.

Sauroplites.etymology: From Greek sauros (lizard) and hoplites (armed foot soldier, hoplite); meaning "saurian hoplite".
Sauroplites.description: Sauroplites is a genus of herbivorous ankylosaurian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of China.

Large plate M with a deep V-shaped cross-section (upper and lower lamellae separated by a deep pocket) and a serrated keel bearing at least six small marginal spines posteriorly

Ribs bearing a pronounced rugose dorsal surface from ~6 cm above the tuberculum, functioning as integument-attachment surface, with strongly broadened cross-section in that zone
Fused pelvic armor of co-ossified polygonal plates (~10 cm diameter) interspersed with rows of much smaller, variably sized plates; no external elevations on individual pelvic plates

Saurornithoides.etymology: From Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard', 'ornis' (stem 'ornith') meaning 'bird', and 'eidos' meaning 'form' or 'resemblance', referring to its bird-like skull.
Saurornithoides.description: Saurornithoides is a genus of troodontid maniraptoran dinosaur, which lived during the Late Cretaceous period. These creatures were predators, which could run fast on their hind legs and had excellent sight and hearing. The name is derived from the Greek stems saur~ (lizard), ornith~ (bird) and eides (form), referring to its bird-like skull.

Saurornitholestes.etymology: From Greek sauros (lizard), ornithos (bird), and lestes (thief); meaning "lizard-bird thief".
Saurornitholestes.description: Saurornitholestes is a genus of carnivorous dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur from the late Cretaceous of Canada (Alberta and Saskatchewan) and the United States (Montana, New Mexico, Alabama, and South Carolina). Two species have been named that are regarded as valid: Saurornitholestes langstoni in 1978 and Saurornitholestes sullivani in 2015. Saurornitholestes was a small, bipedal, meat-eating dinosaur, equipped with a sickle-like claw on each foot.

Savannasaurus.etymology: From English 'savanna', referring to the open grassland/savanna landscape of Queensland, Australia where its fossils were found, combined with Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'.
Savannasaurus.description: Savannasaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Winton Formation of Queensland, Australia. It contains one species, Savannasaurus elliottorum, named in 2016 by Stephen Poropat and colleagues. The holotype and only known specimen, originally nicknamed "Wade", is the most complete specimen of an Australian sauropod, and is held at the Australian Age of Dinosaurs museum. Dinosaurs known from contemporary rocks include its close relative Diamantinasaurus and the theropod Australovenator; associated teeth suggest that Australovenator may have fed on the holotype specimen.

Pubis with ridge extending anteroventrally from ventral margin of obturator foramen on lateral surface
Astragalus proximodistally taller than mediolaterally wide or anteroposteriorly long

Scansoriopteryx.etymology: From Latin 'scansorius' meaning 'climbing' and Greek 'pteryx' meaning 'wing'; meaning 'climbing wing', in reference to its arboreal adaptations.
Scansoriopteryx.description: Scansoriopteryx is a genus of maniraptoran dinosaur. Described from only a single juvenile fossil specimen found in Liaoning, China, Scansoriopteryx is a sparrow-sized animal that shows adaptations in the foot indicating an arboreal (tree-dwelling) lifestyle. It possessed an unusual, elongated third finger which may have supported a membranous wing, much like the related Yi qi. The type specimen of Scansoriopteryx also contains the fossilized impression of feathers.

Scolosaurus.etymology: From Greek 'skolos' (stake, thorn, prickle) + 'sauros' (lizard), meaning 'thorn lizard' or 'spiked lizard', referring to the spiky armor projections.
Scolosaurus.description: Scolosaurus is an extinct genus of ankylosaurid dinosaurs within the subfamily Ankylosaurinae. It is known from the lower levels of the Dinosaur Park Formation and upper levels of the Oldman Formation in the Late Cretaceous (latest middle Campanian stage, about 76.5 Ma ago) of Alberta, Canada. The genus contains two species, S. cutleri and S. thronus. The type species, S. cutleri, measured up to 5.6 meters (18 ft) in length and 2.2 metric tons (2.4 short tons) in body mass.

Scutellosaurus.etymology: From Latin 'scutellum' (diminutive of 'scutum', shield; small shield) + Greek 'sauros' (lizard), meaning 'little shield lizard', referring to the small scutes covering its body.
Scutellosaurus.description: Scutellosaurus is a genus of basal thyreophoran dinosaur that lived approximately 196 million years ago during the early part of the Jurassic Period in what is now Arizona, USA. It is classified in Thyreophora, the armored dinosaurs; its closest relatives may have been Emausaurus and Scelidosaurus, another armored dinosaur which was mainly a quadrupedal dinosaur, unlike bipedal Scutellosaurus. It is one of the earliest representatives of the armored dinosaurs and the basalmost form discovered to date. Scutellosaurus was a small, lightly-built, ground-dwelling herbivore, that could grow up to an estimated 1.3 meters (4.3 ft) long.

Secernosaurus.etymology: From Latin 'secerno' meaning 'to separate' or 'sever' and Greek 'sauros' meaning 'lizard'; meaning 'severed lizard', referring to its geographic separation from other hadrosaurs in South America.
Secernosaurus.description: Secernosaurus is a genus of herbivorous hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous of what is now Argentina. This genus and its close relatives lived in South America, unlike most hadrosaurids, which lived in the Laurasian continents of Eurasia and North America. It has been suggested that the ancestors of Secernosaurus crossed into South America when a land bridge temporarily formed between North and South America during the Late Cretaceous and allowed biotic interchange between the two continents.

Sefapanosaurus.etymology: From Sesotho 'sefapano' (cross) + Greek 'sauros' (lizard), meaning 'cross lizard', referring to the distinctive cross-shaped astragalus (ankle bone).
Sefapanosaurus.description: Sefapanosaurus was an early, herbivorous sauropodomorph dinosaur occurring in the southern regions of Gondwana some 200 million years ago in the Late Triassic or Early Jurassic. The sauropodomorphs were the dominant terrestrial herbivores throughout much of the Mesozoic Era, from their origins in the mid-Triassic (approximately 230 Ma) until their decline and fall at the end of the Cretaceous (approximately 66 Ma). A distinctive feature of this dinosaur is the cross-shaped astragalus or talus bone in its ankle. The generic name is derived from the Sesotho word sefapano, meaning 'cross' and the Greek word saurus, meaning 'lizard'. The specific name refers to Zastron, the type locality, where the specimen was discovered.
